# Quality Assurance Plan

## Testing Strategies and Methodologies
1. Conduct a combination of manual and automated testing to ensure comprehensive coverage.
2. Implement risk-based testing to prioritize critical functionalities and potential failure points.
3. Utilize exploratory testing to uncover unforeseen issues and validate user experience.
4. Perform regression testing to verify system stability after changes or updates.
5. Incorporate usability testing to assess user interaction and satisfaction.

## Quality Assurance Processes
1. Establish clear quality standards and guidelines for all testing activities.
2. Define roles and responsibilities for QA team members and key stakeholders.
3. Implement a robust defect management process to track, prioritize, and resolve issues.
4. Conduct regular code reviews and inspections to identify potential defects early in the development cycle.
5. Ensure continuous integration and deployment practices to maintain code quality and stability.

## Test Planning and Execution
1. Develop a detailed test plan outlining test objectives, scope, resources, and timelines.
2. Create test cases based on functional requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
3. Execute test cases systematically, recording results and identifying defects for resolution.
4. Perform test coverage analysis to ensure all critical functionalities are tested.
5. Conduct test reporting to communicate progress, issues, and risks to project stakeholders.

## Acceptance Criteria and Testing Procedures
1. Define clear acceptance criteria for each feature or deliverable in the project.
2. Align testing procedures with acceptance criteria to validate successful implementation.
3. Conduct user acceptance testing (UAT) with key stakeholders to ensure alignment with business requirements.
4. Document test results and obtain sign-off from stakeholders before moving to production.
5. Implement a formal change management process to address any deviations from acceptance criteria.

## Quality Metrics and KPIs
- Defect density
- Test coverage percentage
- Test execution efficiency
- Defect resolution time
- Customer satisfaction ratings

## Bug Tracking and Resolution Processes
1. Utilize a centralized bug tracking system to log, prioritize, and assign defects.
2. Implement a structured defect resolution process with clear escalation paths.
3. Monitor bug resolution progress and communicate updates to project stakeholders.
4. Conduct root cause analysis for recurring issues to prevent future occurrences.
5. Validate bug fixes through retesting before closing the defect.

## Performance and Load Testing
1. Conduct performance testing to assess system responsiveness, scalability, and stability under varying load conditions.
2. Define performance benchmarks and metrics to measure system performance against established criteria.
3. Implement load testing to simulate real-world usage scenarios and identify performance bottlenecks.
4. Optimize system performance based on test results and recommendations.
5. Continuously monitor system performance post-deployment to ensure ongoing stability.

## Security Testing and Compliance
1. Perform security testing to identify vulnerabilities, threats, and risks to the system.
2. Conduct penetration testing to simulate real-world cyber attacks and assess system resilience.
3. Ensure compliance with industry standards such as ISO 27001, GDPR, and PCI DSS.
4. Implement security controls and measures to protect sensitive data and prevent unauthorized access.
5. Regularly update security protocols and practices to address emerging threats and vulnerabilities.

## User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
1. Collaborate with key stakeholders to define UAT criteria and scenarios.
2. Conduct UAT sessions with end-users to validate system functionality and usability.
3. Capture user feedback and incorporate necessary changes based on UAT results.
4. Obtain final approval from stakeholders before transitioning to production.
5. Document UAT results and lessons learned for future reference and improvement.

- Scope creep or unclear requirements

- Dependencies and environment readiness delays

- Vendor price changes (cloud/SaaS)

- Travel and logistics cost increases
  - Mitigation: Remote-first delivery; T&E pre-approval; cap per policy.
- Compliance/tax changes
  - Mitigation: Contract change mechanism; pass-through taxes; legal review.

Residual risk is rated Low–Medium under the proposed controls. A 10% contingency is included for unknowns.

# Financial Proposal

## Executive Summary
- Objective: Deliver a turnkey cybersecurity capability aligned to the RFP—24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation, and 1-hour incident response (IR) SLA—mapped to ISO 27001.
- Pricing model: Fixed-fee implementation + predictable, usage-based monthly subscription for SIEM and SOC, plus an annual IR retainer.
- Commercial terms: Net 30 days after invoice approval; milestone-based payments; 10% retention on professional services until project completion (per contract).

## Financial Justification & ROI Analysis
- Key benefit drivers:
  - Risk reduction: Faster MTTD/MTTR, 24/7 coverage, curated detections reduce incident impact likelihood and duration.
  - Cost avoidance: Avoid building an in-house 24/7 SOC (7–10 FTEs), SIEM tooling/admin, and out-of-hours coverage premiums.
  - Compliance efficiency: ISO 27001-aligned reporting reduces audit preparation time and non-conformance risk.
  - Operational efficiency: Automated playbooks decrease manual triage time and false positives.
- Illustrative ROI (Standard, 50 GB/day):
  - Assumptions:
    - Expected annual cyber loss baseline: $1.2M (typical mid-market; varies by sector).
    - Loss reduction with solution: 40% via improved detection/response and 24/7 coverage → $480k/year avoided.
    - In-house SOC alternative (fully loaded): 7 FTE × $150k = $1.05M/year vs. managed recurring $183k/year → $867k/year potential saving if displacing build-out.
    - Compliance/audit efficiencies: $80k/year in saved staff/consulting time.
  - Annual quantified benefits (conservative if not replacing staff): $480k (risk) + $80k (compliance) = $560k/year; up to $1.427M/year if replacing an in-house build.
  - 3-year TCO (proposal): $724k. Even with conservative $560k/year benefits, 3-year benefits ~$1.68M; net benefit ~$956k; ROI ≈ 132% and payback < 8 months. If replacing in-house build, ROI is substantially higher.

| Additional IR hours beyond retainer | Overage fees | Medium | Bank size tailored to risk; proactive tabletop exercises; discounted overage rates |

## Discounts, Indexation & Price Protections
- Multi-year term discount: 3% (2-year) or 5% (3-year) on recurring fees.
- Prepayment discount: Additional 2% on pre-paid annual recurring.
- Volume discount: SIEM/SOC per-GB/day rates reduced by 5% at 100+ GB/day; 8% at 200+ GB/day.
- CPI cap: Annual uplift on recurring capped at 3% or CPI, whichever is lower, for terms ≥24 months.
- Service credits: If 1-hour IR SLA missed, monthly service credit of 5% of IR retainer for each material breach, capped at 25% of monthly recurring (excludes force majeure).

## Change Control & Price-Sensitive Assumptions
- Included log sources: Up to 20; beyond scope at $2,000/source (standard) or T&M for custom parsers ($180/hour).
- Retention: 30-day hot and 365-day cold included; hot retention extension priced on request.
- New use-case families (e.g., OT/ICS, mainframe) may require additional content engineering at T&M.
- Out-of-hours on-site support (non-IR): $275/hour + T&E (pre-approved).
- Any scope change requires a mutually agreed change order (CO) before work proceeds.

## Compliance & Audit Support (ISO 27001)
- Included deliverables:
  - Control mapping for SIEM/SOC to ISO 27001 Annex A controls.
  - Pre-built ISO-aligned dashboards and evidentiary logging.
  - Quarterly compliance reports and audit-readiness packets.
  - Participation in audits (up to 16 hours/quarter included; additional hours at $180/hour).
- Outcome: Financially predictable audit preparation and reduced non-conformance risk.

## Stakeholder Alignment
- CISO: Budget predictability, risk reduction metrics (MTTD/MTTR), ISO 27001 alignment.
- IT Operations Manager: Minimal operational friction, change windows, integration support.
- Compliance Officer: Evidence packs, quarterly reports, control mappings.
- Legal Department: Contractual protections, data processing terms.
- Procurement: Transparent rate cards, milestone schedules, Net 30, retention adherence.

- Acceptance criteria:

  - 24/7 SOC monitoring active; escalation paths validated; IR 1-hour SLA tested.
  - ISO 27001 control mappings and compliance reporting delivered.
  - Training completed; UAT sign-off by client.
- Invoicing:
  - Professional services: Upon milestone acceptance (Net 30); 10% retention withheld and released at final acceptance.
  - Subscriptions: Invoiced monthly in arrears (Net 30).
  - IR Retainer: Invoiced annually in advance (or quarterly if preferred).

## Key Dates & Validity
- Price validity: 120 days from proposal date.
- Target implementation: 10–14 weeks from kickoff (subject to timely access and approvals).

## Summary of Value
- Predictable, auditable costs aligned with contract terms (Net 30, milestone-based, 10% retention).
- Flexible tiered options to match log volumes and budget.
- Quantified ROI with accelerated payback via risk and operational cost reductions.
- Alignment to client’s cybersecurity requirements: 24/7 SOC, SIEM, 1-hour IR SLA, ISO 27001 compliance.

# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Parties, Purpose, and Stakeholder Governance
1.1 Parties. This Agreement is entered into by and between [Customer Legal Name] (“Customer”) and [Supplier Legal Name] (“Supplier”), collectively “Parties,” for the provision of cybersecurity services, including 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation, and incident response.
1.2 Purpose. Supplier will deliver managed security services aligned to ISO/IEC 27001, including the implementation and operation of a SIEM platform and 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) services with incident response within one (1) hour for Priority 1 incidents.
1.3 Key Stakeholders. Customer stakeholders include the CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal Department, and Procurement Team. Supplier shall designate a Delivery Manager, Security Architect, and Service Manager.
1.4 Governance. The Parties will establish a joint governance structure with (a) weekly operational meetings; (b) monthly service reviews; (c) quarterly executive reviews. Escalation path: Service Manager → Supplier Security Director → Supplier Executive Sponsor; mirrored by Customer IT Operations Manager → CISO → Executive Sponsor.

## 2. Definitions
2.1 Incident: A suspected or confirmed event that jeopardizes confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information or services.  
2.2 Priority 1 (P1): A critical incident with confirmed active compromise, material business impact, or regulatory breach risk.  
2.3 SIEM: Security Information and Event Management system used for log collection, correlation, alerting, and reporting.  
2.4 Business Day: Any day other than weekends and public holidays in the governing jurisdiction.  
2.5 Confidential Information: Non-public information disclosed by a Party that is designated as confidential or would reasonably be understood as confidential.  
2.6 Personal Data: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person as defined by Applicable Data Protection Laws.  
2.7 Applicable Laws: All laws, regulations, and standards applicable to the Services, including ISO/IEC 27001 and data protection laws.

## 3. Order of Precedence
3.1 The following order of precedence applies in case of conflict: (1) Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and information security annexes; (2) Statement(s) of Work (SOWs); (3) this Master Services Agreement (MSA); (4) RFP and Supplier Proposal; (5) Purchase Orders.  
3.2 Handwritten or typed notations initialed by both Parties supersede printed terms in the affected document.

## 4. Scope of Services
4.1 24/7 SOC Monitoring. Supplier will provide continuous monitoring, alert triage, and escalation.  
4.2 SIEM Implementation and Operation. Supplier will design, deploy, configure, and operate a SIEM with defined log sources, retention, correlation rules, and dashboards.  
4.3 Incident Response. Supplier will provide triage, investigation, containment guidance, and coordination with Customer for P1/P2 events per SLA.  
4.4 Use Cases and Content. Supplier will maintain and tune detection content aligned to evolving threats and Customer risk profile.  
4.5 Deliverables. Architecture diagrams, runbooks, onboarding plans, asset/log source inventory, playbooks, and monthly service reports.  
4.6 Out of Scope. Penetration testing, red teaming, and non-security IT operations unless explicitly included in an SOW.  
4.7 Change Control. Changes to scope require a written change order approved by both Parties.

## 5. Term and Renewal
5.1 Initial Term. The initial term is [36] months from Effective Date unless otherwise stated in the SOW.  
5.2 Renewal. Thereafter, the Agreement renews for successive 12-month terms unless either Party provides 90 days’ notice of non-renewal.  
5.3 Extension for Transition. Customer may extend Services up to 6 months for transition assistance at then-current rates.

## 6. Fees, Invoicing, and Payment
6.1 Fees. Fees are as specified in the SOW and are tied to defined performance milestones.  
6.2 Invoicing. Supplier will invoice monthly in arrears, itemizing Services, milestones achieved, and any approved expenses.  
6.3 Payment Terms. Net 30 days after Customer invoice approval. Performance milestones must be met for payment eligibility. A 10% retention will be withheld until project completion and Acceptance.  
6.4 Disputed Amounts. Customer may withhold payment of disputed amounts with written notice; undisputed amounts remain payable.  
6.5 Taxes. Fees exclude applicable taxes; Customer is responsible for taxes except those based on Supplier’s net income.  
6.6 Price Changes. Fixed for the Initial Term unless otherwise agreed; any proposed adjustments on renewal require 90 days’ notice.

## 7. Acceptance and Milestones
7.1 Acceptance Criteria. Deliverables are accepted when they meet documented criteria in the SOW.  
7.2 Review Period. Customer shall review Deliverables within 10 Business Days; failure to reject with specific deficiencies results in deemed acceptance.  
7.3 Retention Release. The 10% retention is released upon final acceptance and delivery of all required documentation.

## 8. Confidentiality
8.1 Obligations. The receiving Party shall protect Confidential Information with the same care as its own confidential data, not less than reasonable care.  
8.2 Permitted Disclosure. To employees, affiliates, and subcontractors with a need-to-know, under confidentiality obligations.  
8.3 Exclusions. Information that is public, independently developed, or rightfully received from a third party.  
8.4 Compelled Disclosure. Permitted with prompt notice (unless prohibited) and reasonable cooperation.  
8.5 Survival. Confidentiality obligations survive for 5 years from disclosure; trade secrets survive as long as protected by law.

## 9. Data Protection and Privacy
9.1 Roles. Customer is the Controller; Supplier is the Processor (and subprocessor to Customer’s processors, as applicable).  
9.2 Processing. Supplier shall process Personal Data solely on documented instructions from Customer and only for the purpose of performing the Services.  
9.3 Security Measures. Supplier will implement appropriate technical and organizational measures aligned to ISO/IEC 27001, including encryption in transit and at rest, least-privilege access, MFA for privileged accounts, vulnerability management, and secure development practices.  
9.4 Breach Notification. Supplier shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after confirming a Personal Data Breach, providing details sufficient for Customer’s regulatory notifications.  
9.5 DPIA and Cooperation. Supplier will provide information necessary for Customer’s DPIAs, records of processing, and regulator inquiries.  
9.6 Subprocessors. Supplier requires prior written approval for subprocessors, will maintain an up-to-date list, and shall flow down equivalent data protection obligations. Customer may object on reasonable grounds.  
9.7 International Transfers. Cross-border transfers shall comply with Applicable Laws, including use of Standard Contractual Clauses or other valid transfer mechanisms.  
9.8 Data Subject Rights. Supplier shall assist Customer in responding to access, rectification, deletion, portability, and restriction requests within statutory timeframes.  
9.9 Retention and Deletion. Upon termination or request, Supplier will return Customer Data and securely delete all copies within 30 days, subject to legally required retention.  
9.10 Audits. Supplier shall provide audit reports (e.g., ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 Type II if available) and allow audits as set forth in Section 14.

## 10. Information Security Requirements
10.1 Certification. Supplier shall maintain ISO/IEC 27001 certification for the duration of the Agreement.  
10.2 Access Control. Role-based access, MFA for administrative access, and documented joiner/mover/leaver procedures.  
10.3 Logging and Monitoring. End-to-end logging for in-scope systems with tamper-evident storage and defined retention (minimum 365 days online, 1,095 days archive unless otherwise required).  
10.4 Vulnerability and Patch Management. High/Critical vulnerabilities remediated within 7 days; Medium within 30 days; Low within 90 days or risk accepted by Customer.  
10.5 Malware Protection. Endpoint and server protection with real-time scanning and EDR coverage for in-scope assets.  
10.6 Secure Configuration. Baselines aligned with CIS or equivalent standards and regular configuration drift checks.  
10.7 Background Checks. Personnel with access to Customer environments undergo background screening per local law.  
10.8 Physical Security. Data center controls including access badges, CCTV, and visitor logs.  
10.9 Business Continuity. Maintain and test BCP/DR plans annually with RTO ≤ 4 hours and RPO ≤ 1 hour for critical service components.

## 11. Regulatory and Standards Compliance
11.1 ISO/IEC 27001. Mandatory adherence, including continuous improvement and internal audits.  
11.2 Privacy Laws. Compliance with Applicable Data Protection Laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, UK GDPR) as applicable to the Services.  
11.3 Sectoral Laws. If applicable, compliance with HIPAA/HITECH, GLBA, PCI DSS, or other industry-specific regulations; such obligations will be specified in the SOW.  
11.4 Trade Compliance. Compliance with export controls, sanctions, and anti-boycott laws.  
11.5 Anti-Corruption. Compliance with the U.S. FCPA, UK Bribery Act, and analogous anti-bribery laws; no facilitation payments.  
11.6 Modern Slavery and Human Rights. Compliance with applicable anti-slavery and human trafficking laws.  
11.7 Accessibility. Deliverables that include user interfaces shall conform to WCAG 2.1 AA unless otherwise agreed.  
11.8 Records Retention. Maintain service and compliance records for at least 6 years or as required by law.

## 12. Intellectual Property Rights
12.1 Pre-existing IP. Each Party retains ownership of its pre-existing IP; no transfer is implied.  
12.2 Developed Materials. Deliverables specifically created for Customer under the SOW (“Work Product”) are owned by Customer upon payment; Supplier retains rights to its underlying tools, know-how, and generic templates, granting Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use such underlying elements as embedded in the Work Product.  
12.3 Open Source. Supplier will comply with applicable open-source licenses and will not include copyleft code that imposes source disclosure obligations on Customer without prior written consent.  
12.4 License to Supplier. Customer grants Supplier a limited, non-exclusive license to use Customer Data solely to perform the Services.

## 13. Warranties
13.1 Services Warranty. Supplier warrants Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards.  
13.2 Compliance Warranty. Supplier warrants compliance with Applicable Laws and Section 11.  
13.3 Non-Infringement. Supplier warrants that Deliverables and Services will not knowingly infringe third-party IP rights.  
13.4 No Malicious Code. Supplier will not introduce malware or time bombs; all software will be scanned prior to deployment.  
13.5 Remedies. For breach of warranty, Supplier will reperform non-conforming Services or repair/replace Deliverables at no additional cost.  
13.6 Disclaimer. Except as expressly stated, no other warranties are made; statutory warranties that cannot be disclaimed remain unaffected.

## 14. Audit and Verification
14.1 Right to Audit. Upon 15 Business Days’ notice (or immediately for suspected breach), Customer may audit Supplier’s compliance with security and privacy obligations, not more than once per 12 months, during normal business hours.  
14.2 Third-Party Reports. Supplier will provide current ISO 27001 certificate and, if available, SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test executive summaries, and remediation plans.  
14.3 Regulator Access. Supplier will reasonably cooperate with regulators having jurisdiction over Customer’s data or services.

## 15. Subcontracting
15.1 Consent. Supplier may not subcontract material obligations without Customer’s prior written consent; approved subcontractors must be bound by written agreements with equivalent obligations.  
15.2 Responsibility. Supplier remains fully responsible for subcontractor performance.

## 16. Insurance
16.1 Coverage. Supplier shall maintain at its expense: (a) Commercial General Liability: $2,000,000 aggregate; (b) Professional/Technology E&O: $5,000,000 per claim; (c) Cyber Liability: $5,000,000 per claim, including privacy breach, media, and network security; (d) Workers’ Compensation and Employer’s Liability as required by law.  
16.2 Certificates. Certificates of insurance provided upon request; notice to Customer for material cancellation or reduction.

## 17. Service Level Agreements (SLAs)

### 17.1 SLA Metrics and Targets
| Metric | Target | Measurement Window | Service Credits |
|---|---|---|---|
| SOC Availability | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Calendar month | 2% of monthly SOC fee per 0.1% below target, cap 20% |
| SIEM Platform Availability | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Calendar month | 2% of monthly SIEM fee per 0.1% below, cap 20% |
| Log Ingestion Latency (P95) | ≤ 5 minutes | Monthly P95 | 2% of monthly SIEM fee per breach, cap 10% |
| P1 Triage Start Time | ≤ 15 minutes | Each incident | 2% of monthly SOC fee per breach, cap 20% |
| P1 Incident Response Engagement | ≤ 1 hour from alert | Each P1 incident | 5% of monthly SOC fee per breach, cap 30% |
| P1 Mean Time to Contain (MTTC) | ≤ 4 hours | Monthly average | 3% of monthly SOC fee per breach, cap 20% |
| P1 Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR) | ≤ 24 hours | Monthly average | 2% of monthly SOC fee per breach, cap 15% |
| P2 Response Engagement | ≤ 4 hours | Each P2 incident | 1% of monthly SOC fee per breach, cap 10% |
| Vulnerability Remediation (Critical/High) | ≤ 7 days | Monthly | 2% of monthly fee per breach, cap 10% |
| Reporting Timeliness (Monthly Report) | Delivered within 5 Business Days post-month-end | Each month | 1% of monthly fee per breach, cap 5% |

### 17.2 SLA Terms
17.2.1 Measurement. Availability excludes approved maintenance windows (max 4 hours/month, scheduled with 7 days’ notice).  
17.2.2 Credits. Service credits are applied against the next invoice and constitute the sole remedy for SLA breaches, except for chronic failure.  
17.2.3 Chronic Failure. If targets are missed for three consecutive months or five months in any rolling 12-month period, Customer may terminate the affected Service for cause without penalty, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.  
17.2.4 Exclusions. SLA does not apply to failures caused by Customer systems, force majeure, or unauthorized changes by Customer or third parties not under Supplier control.  
17.2.5 Reporting. Supplier will provide monthly KPI dashboards and root cause analyses for P1 events and any SLA breach within 5 Business Days.

## 18. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
18.1 BCP/DR. Supplier maintains tested BCP/DR plans; annual test results and remediation plans will be shared on request.  
18.2 RTO/RPO. Critical service components: RTO ≤ 4 hours; RPO ≤ 1 hour.  
18.3 Pandemic and Workforce Continuity. Remote operations procedures with secure access and monitoring remain in effect as needed.

## 19. Liability and Indemnification
19.1 Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party’s aggregate liability arising out of or related to the Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer for the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to liability.  
19.2 Excluded Claims. The limitations do not apply to: (a) breach of confidentiality; (b) infringement indemnity; (c) data protection breach caused by gross negligence or willful misconduct; (d) bodily injury or tangible property damage; (e) fraud, gross negligence, or willful misconduct; (f) unpaid fees.  
19.3 Exclusion of Consequential Damages. Neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, punitive, or consequential damages, loss of profits or revenue, or business interruption, except to the extent such damages are part of third-party claims indemnified under Section 19.4.  
19.4 Indemnification by Supplier. Supplier shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer against third-party claims alleging (a) IP infringement by the Services or Deliverables; (b) Supplier’s breach of data protection obligations; or (c) bodily injury or property damage caused by Supplier. Supplier may procure the right to continue use, modify, or replace infringing items; if not feasible, Supplier will refund prepaid fees for the affected Services on a pro-rata basis.  
19.5 Indemnification by Customer. Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Supplier against third-party claims arising from Customer Data or instructions that cause infringement, provided Supplier notifies Customer and cooperates in the defense.  
19.6 Procedure. Indemnified Party will provide prompt notice, reasonable cooperation, and allow control of the defense to the Indemnifying Party; settlement requires prior written consent not to be unreasonably withheld.

## 20. Termination and Exit Management
20.1 Termination for Cause. Either Party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days after written notice (10 days for payment breaches).  
20.2 Termination for Convenience. Customer may terminate any SOW for convenience upon 30 days’ notice; Customer pays for Services rendered up to the effective termination date and non-cancellable commitments approved in writing.  
20.3 Effect of Termination. All licenses granted to Supplier cease; Supplier will return or destroy Customer Data per Section 9.9.  
20.4 Transition Assistance. For up to 90 days post-termination (or longer by agreement), Supplier will provide reasonable transition services at agreed rates, including knowledge transfer, data export in industry-standard formats, and cooperation with successor providers.  
20.5 Suspension. Supplier may suspend Services for material security risks or illegal use with immediate notice; Services will resume upon remediation.

## 21. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
21.1 Informal Resolution. The Parties will attempt to resolve disputes via the governance process in Section 1.4 within 15 Business Days.  
21.2 Mediation. If unresolved, the Parties will engage in non-binding mediation under the rules of [Mediation Body] within 30 days.  
21.3 Arbitration or Courts. Thereafter, disputes shall be resolved by [binding arbitration under AAA rules] or [courts of competent jurisdiction] in [Governing Law State/Country], excluding its conflict of laws principles.  
21.4 Injunctive Relief. Either Party may seek injunctive or equitable relief at any time for breach of confidentiality or IP rights.

## 22. Notices
22.1 Notices must be in writing and delivered by email with confirmation, certified mail, or courier to the addresses set forth in the SOW.  
22.2 Notice is effective upon receipt or the next Business Day for confirmed email.

## 23. Miscellaneous
23.1 Assignment. Neither Party may assign without the other’s consent, except to affiliates or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, with notice.  
23.2 Independent Contractors. The Parties are independent contractors; no agency, partnership, or joint venture is created.  
23.3 Publicity. Neither Party may use the other’s name or marks without prior written consent.  
23.4 Force Majeure. Neither Party is liable for delays due to events beyond reasonable control; the affected Party will mitigate and notify the other.  
23.5 Severability. If any provision is unenforceable, the remainder remains in effect.  
23.6 Waiver. Failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver.  
23.7 Entire Agreement. This Agreement and incorporated documents constitute the entire agreement and supersede prior discussions.  
23.8 Counterparts and E-Signatures. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and via electronic signatures.

# Service Level Annex

## A. Severity Definitions
A.1 P1: Active compromise or outage with material impact to regulated data, mission-critical systems, or safety.  
A.2 P2: Significant degradation or confirmed malicious activity without immediate material impact.  
A.3 P3: Suspicious activity requiring investigation; minimal impact.  
A.4 P4: Informational events and tuning.

## B. Maintenance Windows
B.1 Standard: Sundays 00:00–04:00 [Time Zone], with 7 days’ notice.  
B.2 Emergency: As needed to address critical vulnerabilities, with as much notice as practicable.

# Data Processing Addendum (Summary Terms)
1. Subject Matter and Duration: Processing as necessary to provide Services during the Term and transition period.  
2. Nature and Purpose: Managed security operations, SIEM, and incident response.  
3. Categories of Data Subjects: Customer employees, contractors, and end-users; may include Customer’s customers.  
4. Categories of Personal Data: Identifiers, contact details, device identifiers, logs, and security events; no special category data unless explicitly authorized.  
5. Confidentiality of Processing: Personnel bound by confidentiality obligations and trained annually.  
6. Data Security: As per Section 10 and Supplier’s documented controls aligned to ISO 27001.  
7. Subprocessing: As per Section 9.6 with prior approval and continuous transparency.  
8. International Transfers: Standard Contractual Clauses and supplemental measures as required.  
9. Assistance and Cooperation: DPIA support, breach notification, and data subject requests.  
10. Return/Deletion: As per Section 9.9, with certificate of destruction upon request.

# Compliance Matrix

# Exhibits and Attachments (to be completed at contracting)

response:
# Technical Strategy and Approach

## Executive Summary
We propose a modern, standards-aligned Security Operations capability delivering 24/7 monitoring, rapid incident response (≤ 1 hour for high-severity incidents), and an enterprise-grade SIEM/SOAR platform. The solution is designed for high availability, scalability, and compliance with ISO/IEC 27001. It integrates seamlessly with existing IT operations, cloud platforms, and business applications, and establishes clear governance with the CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal, and Procurement.

Key outcomes:
- Always-on SOC with follow-the-sun coverage and defined SLAs.
- SIEM/SOAR implementation with detection engineering mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and CIS Controls.
- IR playbooks meeting ≤ 60-minute response time for Sev-1 and integrated legal/forensics workflows.
- ISO 27001-aligned processes, artifacts, and continuous improvement mechanisms.

---

# Technical Architecture

## High-Level Design
Figure 1: Security Operations Architecture (described)
- Ingestion Layer: Syslog/HTTPS agents, cloud-native connectors, endpoint/EDR telemetry. Edge collectors deployed per site/VPC/VNet.
- Stream/Parse Layer: Normalization to a common schema (e.g., Splunk CIM or Elastic Common Schema), enrichment (GeoIP, asset/CMDB, threat intel STIX/TAXII).
- SIEM Core: Correlation rules, UEBA, ML-driven anomaly detection, detections mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.
- SOAR/Automation: Playbooks for triage, containment (EDR isolate, firewall rules), evidence collection, ticketing/notification.
- Data Lake/Storage: Hot/warm/cold tiers with lifecycle policies, WORM options for compliance, cross-region backup.
- Threat Intelligence: Commercial and open-source feeds, MISP/TAXII ingestion, indicator scoring/de-duplication.
- Case Management/IR: Integrated ITSM (ServiceNow/Jira), incident taxonomy, chain-of-custody, evidence vault.
- Governance and Reporting: Executive dashboards for CISO, operational KPIs for IT Ops, compliance reports for audits.
- Identity and Access: SSO/MFA with RBAC and just-in-time elevated access.
- HA/DR: Multi-AZ active-active for SIEM analytics; RPO ≤ 15 min, RTO ≤ 2 hours.

## Network and Security Zones
- Logging DMZ: Receives events over TLS 1.2/1.3 from on-prem, cloud, and SaaS.
- Analytics Zone: SIEM/SOAR, UEBA, data processing with micro-segmentation and deny-by-default.
- Management Zone: Admin jump hosts, bastions, PAM, and KMS/HSM for keys.
- Evidence Vault: Immutable storage for forensic artifacts with strict RBAC and legal hold.

---

# System Requirements and Specifications

## Functional Requirements
- 24/7 SOC monitoring and triage across endpoint, network, cloud, identity, email, and application layers.
- SIEM correlation and UEBA with MITRE ATT&CK-aligned use cases.
- IR within 1 hour for Sev-1 (containment decision and initial actions), per RFP.
- Automated playbooks for containment, notifications, and evidence capture.
- Threat hunting, purple-team exercises, and continuous detection engineering.
- Compliance reporting (ISO 27001, audit trails, control effectiveness).

## Non-Functional Requirements
- Availability: ≥ 99.9% SIEM/SOAR service availability.
- Performance: End-to-end detection latency ≤ 5 minutes for priority log sources; alert to action automation < 2 minutes.
- Scalability: Horizontal scaling to ≥ 100k EPS with burst handling (autoscales on cloud).
- Retention: 365 days searchable; 1–7 years cold archive (policy-driven).
- Security: Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3), at rest (AES-256), FIPS 140-2 validated crypto modules where available.
- Data Residency: Data stored in approved regions; data classification and masking for PII/PHI.

## Service Levels
- MTTD (Sev-1): ≤ 15 minutes.
- MTTR Initial Response (Sev-1): ≤ 60 minutes (Incident Commander engaged, containment initiated).
- Triage Response (Sev-2): ≤ 2 hours.
- Use Case False Positive Rate: < 5% after tuning period.
- Log Onboarding SLA: Critical sources within 2 weeks of project phase start.

---

# Technology Stack and Tools

## Preferred Technology Options (final selection with Procurement)
| Capability | Primary Options | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SIEM | Microsoft Sentinel; Splunk Enterprise Security; Elastic Security | Cloud-native vs self-managed based on cost/EPS and data residency |
| SOAR | Sentinel Playbooks; Splunk SOAR; Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR | Prebuilt playbooks for IR, EDR, firewalls, ITSM |
| EDR/XDR | Microsoft Defender for Endpoint; CrowdStrike; SentinelOne | Host isolation, telemetry to SIEM |
| Log Collection | Syslog-NG/Rsyslog; Beats/Fluent Bit; Azure/AWS/GCP native connectors | TLS mutual auth, certificate pinning |
| Threat Intel | MISP; Anomali; Recorded Future; OpenCTI | STIX/TAXII, IOC scoring |
| ITSM/CMDB | ServiceNow; Jira Service Management | Incident/case sync, CMDB enrichment |
| IAM/IDP | Azure AD/Entra; Okta; AD | SSO/MFA, SCIM provisioning, JIT admin |
| Key Management | Azure Key Vault; AWS KMS; HashiCorp Vault; HSM | Envelope encryption, key rotation |
| Evidence/Forensics | Velociraptor; KAPE; FTK; GRR | Chain-of-custody workflows |
| Observability | Grafana/Prometheus; CloudWatch; Azure Monitor | Platform health and capacity dashboards |

---

# Implementation Approach and Methodology

## Phased Delivery
1. Initiation and Discovery (Weeks 1–2)
   - Stakeholder workshops (CISO, IT Ops, Compliance, Legal, Procurement).
   - Current-state assessment: log sources, detections, incident history, controls.
   - Define KPIs, SLAs, RACI, data residency, and retention policies.

2. Architecture and Design (Weeks 2–4)
   - High-level and low-level designs; security zoning; HA/DR plans.
   - SIEM/SOAR selection with TCO/EPS sizing; control mapping to ISO 27001.
   - Runbook and playbook design aligned to ISO 27035 and legal requirements.

3. Build and Configuration (Weeks 4–8)
   - Deploy collectors, parsers, normalization (CIM/ECS), enrichment services.
   - Configure SIEM content: 60–100 priority detections mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.
   - Establish SOAR automations; integrate ITSM/CMDB and IDP.

4. Log Source Onboarding and Integrations (Weeks 6–12)
   - Prioritize crown-jewel assets: identity, email, EDR, firewalls, cloud control planes.
   - Validate data quality, timestamps, schemas; implement filtering and sampling policies.

5. SOC Onboarding and Training (Weeks 8–12)
   - Tier 1–3 processes, escalation paths, on-call schedules.
   - Tabletop exercises; red/purple team simulations; playbook dry runs.

6. UAT, Go-Live, and Hypercare (Weeks 12–14)
   - Performance and failover testing; SLA verification.
   - 24/7 cutover with enhanced monitoring; burn-in tuning.

7. Continuous Improvement (Ongoing)
   - Monthly use case sprints; threat intel updates; KPI reviews with stakeholders.
   - Quarterly attack simulations and compliance audits.

## Milestone-Based Deliverables
- M1: Approved Architecture & Runbooks
- M2: SIEM/SOAR Deployed & Core Integrations
- M3: Priority Log Sources Onboarded & Detections Enabled
- M4: SOC Go-Live & SLA Validation
- M5: Stabilization & ISO 27001 Control Evidence Package

---

# Integration Requirements

## Target Systems and Protocols
- Identity: AD/Azure AD/Okta via API, LDAP, Azure Graph; ingest sign-in and risk events.
- Cloud: AWS CloudTrail/GuardDuty, Azure Activity/Defender, GCP Audit Logs via native connectors.
- Endpoint/EDR: Sensor telemetry, alerts, host isolation APIs.
- Network: Firewalls (Palo Alto, Cisco, Fortinet), IDS/IPS, VPNs via syslog/TLS.
- Email/SaaS: Microsoft 365, Google Workspace; O365 audit logs, Defender for Office alerts.
- Applications: Web servers (IIS/Nginx), databases (SQL/Aurora), custom apps via OpenTelemetry/HTTP.
- ITSM/CMDB: ServiceNow/Jira bi-directional ticket sync; CMDB enrichment.
- Threat Intel: TAXII 2.1 feeds; MISP collections.
- Messaging/Collaboration: Teams/Slack for notifications and war room automation.

## Data Governance and Enrichment
- CMDB enrichment: asset criticality, owner, environment tag.
- User context: role, group, privileged user flag.
- Threat intel context: confidence score, first/last seen, TLP marking.

---

# Scalability and Performance Considerations

## Sizing and EPS Planning
| Tier | Daily Events | Peak EPS | SIEM Strategy | Storage Strategy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medium | 3–5B | 50–80k | Cloud SIEM with autoscale | 90 days hot, 275 days warm |
| Large | 8–12B | 120–200k | Hybrid scaling, partitioned indexers | 180 days hot, archive to object store |
| Enterprise+ | 12B+ | 200k+ | Multi-region; cross-cluster federation | Tiered storage + WORM for compliance |

- Burst handling with queueing and backpressure (Kafka-compatible or native buffers).
- Parser optimization and schema normalization to minimize index cost and query latency.
- Horizontal scale-out of indexers/analytics nodes; shard rebalancing; tiered caching.

## HA/DR
- Multi-AZ deployments; quorum-based clusters; stateless collectors.
- RPO ≤ 15 minutes via continuous replication; RTO ≤ 2 hours with automated failover.

---

# Security Architecture

## Zero Trust and Access Control
- Identity-centric policy enforcement; device and user risk signals.
- SSO with MFA, conditional access, RBAC least privilege, JIT privileged access via PAM.
- Admin access via bastion with session recording.

## Data Protection
- Encryption at rest (AES-256) with KMS/HSM-managed keys; rotation every 12 months or per policy.
- TLS 1.2/1.3 with mutual auth for collectors; certificate pinning and mTLS where supported.
- Data classification and masking for sensitive fields; tokenization for PII in logs.

## Platform Hardening
- CIS Benchmarks for OS, Kubernetes, and cloud services.
- Vulnerability management integrated with SIEM (CVE context in detections).
- Secure baselines and drift detection; IaC with policy-as-code (OPA/Conftest).

## Detection and Response
- Detection engineering mapped to MITRE ATT&CK; coverage metrics tracked.
- UEBA for insider threat and account takeover.
- SOAR playbooks: phishing, ransomware containment, credential compromise, exfiltration, BEC.
- Forensics and chain-of-custody with evidence vault; legal hold workflows with Legal.

---

# Security Operations Model

## 24/7 SOC Coverage
- Follow-the-sun with primary and secondary analysts per shift.
- Tiered response model: Tier 1 triage ≤ 15 min, Tier 2 investigation ≤ 30 min, Incident Commander within 60 min for Sev-1.

## Incident Severity and SLA
| Severity | Definition | Initial Response | Containment Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sev-1 | Active compromise or high-impact threat | ≤ 60 min | ≤ 2 hours |
| Sev-2 | Credible threat, limited impact | ≤ 2 hours | ≤ 8 hours |
| Sev-3 | Suspicious activity, low risk | Next business day | As agreed |

## Governance and Reporting
- Daily ops summary to IT Ops; weekly SOC review with CISO; monthly compliance pack to Compliance Officer.
- Quarterly tabletop and purple-team exercises; lessons learned with corrective action tracking.

---

# Technical Standards and Compliance

## Standards and Control Frameworks
- ISO/IEC 27001: ISMS alignment; SoA, risk assessment, internal audit, and management review.
- ISO/IEC 27035: Incident management process and playbooks.
- ISO/IEC 27002: Control selection for logging, monitoring, access control, cryptography.
- NIST CSF and SP 800-53 (moderate baseline mapping as applicable).
- CIS Controls v8 for control maturity and gap tracking.
- MITRE ATT&CK for detection coverage and reporting.
- Crypto: FIPS 140-2 validated modules where supported by platform.
- Privacy: GDPR/CCPA considerations for PII in telemetry; data minimization.

## Compliance Artifacts (Deliverables)
- ISMS-aligned policies: Logging & Monitoring, IR Plan, Access Control, Cryptographic Controls.
- Risk Register and SoA mapped to implemented controls.
- Audit-ready evidence: change records, access reviews, incident records, test results.

---

# Detailed Specifications

## Priority Log Sources and Onboarding
| Source | Method | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity (AD/Azure AD/Okta) | Native connectors/API | Critical | Sign-in, risk events, MFA failures |
| EDR/XDR | Vendor API/stream | Critical | Alerts, telemetry, isolation actions |
| Email Security (M365) | Graph API/O365 connectors | High | Phish, malware, BEC indicators |
| Firewalls/VPN/IDS | Syslog over TLS | High | Allow/deny, VPN auth, IDS alerts |
| Cloud Control Planes | Native connectors | High | CloudTrail, Azure Activity, Admin ops |
| Web/App/DB | Syslog/OTel exporters | Medium | Error spikes, auth failures, DLP |
| Proxy/DNS | Syslog/TLS | Medium | C2, DGA detection, exfiltration patterns |

## Detections and Use Cases (Examples)
- Credential theft and lateral movement (ATT&CK T1003, T1021).
- Ransomware behavior: mass encryption, shadow copy deletion, suspicious process trees.
- Exfiltration: unusual data volume to external destinations, DNS tunneling.
- Cloud privilege escalation: IAM policy changes, key creation anomalies.
- Business email compromise: mailbox rules, impossible travel, vendor bank change.

---

# Testing, Validation, and Acceptance

- Data Quality: Timestamp, hostname, completeness checks with automated alerts.
- Performance: EPS stress testing to 1.5x peak; query latency < 5s for standard searches.
- HA/DR: Failover exercises; recovery point/time verification.
- Security: Playbook dry runs; red/purple team validations; BAS platform (e.g., AttackIQ/SafeBreach) scenarios.
- UAT: Stakeholder sign-off (CISO, IT Ops, Compliance, Legal for IR/legal-hold workflows).

---

# Risk Management and Assumptions

## Key Risks and Mitigations
- Incomplete log coverage: Prioritized onboarding and automated coverage dashboards.
- Alert fatigue: Phased tuning, suppression rules, FP rate target < 5%.
- Data residency constraints: Regional data stores and policy-based routing.
- Tool sprawl/integration gaps: Standardized connectors and interface contracts; API-first design.

## Assumptions
- Access to required APIs and administrative privileges for integrations.
- Stakeholder availability for workshops and UAT.
- Procurement support for licensing aligned to EPS and retention targets.

---

# Deliverables

- Architecture: HLD/LLD diagrams, data flows, HA/DR runbooks.
- SIEM/SOAR: Configured platform, parsers, enrichment, 60–100 priority detections, dashboards.
- IR: Incident Response Plan, severity matrix, playbooks, communication templates.
- Compliance: ISO 27001 SoA, policies, control mappings, audit evidence pack.
- Operations: SOPs for Tier 1–3, on-call schedule, RACI, training materials.
- Reports: Executive dashboards, KPI packs, monthly compliance and posture reports.

---

# KPIs and Continuous Improvement

- Coverage: % of critical assets and log sources onboarded (target ≥ 95%).
- SLA Adherence: Sev-1 initial response within 60 minutes (target ≥ 99%).
- Mean Time to Detect/Respond: Trend reduction ≥ 20% over first 2 quarters.
- Detection Efficacy: True Positive rate and use case ROI; ATT&CK coverage score.
- Compliance: Audit findings closure within agreed timelines; ISO 27001 surveillance success.

---

# Cost and Performance Optimization (Guiding Principles)

- Right-size ingestion via field filtering, deduplication, and dynamic sampling.
- Tiered storage with lifecycle policies and just-in-time rehydration.
- Leverage cloud-native capabilities (serverless collectors, autoscale analytics) where compliant.
- Reuse existing investments (EDR, ITSM, IDP) with deep integration to reduce MTTR.

---

# Stakeholder Engagement Plan

- CISO: Executive dashboards; risk and KPI reviews; strategy updates.
- IT Operations Manager: Operational runbooks; change windows; platform SLOs.
- Compliance Officer: ISO 27001 evidence, SoA updates, audit support.
- Legal Department: Breach notification decision trees; legal hold; counsel engagement.
- Procurement Team: Tool selection matrices, license/EPS forecasts, milestone-based acceptance.

This technical strategy delivers a robust, scalable, and compliant Security Operations capability aligned with ISO 27001, meeting the RFP’s 24/7 monitoring, SIEM implementation, and 1-hour incident response requirements. It is designed for rapid value realization, strong stakeholder alignment, and sustained continuous improvement.

# Financial Proposal

## Executive Summary
- This financial proposal supports the RFP requirement for 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation, 1-hour incident response, and ISO 27001 compliance enablement.
- We provide two pricing options to align with budget preferences while maintaining the same service-level commitments:
  - Option A: Fixed-Fee Managed Security Subscription (predictable OpEx).
  - Option B: Hybrid Consumption Model (lower base with variable usage and incident overages).
- Payment terms align with the provided contract guidelines: Net 30 days after invoice approval, milestone-based payments for implementation, and a 10% retention on project invoices until completion.

## Pricing Model Options

### Option A: Fixed-Fee Managed Security Subscription (Recommended)
- Scope: End-to-end 24/7 SOC, SIEM deployment and management, incident response (1-hour SLA), threat intelligence, compliance reporting, and ISO 27001 control mapping support.
- Commercial profile:
  - One-time implementation fee (CapEx): $150,000
  - Recurring managed service fee (OpEx): $58,250 per month
  - Annual Recurring: $699,000
  - 3-Year TCO (no escalation): $2,247,000

### Option B: Hybrid Consumption Model
- Scope: Same as Option A, with variable/usage-based charges to optimize for lower baseline consumption.
- Commercial profile:
  - One-time implementation fee (CapEx): $120,000
  - Base managed service fee (OpEx): $42,000 per month
  - Variable usage:
    - SIEM data ingest above 50 GB/day: $35 per GB/day per month
    - Incident response hours beyond included 20 hours/month: $225 per hour

# Quality Assurance and Testing Plan

## QA Governance and Standards Alignment
### Standards and Frameworks
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (mandatory) — ISMS controls, risk management, continuous improvement
- ISO 9001:2015 — Quality management and documented procedures
- ISTQB — Testing principles, terminology, and lifecycle practices
- NIST SP 800-61r2 — Computer Security Incident Handling Guide (incident response)
- OWASP ASVS/SAMM — Application and security validation practices
- ITIL v4 — Service operations, incident, change, and problem management

### Stakeholders and Responsibilities
- CISO: Approves security acceptance criteria, risk treatment, and final security sign-off
- IT Operations Manager: Owns operational readiness, monitoring, and deployment approvals
- Compliance Officer: Verifies ISO 27001 control conformance and audit evidence
- Legal Department: Reviews regulatory/compliance attestations and data handling commitments
- Procurement Team: Confirms milestone evidence for payment and retention release
- QA Lead (Vendor): Owns QA strategy, test planning, execution oversight, and reporting
- SOC Manager (Vendor): Owns 24/7 monitoring readiness, SIEM runbook quality, IR drills
- Project Manager: Milestone tracking, change control, risk/issue management

## Testing Strategy and Methodology
### Approach
- Risk-based, requirements-driven testing with full traceability to RFP items
- Shift-left with early reviews of requirements, threat models, and designs
- Automation-first for regression, security scans, and performance benchmarking
- Multi-level testing: unit, integration, system, security, performance, UAT, operational readiness
- DevSecOps integration in CI/CD with gated releases

### Test Levels and Types
1. Unit and Integration Tests — Functional correctness, interface contracts
2. System and End-to-End Tests — Workflow validation across components
3. Security Testing — SAST, DAST, SCA, configuration hardening, penetration testing, SIEM rule validation
4. Performance and Load Testing — Throughput, latency (p50/p95/p99), resource utilization, spike/soak
5. Operational Readiness Tests (ORT) — Monitoring, alerting, backup/restore, DR runbooks
6. User Acceptance Testing (UAT) — Scenario-based validation against business needs
7. Compliance Verification — ISO 27001 evidence, policy/procedure reviews, control testing

### Environments and Data
- Environments: Dev → Test → Staging (Production-like) → Production
- Test data management: Synthetic/anonymized data sets, data masking, GDPR-aligned handling
- Configuration as code: Version-controlled IaC, SIEM parsers, correlation rules, dashboards

## Test Planning and Execution
### Test Plan Overview

| Phase | Objectives | Scope | Environment | Entry Criteria | Exit Criteria | Deliverables |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Planning | Define scope, risks, resources, schedule | All RFP requirements | N/A | Approved requirements baseline, risk register | Approved Master Test Plan | Test Plan, Traceability Matrix, Test Data Plan |
| Preparation | Develop cases, scripts, automation, data | Functional, security, performance, ORT, UAT | Test/Staging | Test env ready; seeded data; tooling configured | Test Readiness Review sign-off | Test Cases, Automation Suites, Test Data |
| Execution | Run tests, capture evidence, triage defects | All planned test suites | Test/Staging | TRR complete; stable build | Exit criteria met per suite | Test Results, Defect Log, Evidence Repo |
| Performance | Validate throughput/latency/resource targets | Load/spike/soak tests | Staging (prod-like) | Stable build; data generators | Metrics within thresholds | Performance Report and Baseline |
| Security | Validate security posture, ISO mapping | SAST/DAST/SCA, pentest, IR drills | Staging/Production (as allowed) | Authorizations, scoping | Zero critical vulns; IR SLA met | Security Test Report, ISO Evidence |
| UAT | Business validation and sign-off | Priority business workflows | Staging | Functional pass ≥ 95%; Sev1/2 closed | Stakeholder sign-offs | UAT Scripts, Sign-off Memo |
| ORT/Go-Live | Operational readiness and runbooks | Monitoring, alerting, backup, DR | Prod/Pre-prod | UAT signed; change approvals | Go-live checklist complete | ORT Report, Go-Live Approval |

### Execution Cadence
- Daily defect triage; weekly QA status to stakeholders; phase gate reviews at each milestone

## Acceptance Criteria and Testing Procedures
### Acceptance Criteria (Aligned to RFP)
1. 24/7 SOC Monitoring: Demonstrated continuous monitoring coverage with documented runbooks, on-call roster, and escalation paths.
2. SIEM Implementation: Centralized log ingestion from in-scope sources ≥ 95% coverage with validated parsers and correlation rules; dashboards and alerting configured.
3. Incident Response SLA: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) ≤ 15 minutes and time to begin containment (TTBC) ≤ 60 minutes for high/critical incidents, measured across drills and live incidents.
4. ISO 27001 Compliance: ISMS scope, risk assessment, Statement of Applicability, and control implementation evidence complete; internal audit passed; management review documented.
5. Performance: SIEM ingestion supports peak load with sustained throughput meeting design targets; alert generation latency p95 within threshold; system stability maintained in soak.
6. Defects: 0 open Severity 1 and 0 open Severity 2 defects at go-live; Severity 3 ≤ 5 with agreed workarounds and remediation plan.
7. UAT: ≥ 95% UAT test case pass rate; all business-critical workflows pass; formal sign-offs received from CISO, IT Operations Manager, and Compliance Officer.
8. Documentation: All runbooks, SOPs, architecture diagrams, and evidence repositories complete and handed over.

### Key Testing Procedures
1. SIEM Log Onboarding and Coverage Test
   1. Identify in-scope sources (firewalls, endpoints, servers, cloud, identity).
   2. Configure connectors/agents and parsers.
   3. Generate representative test events per source.
   4. Verify ingestion, parsing fields, timestamps, and normalization.
   5. Validate correlation rules fire expected alerts.
   6. Confirm dashboards and reports display metrics accurately.
2. 24/7 SOC Monitoring Continuity Test
   1. Review staffing schedule and on-call roster for a full week.
   2. Inject test alerts across 24-hour cycles (including nights/weekends).
   3. Measure MTTA, escalation timing, and analyst actions.
   4. Validate handover notes between shifts and shift-change procedures.
3. Incident Response SLA Validation (1-Hour Response)
   1. Execute unannounced high-severity incident tabletop and live drill.
   2. Record alert time, acknowledgment time, containment start time.
   3. Verify communication to stakeholders within runbook timelines.
   4. Capture artifacts: tickets, chat transcripts, evidence logs.
4. ISO 27001 Control Conformance Test
   1. Review risk assessment and SoA mapping to implemented controls.
   2. Sample evidence for controls (e.g., A.5–A.8 governance, access, ops).
   3. Verify policy approvals, training records, monitoring, and audit logs.
   4. Conduct internal audit and management review; record findings.
5. Performance and Load Test for SIEM
   1. Model daily and peak EPS (events per second) with growth factor.
   2. Run stepped load, spike, and 24-hour soak tests.
   3. Measure ingestion throughput, queue depth, rule evaluation latency.
   4. Validate autoscaling, backpressure handling, and data loss = 0.

## Quality Metrics and KPIs
- Requirements coverage ≥ 100% (requirements-to-tests traceability)
- Test case pass rate ≥ 95% before UAT; ≥ 98% for critical path
- Defect density ≤ 0.5 per KLOC (or per major feature module)
- Defect leakage to UAT ≤ 2%; to production ≤ 1%
- Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) security incidents ≤ 10 minutes; MTTA ≤ 15 minutes
- Incident response TTBC ≤ 60 minutes for high/critical incidents (≥ 99% compliance)
- SIEM log source coverage ≥ 95% of in-scope systems
- Alert fidelity: precision ≥ 80%, recall ≥ 85% for priority correlation rules
- Performance: Ingestion throughput meets peak EPS; alert latency p95 ≤ 60 seconds
- Change failure rate ≤ 10%; mean time to restore (MTTR) ≤ 2 hours
- ISO 27001 audit nonconformities: zero major; ≤ 2 minor with corrective actions

### Quality Metrics Matrix

| Metric | Definition | Target | Data Source | Frequency | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Requirements Coverage | % of requirements with ≥ 1 passing test | 100% | RTM, Test Mgmt | Weekly | QA Lead |
| Test Case Pass Rate | Passed/Executed test cases | ≥ 95% pre-UAT; ≥ 98% critical | Test Mgmt | Daily | QA Lead |
| Defect Density | Defects per KLOC/feature | ≤ 0.5 | Defect Tracker | Weekly | QA Lead |
| Defect Leakage | % defects found in UAT/Prod | UAT ≤ 2%; Prod ≤ 1% | Defect Tracker | Per phase | QA Lead |
| MTTD/MTTA | Detect/Acknowledge times | MTTD ≤ 10m; MTTA ≤ 15m | SIEM/SOAR, ITSM | Weekly | SOC Manager |
| IR SLA Compliance | % critical incidents with TTBC ≤ 60m | ≥ 99% | ITSM, Drill Logs | Monthly | SOC Manager |
| Log Coverage | % in-scope sources sending parsed logs | ≥ 95% | SIEM Dashboards | Weekly | SIEM Engineer |
| Alert Fidelity | Precision/Recall on key rules | ≥ 80% / ≥ 85% | Labelled Alerts | Monthly | Threat Intel |
| Performance Throughput | Sustained EPS under peak | Meets design | Perf Tooling | Per release | Perf Engineer |
| Alert Latency p95 | Time event→alert | ≤ 60s | SIEM Metrics | Per release | Perf Engineer |
| ISO 27001 Nonconformities | Major/minor audit findings | 0 major; ≤ 2 minor | Audit Reports | Per audit | Compliance Officer |
| Change Failure Rate | % failed changes requiring rollback | ≤ 10% | ITSM | Monthly | IT Ops Manager |
| MTTR | Mean time to restore after failure | ≤ 2h | ITSM | Monthly | IT Ops Manager |

## Defect, Bug Tracking, and Resolution
### Severity and Priority
- Sev 1: Critical outage/security breach; Sev 2: Major function impaired; Sev 3: Minor defect; Sev 4: Cosmetic/documentation

### Process
1. Log: Create ticket with repro steps, environment, evidence, and impact.
2. Triage: Assign severity/priority within 4 business hours (Sev1 immediate).
3. Assignment: Route to owner with ETA and remediation plan.
4. Fix and Verify: Implement fix; peer review; retest; regression suite.
5. RCA: For Sev1/2, complete root cause analysis within 3 business days.
6. Closure: Confirm acceptance criteria and evidence; update traceability.

### SLAs
- Triage: Sev1 immediate; Sev2 ≤ 4h; Sev3 ≤ 1 business day; Sev4 ≤ 2 business days
- Workaround: Sev1 ≤ 4h; Sev2 ≤ 1 business day
- Resolution: Sev1 ≤ 24h; Sev2 ≤ 3 business days; Sev3 ≤ 10 business days; Sev4 per backlog
- Communication: Hourly updates (Sev1), twice daily (Sev2), weekly (Sev3/4)

## Performance and Load Testing
### Objectives
- Validate SIEM can ingest peak EPS without data loss
- Ensure correlation/alert latency within thresholds
- Confirm system stability under sustained load and rapid spikes

### Scenarios
1. Baseline Load: Average daily EPS with normal variance
2. Peak Load: 2× baseline EPS for 2 hours
3. Spike: 5× baseline EPS for 10 minutes
4. Soak: 24-hour steady-state at ≥ baseline EPS
5. Failure Injection: Connector drops, network jitter, delayed logs

### Metrics
- Ingestion throughput (EPS), queue/backlog depth
- Alert generation latency (p50/p95/p99)
- Resource utilization (CPU, memory, I/O), autoscaling behavior
- Error/retry rate, data loss (must be 0)
- Time-to-catch-up after backlog ≤ 30 minutes for 2× baseline

### Tooling and Evidence
- Load generators (e.g., Kafka producers/log replayers), APM/infra metrics, SIEM native telemetry
- Performance report with charts, raw logs, and threshold comparisons

## Security Testing and Compliance
### Security Testing Scope
1. SAST/DAST/SCA integrated in CI/CD with blocking on critical findings
2. Penetration Testing (internal/external) with remediation verification
3. Configuration Hardening: Benchmarks (e.g., CIS) for hosts, network, SIEM
4. Vulnerability Management: CVSS-based prioritization; zero criticals at release
5. SIEM Correlation Validation: Test rule efficacy, tuning to reduce false positives
6. Incident Response Drills: Tabletop and hands-on, unannounced and scheduled
7. Access Controls: RBAC reviews, least privilege, MFA enforcement
8. Logging and Monitoring: Coverage, retention, immutability, time sync

### ISO 27001 Mapping and Evidence

| RFP Requirement | ISO 27001 Control (Annex A) | Test Method | Evidence | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24/7 SOC Monitoring | A.8.16 Monitoring activities | ORT, drill observation | Monitoring SOPs, shift rosters, alert logs | Continuous coverage demonstrated |
| SIEM Implementation | A.8.15 Logging; A.8.16 Monitoring | Functional, perf tests | Parser configs, coverage dashboard, alert tests | ≥ 95% source coverage; alert fidelity targets |
| 1-Hour IR | A.5.24 Incident mgmt; A.5.26 Response | IR drills, ticket review | Timestamps MTTA/TTBC, comms records | TTBC ≤ 60m at ≥ 99% |
| ISO Compliance | ISMS scope, SoA, internal audit | Document review, audit | SoA, risk log, audit report, MR minutes | 0 major nonconformities |

## User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
### Process
1. Entry: Functional pass ≥ 95%; no open Sev1/2; environment signed-off
2. Script Development: Business-led with QA support; scenarios mapped to requirements
3. Execution: Stakeholders execute scripts; vendor facilitates and captures evidence
4. Defect Handling: UAT defects triaged and resolved with targeted re-tests
5. Exit: ≥ 95% pass rate; all critical workflows pass; sign-offs from CISO, IT Ops, Compliance

### UAT Roles
- Business Testers (Client): Primary execution and acceptance
- QA Lead (Vendor): Coordination, evidence, defect management
- CISO/Compliance Officer: Security/compliance sign-off
- IT Operations Manager: Operational readiness acceptance

## Traceability Matrices
### Requirements-to-Tests Matrix (Excerpt)

| Requirement ID | Requirement | Test Case IDs | Status | Evidence Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-SEC-001 | 24/7 SOC Monitoring | TC-SEC-003, TC-OPS-002 | Planned | Repo/Evidence/SOC |
| R-SEC-002 | SIEM ≥ 95% Coverage | TC-SIEM-001, TC-PERF-002 | In Progress | Repo/Evidence/SIEM |
| R-IR-001 | IR TTBC ≤ 60m | TC-IR-004, TC-IR-005 | Planned | Repo/Evidence/IR |
| R-ISO-001 | ISO 27001 Compliance | TC-ISO-007 | Planned | Repo/Evidence/ISO |

## Sample Test Cases (Excerpt)

| ID | Requirement | Description | Steps | Expected Result | Acceptance Criteria | Priority | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-SIEM-001 | SIEM Coverage | Validate ingestion from all in-scope sources | 1) Configure connectors; 2) Generate test events; 3) Verify parsing/normalization | All sources ingest and parse correctly | ≥ 95% sources active; 0 parsing errors | High | SIEM dashboards, parser logs |
| TC-SEC-003 | 24/7 Monitoring | Validate shift handover and after-hours alert handling | 1) Inject alerts at night/weekend; 2) Measure MTTA; 3) Review handover notes | Alerts acknowledged within SLA; complete handovers | MTTA ≤ 15m; no missed alerts | High | ITSM tickets, chat logs |
| TC-IR-004 | 1-Hour IR | Validate containment start within 60 minutes | 1) Trigger high-sev drill; 2) Track timestamps; 3) Confirm containment actions | Containment initiated ≤ 60m | TTBC ≤ 60m; comms per runbook | High | Drill report, ITSM |
| TC-PERF-002 | Ingestion Throughput | Validate peak EPS handling | 1) Run 2× peak EPS; 2) Monitor queues; 3) Assess latency | No data loss; stable latency | Data loss = 0; p95 alert ≤ 60s | High | Perf charts, logs |
| TC-SEC-006 | Alert Fidelity | Validate rule precision/recall | 1) Replay labelled events; 2) Measure hits/false positives | Accurate detections; low false positives | Precision ≥ 80%; Recall ≥ 85% | Medium | Confusion matrix |
| TC-ISO-007 | ISO Evidence | Verify ISMS artifacts and audit | 1) Review SoA; 2) Sample controls; 3) Verify audit closure | Complete documentation; no major NCs | 0 major; ≤ 2 minor with CAPA | High | Audit report |
| TC-UAT-010 | UAT Sign-off | Validate business workflow | 1) Execute UAT script; 2) Record results; 3) Obtain sign-off | Workflow passes; sign-off recorded | 100% pass for critical flow | High | Signed UAT memo |

## Quality Assurance Processes
### Requirements and Change Management
1. Baseline requirements with version control; maintain RTM

1.9 “SLA” means the service level agreements and metrics set forth herein.

1.11 “Applicable Law” means all applicable laws, regulations, codes, standards, and directives, including data protection laws and industry standards (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001).  
1.12 “Business Day” means any day other than a weekend or public holiday at Customer’s primary place of business.

## 2. Stakeholder Governance
2.1 The following stakeholders will participate in governance: CISO (executive sponsor), IT Operations Manager (technical owner), Compliance Officer (regulatory oversight), Legal Department (contractual compliance), Procurement Team (commercial governance).  
2.2 Provider will establish a Joint Governance Committee (JGC) comprising designated representatives of the above roles and Provider’s account manager and security lead.  
2.3 The JGC will meet at least quarterly to review performance, risk, compliance posture, audit findings, and roadmap; monthly operational reviews will be held with IT Operations and SOC leadership.

3.7 Reporting and governance: weekly operational reports, monthly KPI/MTTR reviews, and quarterly executive reviews.

3.9 Optional services: threat hunting, DFIR surge support, red/purple team exercises, cloud and endpoint telemetry integration.

4.1 Project plan and onboarding schedule within 10 Business Days of contract effective date.  
4.2 SIEM architecture, data source roadmap, and log ingestion plan.  
4.3 Use-case catalogue and alert tuning backlog with risk prioritization.  
4.4 Incident response runbooks aligned with Customer policies.  
4.5 Baseline and steady-state reports: weekly SOC report, monthly KPI dashboard, quarterly risk and compliance report.  
4.6 Knowledge transfer sessions and documentation.  
4.7 Final project completion report and acceptance package.

# Contract Terms and Conditions

## 5. Term and Renewal
5.1 Initial Term: 12–36 months from Effective Date (as specified in the Order or SOW).  
5.2 Renewal: auto-renewal for successive 12-month terms unless either Party provides 60 days’ notice prior to expiration.

## 6. Order of Precedence
6.1 In case of conflict: (1) Executed Change Orders, (2) Statement(s) of Work, (3) this Agreement, (4) Policies/Schedules, (5) RFP and Provider’s proposal, (6) Purchase Orders (commercial terms only).

## 7. Acceptance
7.1 Deliverables will be subject to written acceptance criteria in the SOW.  
7.2 Customer will accept or reject deliverables within 10 Business Days of delivery.  
7.3 If rejected, Provider will remedy non-conformities within a commercially reasonable time and re-submit.

## 8. Change Control
8.1 Material changes to scope, deliverables, or timelines require a written Change Order, including impacts to schedule, cost, and risk.  
8.2 No Party is obligated to commence changed work absent an executed Change Order.

## 9. Subcontracting
9.1 Provider may use qualified Subcontractors/Subprocessors with Customer’s prior written approval; Provider remains fully responsible.  
9.2 Provider will flow down confidentiality, security, and data protection obligations to all Subcontractors.

## 10. Personnel and Background Screening
10.1 Provider personnel accessing Customer systems/data will be background screened to industry standards and trained on security, privacy, and ethics annually.  
10.2 Provider will replace any assigned personnel at Customer’s reasonable request for cause.

## 11. Records and Audit
11.1 Provider will maintain complete and accurate records of Services, SLAs, security controls, and fees for at least 7 years (or longer where required by law).  
11.2 Customer and its auditors/regulators may audit upon 10 Business Days’ notice up to once per year (or more if required by law or following a material security incident).  
11.3 Provider will remediate material findings within an agreed timeline.

# Service Levels and Reporting

## 12. Priority Definitions
12.1 P1 (Critical): Active compromise, data exfiltration, or material service outage/security risk.  
12.2 P2 (High): High-risk suspicious activity or active threat needing rapid action.  
12.3 P3 (Medium): Non-urgent anomalies, tuning, or advisory cases.  
12.4 P4 (Low): Routine requests, reporting, or informational tasks.

## 13. Service Level Agreements (SLAs)
| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Reporting | Service Credits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24/7 SOC Coverage | 100% continuous monitoring | Staffing rosters + system uptime logs | Monthly | 2% MRC credit per hour of unstaffed coverage, capped at 15% |
| SIEM Platform Availability | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Synthetic checks + platform telemetry | Monthly | 3% MRC per 0.1% below target, capped at 15% |
| P1 Initial Response | ≤ 1 hour from alert creation | Ticket timestamps | Monthly + real-time dashboard | 5% MRC per validated breach of target (max 15%) |
| P2 Initial Response | ≤ 4 hours | Ticket timestamps | Monthly | 2% MRC per breach (max 10%) |
| Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) P1 | ≤ 15 minutes median | Correlation timestamps | Monthly | 2% MRC if median > target |
| Mean Time to Contain (MTTC) Guidance for P1 | ≤ 4 hours | Ticket and comms log | Monthly | 3% MRC per breach (max 12%) |
| Use Case Tuning Backlog Burn | ≥ 90% of committed items per month | Sprint reports | Monthly | 2% MRC if < 90% |
| Log Ingestion Coverage | ≥ 95% of in-scope sources | Source inventory + health status | Monthly | 2% MRC if < 95% |
| Report Delivery | 100% on schedule | Report timestamps | Monthly | 1% MRC per late report (max 5%) |

Notes:
- MRC = Monthly Recurring Charges for in-scope Services.  
- Service credits are not penalties and are Customer’s exclusive monetary remedy for SLA failures, except in cases of chronic failure (3 consecutive months or 4 months in any rolling 12), which allows termination for chronic failure with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

## 14. Reporting and Reviews
14.1 Weekly: incident summaries, tuning progress, open risks.  
14.2 Monthly: SLA report, KPI dashboard (MTTD/MTTR/alert volume), capacity/utilization, service credits if any.  
14.3 Quarterly: executive review, compliance attestation updates (e.g., ISO 27001), roadmap and risk register.

# Security and Regulatory Compliance

## 15. Mandatory Standards and Controls
15.1 ISO/IEC 27001: Provider will maintain certification and provide current certificate and Statement of Applicability.  
15.2 NIST CSF and CIS Controls: Provider aligns controls and will furnish mapping on request.  
15.3 Logging and Retention: Retain SIEM logs minimum 365 days online and 1–2 years archived, unless otherwise required by law or SOW.  
15.4 Access Controls: MFA for privileged access; RBAC with least privilege; quarterly access reviews.  
15.5 Encryption: Data in transit via TLS 1.2+; data at rest AES-256 or equivalent.  
15.6 Secure Development and Change: Change management with approvals; infrastructure-as-code where applicable; segregation of environments.  
15.7 Vulnerability and Patch Management: Critical patches within 14 days; High within 30 days or per risk-based exception with documented compensating controls.  
15.8 Business Continuity/Disaster Recovery: Documented BCP/DR with annual testing; RTO/RPO per SOW.  
15.9 Incident Management: Documented IR plan; joint exercises with Customer at least annually.

## 16. Compliance Matrix
| Requirement | Standard/Regulation | Control Reference | Party Responsible | Evidence | Compliance Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24/7 SOC Monitoring | ISO 27001 A.5, A.8, A.16 | SOC staffing, monitoring procedures | Provider | Staffing schedules, playbooks | Compliant |
| SIEM Implementation/Operations | ISO 27001 A.8, A.12 | Log mgmt, correlation rules | Provider | Architecture, tuning catalog | Compliant |
| 1-hour Incident Response (P1) | ISO 27001 A.16 | IR procedures, on-call | Provider | Ticket metrics | Compliant |
| Data Protection | GDPR, CPRA | Art. 28, 32; CPRA §1798.100+ | Joint | DPA, DPIAs, TOMs | Compliant (as applicable) |
| Audit and Records | ISO 27001 A.5, A.9, A.12 | Audit logging, retention | Provider | Audit logs, reports | Compliant |
| Vendor Management | ISO 27001 A.5.19 | Third-party risk | Provider | Subprocessor list, DD | Compliant |
| Payment Terms | Local commercial law | Contract terms | Customer/Provider | Invoices, approvals | Compliant |

# Data Protection and Privacy

## 17. Roles and Processing
17.1 Customer acts as Controller; Provider acts as Processor for Personal Data processed under the Services.  
17.2 Processing shall be limited to the purposes of security monitoring, incident response, and related support.

## 18. Data Processing Agreement (DPA)
18.1 Parties will execute a DPA consistent with GDPR Art. 28 and applicable laws.  
18.2 Provider will implement appropriate technical and organizational measures (TOMs) including encryption, access control, and logging.

This Legal Terms and Compliance section (Agreement) governs the provision of cybersecurity and related services (Services) by the vendor (Vendor) to the procuring entity (Customer), as identified in the applicable Order Form, Statement of Work (SOW), or Purchase Order (collectively, Ordering Documents).

1.3 Order of Precedence. In case of conflict: (1) DPA or data protection-specific addendum; (2) main body of this Agreement; (3) SOW; (4) Order Form; (5) Vendor security and support policies; (6) Customer’s RFP, to the extent incorporated.  
1.4 Stakeholders. The parties acknowledge the following Customer stakeholders for governance and escalations: CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal Department, and Procurement Team.

2.5 Customer Responsibilities. Customer will provide timely access to systems, logs, endpoints, cloud environments, and personnel; designate an engagement owner; and maintain internet connectivity and infrastructure required for SIEM/SOC integration.

## 3. Term, Renewal, and Suspension
3.1 Term. The Agreement term is as set forth in the Ordering Documents.

5.1 Acceptance Testing. For each milestone or Deliverable, Customer will have 10 business days (or as specified in the SOW) to validate against acceptance criteria.

## 6. Service Levels, Support, and Reporting
