| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Reporting Frequency | Service Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOC Monitoring Coverage | 24/7/365 continuous monitoring | Availability of SOC staff and monitoring systems | Monthly | 2% of monthly fee for each month coverage is not maintained (cap 10%) |
| SIEM Onboarding | Initial ingestion and baseline use-cases live within 30 days of project start (unless otherwise agreed) | Project plan milestones | Bi-weekly until completion | 2% of SIEM setup fee per week of delay beyond 2-week grace (cap 10%) |
| P1 Incident Response Time | Acknowledge and initiate triage within 1 hour, 24/7 | Time from P1 alert generation to initial triage start | Monthly | 5% of monthly fee for each P1 breach of target (cap 20%) |
| P2 Incident Response Time | Acknowledge within 2 hours; triage within 4 hours, 24/7 | Ticket timestamps | Monthly | 2% of monthly fee per breach (cap 10%) |
| P3 Response Time | Acknowledge within 8 business hours | Ticket timestamps | Monthly | 1% of monthly fee per 5 breaches (cap 5%) |
| Incident Notification to Customer | For confirmed material security incidents: notify Customer within 4 hours of confirmation | Incident management system logs | Monthly | 2% of monthly fee per breach (cap 10%) |
| Monthly Executive Reporting | Deliver by 10th business day of following month | Report delivery record | Monthly | 1% of monthly fee per late report (cap 5%) |
| Platform Uptime (Managed SIEM, if hosted by Vendor) | 99.9% monthly | Uptime monitoring excluding planned maintenance | Monthly | 5% of monthly platform fee for each 0.1% below target (cap 20%) |

Notes: Credits are not cumulative beyond the cap listed per metric and an overall cap of 20% of the monthly fees for the affected month.

## 7. Information Security, Privacy, and Data Protection
7.1 Security Program. Vendor will maintain a written information security program aligned to ISO/IEC 27001 (certification required and maintained), incorporating risk management, asset management, access control, cryptography, operations security, communications security, system acquisition/development, supplier relationships, incident management, business continuity, and compliance.  
7.2 Certifications and Audits. Upon request annually, Vendor will provide evidence of current ISO/IEC 27001 certification and SOC 2 Type II or equivalent independent assurance (if applicable), including management responses to findings.  
7.3 Technical and Organizational Measures (TOMs).  
7.3.1 Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for Customer Data.  
7.3.2 Access Control: Role-based access, MFA for privileged access, least privilege, quarterly access reviews.  
7.3.3 Logging and Monitoring: Centralized logging, tamper detection, retention in accordance with SOW; integrity controls.  
7.3.4 Vulnerability Management: Monthly vulnerability scans; critical patches within 7 days; high within 14 days unless risk-accepted by Customer.  
7.3.5 Endpoint and Network Security: EDR where in scope; network segmentation; secure bastion access.  
7.3.6 Secure Development: For any code, follow secure SDLC, code reviews, and dependency scanning.  
7.4 Data Minimization and Retention. Vendor will only process Customer Data necessary for the Services. Retain operational data per SOW; upon termination, delete or return Customer Data within 30 days and certify deletion within 45 days, subject to legal holds.  
7.5 Data Transfers. Cross-border transfers will rely on approved transfer mechanisms (e.g., EU SCCs, UK IDTA/Addendum) and supplementary measures, as applicable.  
7.6 Subprocessors. Vendor may use subprocessors subject to due diligence, written contracts with equivalent protections, and Customer’s right to receive notice of changes and object on reasonable security grounds.  
7.7 Breach Notification. Vendor will notify Customer without undue delay and no later than 4 hours after confirming a material Information Security Incident impacting Customer Data, and provide timely updates, forensic details, containment actions, and remediation plans.  
7.8 Privacy Compliance. Vendor will comply with applicable Data Protection Laws, including executing a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) where Vendor acts as a processor.  
7.9 Customer Instructions. Vendor will process Personal Data solely on documented instructions from Customer, including with respect to international transfers.  
7.10 Data Subject Requests. Vendor will assist Customer with data subject access, correction, deletion, and portability requests, and privacy impact assessments, as applicable.  
7.11 Audit Rights. Upon reasonable notice, Customer may conduct (or have a third party conduct) security audits no more than annually or after a material incident, subject to confidentiality and operational safeguards.  
7.12 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery. Vendor maintains BCDR plans tested at least annually; Recovery Time Objective (RTO) ≤ 4 hours and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) ≤ 1 hour for managed SIEM platform elements, unless otherwise set in the SOW.

## 8. Intellectual Property and Licensing
8.1 Background IP. Each party retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property and anything developed independently of this Agreement.  
8.2 Deliverable IP.  
8.2.1 Customer-Funded Deliverables: Subject to payment, Vendor grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, transferable (to affiliates) license to use, modify, and reproduce Deliverables for Customer’s internal business and security purposes.  
8.2.2 Vendor Tools and Templates: Vendor retains ownership of its methodologies, frameworks, playbooks, and tools; Vendor grants Customer a non-exclusive, perpetual license to use embedded Vendor materials as part of the Deliverables for internal purposes.  
8.3 Third-Party Materials. Third-party software and content are subject to their respective licenses; Vendor will identify any such materials in the SOW.  
8.4 Open-Source Compliance. Vendor will comply with applicable open-source licenses and, on request, provide a bill of materials for components embedded in deliverables.  
8.5 IP Indemnity. Vendor will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe IP rights, and will provide remedies (procure rights, modify, or replace). If not feasible, Customer may terminate the affected Services with a pro-rata refund. Exclusions apply for Customer modifications or combinations not provided by Vendor.

## 9. Confidentiality
9.1 Obligations. The receiving party will protect the disclosing party’s Confidential Information with at least the same care used to protect its own similar information, and not less than a reasonable standard of care.  
9.2 Permitted Disclosures. On a need-to-know basis to employees, contractors, advisors under confidentiality obligations, or as required by law (with notice where legally permitted).  
9.3 Duration. Confidentiality obligations survive for five (5) years after disclosure; trade secrets survive as long as they remain trade secrets.

## 10. Regulatory and Standards Compliance
10.1 ISO/IEC 27001. Vendor shall maintain ISO 27001 certification throughout the term (mandatory RFP requirement).  
10.2 Cybersecurity Frameworks. Services will align with NIST CSF and CIS Controls as appropriate to Customer environments.  
10.3 Sectoral Laws. Where applicable, Vendor will comply with sectoral regulations (e.g., HIPAA/HITECH for PHI, GLBA, PCI DSS for card data; defense or critical infrastructure requirements), as specified in the SOW.  
10.4 Export Controls and Sanctions. The parties will comply with applicable export, re-export, and sanctions laws.  
10.5 Anti-bribery/Corruption. The parties will comply with anti-corruption laws (e.g., FCPA, UK Bribery Act).  
10.6 Accessibility and Recordkeeping. Where applicable, Vendor will support reasonable accessibility and recordkeeping requirements and cooperate with regulatory inquiries.

## 11. Audit, Assessments, and Reporting
11.1 Compliance Evidence. Vendor will furnish ISO/IEC 27001 certificate, SoA, SOC 2 report (if applicable), penetration test executive summary, and remediation plans upon request.  
11.2 Onsite/Remote Assessments. Customer may perform assessments on 30 days’ notice, not more than annually, or after a material incident, subject to reasonable time, place, and manner.  
11.3 Remediation. Vendor will promptly address high-risk findings according to mutually agreed timelines.  
11.4 Log Retention. SIEM log retention periods will be defined in the SOW; typical baseline is 365 days online, 18 months archive, unless otherwise specified.

## 12. Changes, Subcontracting, and Personnel
12.1 Change Control. Material changes to scope or SLAs require a mutually executed change order.  
12.2 Subcontractors. Vendor remains responsible for subcontractors’ performance and compliance; use of new subcontractors providing material portions of Services requires prior written notice and Customer’s reasonable objection right.  
12.3 Key Personnel. Identify key roles in the SOW; replacements require equivalent qualifications and prior notice.  
12.4 Background Checks. Vendor will ensure personnel with access to Customer Data pass background checks consistent with applicable laws.

## 13. Liability, Indemnities, and Insurance
13.1 Limitation of Liability.  
13.1.1 Cap. Each party’s aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement will not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer for the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to liability.  
13.1.2 Exclusions from Cap. The above cap does not apply to: (a) IP infringement indemnity; (b) breach of confidentiality; (c) willful misconduct or gross negligence; (d) unpaid fees; (e) data protection breach directly caused by a party’s failure to implement agreed TOMs. For these, the cap is two (2) times the 12-month fees.  
13.1.3 Exclusion of Damages. Neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, punitive, or consequential damages, or lost profits, arising from this Agreement, to the maximum extent permitted by law.  
13.2 Mutual Indemnity. Each party will defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the other against third-party claims arising from: (a) bodily injury or tangible property damage caused by its negligence; (b) its violation of law; and (c) its breach of this Agreement.  
13.3 Insurance. Vendor will maintain, at its expense:  
13.3.1 Commercial General Liability: $2,000,000 aggregate.  
13.3.2 Professional Liability/Technology E&O (including Cyber): $5,000,000 aggregate.  
13.3.3 Workers’ Compensation and Employer’s Liability: statutory and $1,000,000, respectively.  
13.3.4 Evidence of insurance provided upon request; 30 days’ notice of material changes or cancellation where available.

## 14. Termination and Exit Management
14.1 Termination for Cause. Either party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days of written notice (10 days for non-payment).  
14.2 Termination for Convenience. Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days’ written notice; Customer will pay for Services performed through the effective date and non-cancellable commitments.  
14.3 Insolvency. Either party may terminate if the other becomes insolvent or enters bankruptcy proceedings not dismissed within 60 days.  
14.4 Effect of Termination.  
14.4.1 Transition Assistance. For up to 60 days (or as specified in SOW), Vendor will provide termination assistance at time-and-materials rates to ensure orderly transition, including runbook handover, configuration exports, and knowledge transfer.  
14.4.2 Data Return/Deletion. Vendor will return Customer Data in a mutually agreed, industry-standard format and delete copies per Section 7.4.  
14.4.3 Retention Release. Upon project completion and acceptance, any 10% retention is released in accordance with Section 4.4.  
14.5 Survival. Sections relating to fees, confidentiality, IP, data protection, liability, indemnity, dispute resolution, and audit survive termination.

## 15. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
15.1 Executive Escalation. Disputes will first be escalated to the parties’ designated stakeholders, including Customer’s CISO and IT Operations Manager, for good-faith resolution within 10 business days.  
15.2 Mediation. If unresolved, the parties will participate in non-binding mediation within 30 days.  
15.3 Arbitration/Courts. Failing mediation, disputes will be finally resolved by arbitration under the rules specified in the Ordering Documents (e.g., AAA or ICC), or in the courts of the agreed venue, each party submitting to the chosen forum’s jurisdiction.  
15.4 Governing Law. As specified in the Ordering Documents, excluding conflict of law principles.

## 16. Notices and Governance
16.1 Notices. Legal notices must be in writing and delivered by email with confirmation, courier, or certified mail to the contacts in the Ordering Documents, with copies to Customer Legal Department and Procurement Team.  
16.2 Governance Cadence.  
16.2.1 Weekly/Twice-Monthly Operations Review: SOC leads and Customer IT Operations Manager.  
16.2.2 Monthly Performance Review: KPIs, SLA performance, open risks, and action items.  
16.2.3 Quarterly Executive Review: CISO, Compliance Officer, Vendor executive sponsor—roadmap, risk posture, and program improvements.  
16.3 RACI. A RACI or equivalent governance matrix will be maintained and updated as part of the SOW.

## 17. Miscellaneous
17.1 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other’s consent, except to affiliates or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee assumes all obligations.  
17.2 Force Majeure. Neither party is liable for failure to perform due to events beyond reasonable control, provided it uses diligent efforts to mitigate and resumes performance promptly.  
17.3 Publicity. Press releases or public use of the other party’s name or marks require prior written consent.  
17.4 Severability; Waiver. If any provision is unenforceable, the remainder remains in effect. No waiver is effective unless in writing.  
17.5 Entire Agreement; Amendments. This Agreement and Scope Documents constitute the entire agreement. Amendments must be in writing and executed by authorized representatives.

# Quality Assurance and Testing Plan

## Objectives and Scope
- Establish a measurable, auditable QA framework ensuring solution quality, security, and compliance throughout the lifecycle.
- Validate delivery of 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation, and incident response within 1 hour.
- Demonstrate ISO 27001 compliance with verifiable controls, evidence, and audit readiness.
- Assure performance, availability, and usability SLAs through systematic testing, monitoring validation, and KPIs.
- Enable transparent defect management, risk mitigation, and stakeholder-driven acceptance.

## Governance, Standards, and Stakeholders

### Applicable Standards and Frameworks
- ISO/IEC 27001:2013/2022 – Information Security Management System (controls around logging, monitoring, incident management, change management, supplier management).
- ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119 – Software testing processes and documentation.
- NIST SP 800-61 – Computer Security Incident Handling Guide.
- NIST SP 800-53 / CIS Controls – Security control testing baseline.
- OWASP ASVS/Top 10 – Application security assurance.
- ITIL v4 – Service management processes (Change, Incident, Problem).

### Stakeholder Roles and Approvals
| Role | Responsibilities | QA Approvals |
|---|---|---|
| CISO | Security risk ownership, policy alignment, incident response governance | Security Test Plan, Pen Test Results, ISO 27001 Control Evidence |
| IT Operations Manager | Operations readiness, monitoring, SIEM operations | Performance Test Report, DR/Failover Tests, Runbooks |
| Compliance Officer | Regulatory and ISO 27001 conformance | Compliance Matrix, Audit Evidence Pack, Exceptions Register |
| Legal Department | Contractual compliance, data processing, privacy | Data Protection Impact Assessment, Third-Party Risk Evidence |
| Procurement Team | Milestone validation, payment triggers | Acceptance Certificates against milestones and SLAs |
| QA Lead (Vendor) | QA strategy, execution, reporting | Test Strategy, Test Summary Reports, Go/No-Go Recommendations |

# Testing Strategy and Methodology

## Risk-Based, Shift-Left, Automation-First Strategy
1. Prioritize testing by business risk: safety, security, compliance, availability, financial impact.
2. Apply shift-left practices: early static analysis, threat modeling, and unit/integration tests in CI.
3. Maximize automation for regression, API, SIEM content validation, and performance baselines.
4. Continuously validate monitoring/alerting and incident workflows in non-business hours to ensure 24/7 readiness.
5. Enforce quality gates across environments with measurable thresholds for entry/exit.

## Test Methodologies
1. Unit Testing: Component-level functional validation by developers in CI.
2. Integration Testing: Interface contracts, log ingestion pipelines, and data mappings.
3. System Testing: End-to-end SIEM and SOC workflows, correlation rules, and dashboards.
4. Regression Testing: Automated suites guarding against functional and security regressions.
5. Performance/Load/Stress Testing: Throughput, concurrency, latency, and resilience under fault conditions.
6. Security Testing: SAST, SCA, DAST, configuration reviews, penetration testing, and SIEM content efficacy.
7. Operability Testing: Monitoring validation, alert fidelity, escalation routing, on-call runbooks.
8. Disaster Recovery/Failover Testing: Backup, restore, DR runbooks, RTO/RPO validation.
9. Data Migration/Quality Testing: Source-to-destination mapping, completeness, timeliness, and retention policies.
10. UAT: Stakeholder validation against business workflows and acceptance criteria.

# Quality Assurance Processes

## SDLC Quality Gates
1. Requirements Gate: Signed-off requirements, risk assessment, testability review, traceability established.
2. Design Gate: Threat model completed, security design review, logging/monitoring design reviewed.
3. Build Gate: SAST/SCA pass, unit test coverage ≥ 80%, no critical/high vulnerabilities open.
4. Test Gate: Functional pass ≥ 95%, zero open critical defects, performance baselines met.
5. Release Gate: Go/No-Go based on exit criteria, stakeholder approvals, rollback plan verified.
6. Operations Gate: Monitoring configured, SOPs/runbooks approved, UAT sign-off, DR readiness.

## Change and Configuration Control
1. All changes tracked via change management with risk classification and rollback plan.
2. Configuration baselined and versioned; infrastructure as code peer-reviewed and tested.
3. Emergency changes include post-implementation review and regression risk assessment.

## Peer Reviews and Static Analysis
1. Mandatory peer reviews with secure coding checklist.
2. Automated SAST/SCA thresholds: no critical/high vulnerabilities at release; medium mitigated within SLA.

## Test Data and Environments
1. Use synthetic or de-identified data; comply with privacy and retention requirements.
2. Environment parity with production; configuration drift monitored and corrected prior to release.

## Traceability
1. Bi-directional traceability between requirements, risks, tests, defects, and releases maintained in the test management system.

# Test Planning and Execution

## Test Plan Overview
| Test Phase | Objectives | Entry Criteria | Exit Criteria | Owner | Tools | Schedule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Integration | Validate interfaces, ingestion, APIs | Design sign-off, integration specs complete | 95% pass rate, no critical defects | QA Lead | Postman, k6 | Sprint N+1 |
| System | Validate end-to-end workflows | Integration exit met | 95% pass, core use cases pass | QA Lead | Selenium, Robot, Splunk/QRadar | Sprint N+2 |
| Performance | Throughput/latency under load | System entry met, stable build | Meets SLOs, no critical perf defects | Perf Eng. | JMeter, Grafana, APM | Sprint N+2 |
| Security | Vulnerability/pen testing, SIEM content | System stability, threat model | No critical/high vulns; SIEM detections ≥ 95% | Sec Eng. | SAST/SCA, ZAP/Burp, Nessus | Sprint N+3 |
| UAT | Business acceptance | System exit met, UAT plan signed | UAT pass ≥ 95%, all P1 issues resolved | Business | Test Mgmt Tool | Sprint N+3 |
| DR/Failover | RTO/RPO, continuity | Ops runbooks drafted | RTO ≤ target, RPO ≤ target, evidence captured | IT Ops | DR tools, Backups | Pre-Go-Live |

## Test Environments
| Environment | Purpose | Key Configurations | Security Controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEV | Developer tests | Feature flags on, mock services | Least privilege, SAST/SCA |
| TEST | QA functional/system | Representative data, SIEM dev stack | Segmented network, DAST |
| PERF | Performance testing | Scaled infra, telemetry on | APM, synthetic monitoring |
| UAT | Business sign-off | Production-like config | Access control for stakeholders |
| DR | Recovery validation | Alternate region/site | Backup/restore controls |

# Test Cases and Procedures (Samples)

## Sample Functional Test Cases
| ID | Title | Pre-Conditions | Steps | Expected Results | Acceptance Criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-SIEM-001 | Log Ingestion from Firewall | SIEM up; firewall sending logs | 1. Generate traffic 2. Verify logs received 3. Check parsing | Logs visible with correct fields; no drops | ≥ 99% log parse success; latency ≤ 60s |
| TC-ALERT-004 | High-Severity Alert Correlation | Use test dataset | 1. Trigger known IOC 2. Verify rule fires 3. Notify on-call | Alert created, ticket opened, on-call paged | Detection within 5 min; ticket within 10 min |
| TC-IR-007 | Incident Escalation | On-call roster active | 1. Trigger P1 alert 2. Verify L1 triage 3. Escalate L2 | L1 ack ≤ 5 min; L2 engaged ≤ 15 min | End-to-end response ≤ 60 min |

# Acceptance Criteria and Testing Procedures

## SOC Monitoring and SIEM

### Acceptance Criteria
1. 24/7 monitoring coverage with documented on-call rota and escalation paths.
2. Log sources onboarded: ≥ 95% of in-scope sources with health checks and alerting on ingestion failures.
3. SIEM parsing accuracy: ≥ 99% field extraction for critical sources; parsing errors auto-ticketed within 15 minutes.
4. Correlation rules: ≥ 95% detection rate for defined use cases with false positive rate ≤ 5% during steady state.
5. Alert pipeline latency: ≤ 5 minutes from event to alert for P1 use cases.
6. SIEM uptime: ≥ 99.9% monthly for ingestion and analysis pipeline.

### Testing Procedures
1. Validate on-call schedules and escalation runbooks; perform after-hours paging tests.
2. Simulate log bursts and source failures; confirm ingestion alerts and auto-remediation.
3. Run sample logs to verify parsers and field mappings; assess parsing error handling.
4. Execute rule library with synthetic IOCs and TTPs; measure detection rate and false positives.
5. Measure end-to-end alert latency via timestamp correlation across components.
6. Monitor SIEM service health for 14-day steady-state; review uptime and backlog metrics.

## Incident Response (1-Hour SLA)

### Acceptance Criteria
1. Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) for P1: ≤ 10 minutes.
2. Mean Time to Acknowledge (MTTA) for P1: ≤ 5 minutes.
3. Mean Time to Respond/Contain (MTTR) for P1: ≤ 60 minutes from alert creation.
4. Incident runbook coverage: 100% for top 10 incident types; owners assigned.
5. Post-incident review within 48 hours; corrective actions tracked to closure.

### Testing Procedures
1. Conduct timed tabletop exercises for top incident types; record MTTD/MTTA/MTTR.
2. Trigger live-fire simulations off-hours; measure paging reliability and escalation.
3. Validate SOAR playbooks and manual fallbacks; verify containment steps.
4. Review PIR documentation and action tracking in the ITSM tool.
5. Audit evidence: timestamps, call logs, tickets, and containment artifacts.

## ISO 27001 Compliance

### Acceptance Criteria
1. Evidence pack mapped to ISO 27001 Annex A controls for logging, monitoring, incident management, access control, and supplier management.
2. Risk assessment and Statement of Applicability approved by Compliance Officer.
3. Control effectiveness tested with ≥ 95% pass rate; gaps tracked with remediation plans and due dates.
4. Annual internal audit plan defined and initial cycle executed prior to go-live.

### Testing Procedures
1. Map requirements to ISO 27001 controls; build control-test-evidence matrix.
2. Execute control testing: access reviews, logging retention, monitoring, incident records.
3. Validate supplier controls and data processing agreements with Legal.
4. Compile audit evidence: policies, procedures, logs, tickets, training records.

## Performance and Load

### Acceptance Criteria
1. Ingestion throughput: Meet or exceed peak expected EPS/TPS with 30% headroom.
2. Query performance: 95th percentile query response ≤ 2 seconds for standard dashboards.
3. Alert processing latency: ≤ 5 minutes at peak load.
4. Resource utilization at peak: CPU ≤ 70%, memory ≤ 75%, sustained; no throttling.

### Testing Procedures
1. Develop workload models for peak/seasonal loads; include burst tests.
2. Execute baseline, load, stress, and soak tests (≥ 8 hours).
3. Measure latency, throughput, saturation; analyze bottlenecks with APM.
4. Repeat after tuning; confirm stability and no error budget regression.

## Security Testing and Compliance

### Acceptance Criteria
1. No open critical/high vulnerabilities at release; medium resolved within 30 days.
2. Penetration test findings: all critical/high remediated and retested.
3. Configuration benchmarks (CIS/NIST) ≥ 95% compliance for in-scope systems.
4. SIEM content validates top MITRE ATT&CK techniques relevant to environment.

### Testing Procedures
1. Run SAST/SCA on each commit; block on policy violations.
2. Conduct authenticated DAST and configuration scans; verify remediation.
3. Perform internal/external penetration testing; validate fixes.
4. Test SIEM detection content against ATT&CK simulations; document coverage.

## User Acceptance Testing (UAT)

### Acceptance Criteria
1. UAT pass rate ≥ 95% of planned test cases; no open P1/P2 issues at sign-off.
2. Business workflows validated by CISO, IT Ops, and Compliance Officer.
3. Training materials and runbooks approved; knowledge transfer completed.

### Testing Procedures
1. Execute UAT script set with stakeholder observers; record results in test tool.
2. Triage defects; retest fixes; capture sign-offs.
3. Validate reporting dashboards and operational handover artifacts.

# Quality Metrics and KPIs

## KPI Targets
- Test case pass rate: ≥ 95% before release.
- Requirements coverage: 100% traceability to tests.
- Defect density: ≤ 0.5 per KLOC in system test; escape rate ≤ 2% to production.
- Automation coverage: ≥ 70% of regression test cases automated.
- MTTD (P1): ≤ 10 minutes; MTTA (P1): ≤ 5 minutes; MTTR (P1): ≤ 60 minutes.
- SIEM detection efficacy: ≥ 95% for defined use cases; false positive rate ≤ 5%.
- Ingestion uptime: ≥ 99.9%; Alert latency: ≤ 5 minutes.
- Vulnerability SLA compliance: 100% for critical/high by release.

## Quality Metrics Matrix
| Metric | Definition | Target | Frequency | Data Source | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Requirements Coverage | % requirements mapped to tests | 100% | Weekly | Test Mgmt | QA Lead |
| Test Pass Rate | % passed test cases | ≥ 95% | Per Cycle | Test Mgmt | QA Lead |
| Defect Density | Defects/KLOC | ≤ 0.5 | Per Release | Repo, Test Mgmt | QA Lead |
| Escape Rate | Prod defects/Total defects | ≤ 2% | Monthly | ITSM, Test Mgmt | QA Lead |
| Automation Coverage | % automated regression | ≥ 70% | Bi-Weekly | CI Pipelines | QA Lead |
| MTTD/MTTA/MTTR | Incident response times (P1) | 10/5/60 min | Monthly | SIEM, ITSM, Pager | CISO |
| SIEM Detection Rate | % detected test TTPs | ≥ 95% | Monthly | SIEM Reports | Sec Eng. |
| False Positive Rate | False alerts / total alerts | ≤ 5% | Monthly | SIEM | Sec Eng. |
| Ingestion Uptime | Availability of pipelines | ≥ 99.9% | Monthly | Uptime Mon | IT Ops |
| Perf 95p Latency | Query/alert latency | ≤ Targets | Per Test | APM, JMeter | Perf Eng. |
| Vuln SLA Compliance | % remediated within SLA | 100% | Weekly | SAST/SCA, DAST | Sec Eng. |

# Bug Tracking and Resolution Process

## Defect Lifecycle
1. Log: Create defect with repro steps, environment, logs, and severity/priority.
2. Triage: Daily triage with QA, Dev, Sec Eng., and IT Ops to set priority and owner.
3. Fix: Implement fix with peer review and unit tests.
4. Verify: QA retest and regression; link to requirements.
5. Close: Confirm in production if applicable; update knowledge base.
6. Report: Weekly defect trends and SLA adherence shared with stakeholders.

## Severity, Priority, and SLAs
| Severity | Description | Response SLA | Resolution SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical (P1) | Outage/security breach; no workaround | 1 hour | 24 hours |
| High (P2) | Major functionality impaired | 4 hours | 3 business days |
| Medium (P3) | Limited impact; workaround exists | 1 business day | 10 business days |
| Low (P4) | Minor issue; cosmetic | 2 business days | Next release |

# Performance and Load Testing Approach

## Workload Modeling
1. Derive EPS/TPS from historical/forecasted volumes; include burst of +50% for 30 minutes.
2. Define user journeys: dashboard queries, alert triage, incident updates.
3. Establish SLOs for each path with P50/P95/P99 targets.

## Execution
1. Baseline test at steady load; collect APM metrics and GC stats.
2. Step-load to peak + headroom; monitor saturation, queues, and latency.
3. Stress, spike, and soak (≥ 8 hours) to assess stability and leaks.
4. Fault-injection (e.g., source outage, node failure); validate resiliency and auto-recovery.

## Reporting
1. Provide comparative charts vs. SLOs; highlight bottlenecks and optimizations.
2. Re-test after tuning; confirm improvements and no regressions.

# Security Testing and Compliance

## Security Test Suite
1. Threat Modeling: Identify high-risk assets and attack paths; map to ATT&CK.
2. SAST/SCA: Enforce policies with build breakers on critical/high.
3. DAST: Authenticated scans against staging; verify findings.
4. Penetration Testing: Internal/external; scope includes SIEM, management interfaces, and APIs.
5. Configuration and Hardening: Validate CIS/NIST baselines; remediate drift.
6. SIEM Content Validation: Simulate TTPs; measure detection time and accuracy.
7. Incident Response Drills: Tabletop and live-fire with 24/7 coverage validation.

## ISO 27001 Control Mapping (Excerpt)
| Control | Test | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A.8.16 Monitoring Activities | Review monitoring scope and dashboards | SIEM dashboards, coverage report |
| A.8.15 Logging | Verify log sources, retention, integrity | Log source inventory, WORM storage proof |
| A.5.24 Information Security Incident Mgmt | Validate IR plan and records | IR policy, tickets, PIRs |
| A.5.23 Information Security in Dev | Check SAST/SCA, code reviews | CI logs, review checklists |
| A.5.19 Access Control | Review RBAC, least privilege | Access reviews, role matrices |

# User Acceptance Testing (UAT)

## UAT Plan
1. Scope: Business workflows for monitoring, alert triage, incident handling, reporting, and compliance evidence generation.
2. Participants: CISO (security acceptance), IT Operations Manager (operational readiness), Compliance Officer (compliance acceptance), selected SMEs.
3. Entry Criteria: System test exit met; data and environments ready; UAT scripts approved.
4. Exit Criteria: ≥ 95% pass; no P1/P2 open; all documentation/runbooks approved; training completed.

## UAT Execution
1. Conduct orientation and test dry-runs.
2. Execute test scenarios; capture defects and enhancement requests.
3. Re-test fixes; capture sign-offs per stakeholder role.

# Requirements Traceability Matrix (Excerpt)
| Requirement | Source | Test Cases | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24/7 SOC Monitoring | RFP | TC-ALERT-004, TC-OPS-010 | On-call tests, Pager logs | Planned |
| SIEM Implementation | RFP | TC-SIEM-001, TC-SIEM-020 | Parser reports, Dashboards | In Progress |
| 1-Hour Incident Response | RFP | TC-IR-007, TC-IR-012 | ITSM timestamps, Call logs | Planned |
| ISO 27001 Compliance | RFP | TC-COMP-001..010 | Control evidence pack | Planned |

# Deliverables, Reporting, and Milestones

## QA Deliverables
- Test Strategy and Detailed Test Plans (functional, performance, security, UAT).
- Requirements Traceability Matrix and Risk Register.
- Test Cases/Scripts and Automation Suites.
- Test Execution Reports and Defect Logs.
- Security Testing Reports (SAST/SCA, DAST, Pen Test) and ISO 27001 Evidence Pack.
- Performance Test Reports with SLO attestation.
- UAT Plan, Results, and Acceptance Certificates.
- Operations Runbooks, DR Plans, and Handover Package.

## Reporting Cadence
- Daily: Test progress and defect triage updates.
- Weekly: KPI dashboard and risk/issue log to stakeholders.
- Per Phase: Entry/Exit criteria assessment and Go/No-Go recommendation.

## Milestones and Payment Alignment
| Milestone | Description | Acceptance Evidence | Payment Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1: Test Strategy Approved | Governance, plans, and RTM baselined | Signed Test Strategy, RTM | Milestone payment per contract |
| M2: System & Security Test Exit | Functional/security exit criteria met | Test Summary, No Critical/High vulns | Milestone payment; Net 30 |
| M3: Performance Exit | SLOs met with headroom | Perf Report, SLO attestation | Milestone payment; Net 30 |
| M4: UAT Sign-Off | Business acceptance achieved | UAT Certificate signed by CISO, IT Ops, Compliance | Milestone payment; Net 30 |
| M5: Go-Live & DR Validation | Production readiness and DR tested | DR Report, Monitoring evidence | Release of 10% retention at completion |

# Risk Management and Mitigation
- Incomplete log source onboarding: Maintain onboarding checklist, automatic health alerts, and weekly coverage reviews.
- Alert fatigue/false positives: Iterative tuning with labeled datasets; target ≤ 5% FPR; stakeholder feedback loops.
- Off-hours response gaps: Monthly after-hours drills; on-call rota audits; automated paging redundancy.
- Performance regressions: Performance tests integrated into CI; block releases on SLO breaches.
- Compliance gaps: Early internal audit and remediation plan; evidence automation where possible.

# Tools and Platforms (Representative)
- Test Management: Azure DevOps Test Plans / Jira + Xray.
- CI/CD: GitLab CI / GitHub Actions.
- Functional/API: Postman, Karate, Robot Framework.
- Performance: JMeter, k6, Grafana, InfluxDB.
- Security: SAST/SCA (e.g., SonarQube, Dependabot), DAST (OWASP ZAP/Burp), Vuln Scanners (Nessus).
- Monitoring/SIEM: Splunk/QRadar/Elastic; SOAR for playbooks; PagerDuty/Opsgenie for on-call.
- APM/Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry.

# Quality Gates and Go/No-Go Criteria

## Entry Criteria (per Test Phase)
1. Approved requirements and test plans.
2. Stable build and environment availability.
3. Test data ready and access provisioned.

## Exit Criteria (Release)
1. Functional pass ≥ 95%; no open P1/P2 defects.
2. Performance SLOs met with ≥ 30% capacity headroom.
3. Security: no open critical/high vulnerabilities; pen test retest passed.
4. Compliance: ISO 27001 evidence pack approved by Compliance Officer.
5. UAT: Signed acceptance by CISO, IT Ops Manager, and Compliance Officer.
6. Operations: 24/7 on-call validated; runbooks approved; DR test passed.

This QA and Testing Plan is designed to be comprehensive, measurable, aligned with ISO 27001 and industry best practices, and tailored to the RFP requirements for 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation, and 1-hour incident response SLAs.

# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Parties, Scope, and Order of Precedence
1. Parties. This Agreement is entered into by and between [Customer Legal Entity] (“Customer”) and [Provider Legal Entity] (“Provider”), each a “Party” and together the “Parties.”
2. Scope. Provider will deliver managed cybersecurity services, including 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) monitoring, Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) implementation and operations, and incident response services as further defined in the Statement(s) of Work (“SOW”).
3. Order of Precedence. In the event of conflict: (1) an executed Change Order (if expressly superseding a specified term) prevails over (2) the applicable SOW, which prevails over (3) this Master Agreement, which prevails over (4) any incorporated policies or schedules.

## 2. Definitions
1. “Confidential Information” means all non-public information disclosed by a Party that is marked or reasonably understood to be confidential, including security architecture and incident data.
2. “Customer Data” means data provided by or collected on behalf of Customer, including personal data and security telemetry.
3. “Deliverables” means all reports, configurations, runbooks, dashboards, integrations, and other work product identified in the SOW.
4. “Force Majeure Event” means events beyond a Party’s reasonable control, including natural disasters, acts of war, terrorism, strikes (excluding those affecting a Party’s own personnel only), government actions, or widespread internet outages.
5. “Personal Data” means information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
6. “Service Credits” means fee reductions awarded for verified Service Level Agreement (SLA) failures as defined herein.

## 3. Term and Termination
1. Term. The Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for the initial term stated in the SOW, renewing per the SOW unless either Party gives at least 60 days’ notice of non-renewal.
2. Termination for Convenience. Either Party may terminate any SOW for convenience on 30 days’ prior written notice after the initial term, unless otherwise stated in the SOW.
3. Termination for Cause. Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW immediately upon written notice if the other Party: (a) materially breaches and fails to cure within 30 days of receipt of notice; or (b) becomes insolvent, enters bankruptcy, or ceases business.
4. Termination for Repeated SLA Failures. Customer may terminate the affected services on 30 days’ notice if Provider (a) incurs three or more Critical SLA breaches in any rolling 90-day period, or (b) fails to implement an agreed corrective action plan within 30 days.
5. Termination Assistance. Upon expiration or termination, Provider will: (a) continue providing services for up to 90 days (transition period) at the then-current rates to facilitate orderly transition; (b) transfer Customer Data and Deliverables in a mutually agreed format; and (c) provide reasonable knowledge transfer and documentation.

## 4. Governance and Stakeholders
1. Stakeholder Roles. Governance will include participation by Customer’s CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal Department, and Procurement Team (collectively, “Customer Stakeholders”). Provider will designate a Service Delivery Manager and Security Lead.
2. Steering Committee. A joint committee will meet at least quarterly to review security posture, SLAs, risk, compliance, and roadmap.
3. Escalation. Operational issues escalate from Provider’s Service Delivery Manager to Customer’s IT Operations Manager and CISO; contractual issues escalate to Legal and Procurement.

## 5. Services, Acceptance, and Change Control
1. Services. Provider will deliver 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation and operations, and incident response in accordance with the SOW and SLAs.
2. Acceptance. Deliverables are deemed accepted upon the earlier of (a) Customer’s written acceptance, or (b) 10 business days after delivery with no written rejection identifying material non-conformities. Provider will remedy any non-conformity within a reasonable period and resubmit for acceptance.
3. Change Control. Changes to scope, timelines, or costs require a written Change Order signed by both Parties. Emergency changes necessary to mitigate active threats may proceed immediately, with a follow-up Change Order within 5 business days.

## 6. Payment Terms, Taxes, and Retention
1. Fees. Fees are as stated in the SOW and may include one-time implementation fees and recurring service fees.
2. Invoicing and Payment. Invoices will be issued per milestone or monthly in arrears for managed services. Payment terms are Net 30 days after invoice approval. Performance milestones must be met for payment. A 10% retention will be withheld until project completion, as defined in the SOW acceptance criteria.
3. Disputed Amounts. Customer will pay undisputed amounts when due and notify Provider of any dispute within 10 business days; the Parties will cooperate to resolve disputes promptly.
4. Taxes. Fees exclude taxes. Customer is responsible for applicable taxes (excluding taxes based on Provider’s net income). Withholding tax gross-up will not apply unless required by law, in which case the Parties will cooperate to minimize tax.
5. Expenses. Pre-approved, reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses will be reimbursed per Customer policy.

## 7. Warranties
1. Services Warranty. Provider warrants that services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by appropriately qualified personnel and in accordance with the SOW, Applicable Law, and ISO 27001 controls.
2. Non-Infringement Warranty. Provider warrants that Deliverables (excluding Customer Materials and Third-Party Materials) will not knowingly infringe third-party intellectual property rights.
3. Malware Warranty. Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts, including industry-standard tools and processes, to avoid introducing malware.
4. Disclaimer. Except as expressly warranted, the services and deliverables are provided “as is.” Provider does not warrant that security incidents will be fully prevented or that all vulnerabilities will be detected.

## 8. Intellectual Property Rights
1. Background IP. Each Party retains all right, title, and interest in and to its pre-existing and independently developed materials, tools, methods, and know-how (“Background IP”).
2. Deliverables. Subject to payment of applicable fees, Customer owns all right, title, and interest in Deliverables specifically developed for Customer under an SOW, excluding Provider Background IP and Third-Party Materials.
3. Provider Materials License. To the extent Deliverables incorporate Provider Background IP, Provider grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use such Background IP as embedded in the Deliverables solely for Customer’s internal business purposes.
4. Third-Party Materials. Third-party software or content is subject to the applicable third-party license. Provider will identify any material third-party dependencies in the SOW.
5. Feedback. Customer grants Provider a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free license to use anonymized feedback to improve Provider’s services without identifying Customer or exposing Customer Data.

## 9. Confidentiality
1. Obligations. The receiving Party will: (a) use Confidential Information solely to perform under this Agreement; (b) restrict disclosure to personnel, affiliates, and subprocessors with a need to know and subject to obligations no less protective than herein; and (c) protect Confidential Information using at least the safeguards used for its own similar information and no less than reasonable care.
2. Exclusions. Confidential Information excludes information that is: (a) public through no breach; (b) known to the receiving Party without confidentiality obligations; (c) independently developed; or (d) rightfully received from a third party without confidentiality obligations.
3. Compelled Disclosure. The receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information when legally compelled, with prompt notice to the disclosing Party (unless prohibited) to allow protective measures.
4. Return/Destruction. Upon request or termination, Confidential Information will be returned or securely destroyed, except for archival copies retained as required by law or standard backup practices, which remain subject to confidentiality.

## 10. Data Protection and Privacy (Data Processing Addendum)
1. Roles. For services involving Personal Data, Customer is the Controller and Provider is the Processor (or sub-processor, as applicable).
2. Instructions. Provider will process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Customer and for the purposes described in the SOW.
3. Compliance. Provider will comply with Applicable Data Protection Laws, including GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, UK GDPR, and other jurisdiction-specific privacy laws, to the extent applicable to the services.
4. Security Measures. Provider will implement appropriate technical and organizational measures aligned to ISO 27001, including: (a) encryption in transit and at rest; (b) access control and MFA; (c) security logging and monitoring; (d) secure software development practices; (e) vulnerability management and timely patching; and (f) employee background checks and security training.
5. Subprocessors. Provider may engage subprocessors subject to prior notice to Customer, written contracts imposing equivalent data protection obligations, and responsibility for subprocessor performance. Customer may object on reasonable grounds relating to data protection risk.
6. International Transfers. Cross-border transfers of Personal Data will comply with applicable transfer mechanisms (e.g., EU SCCs, UK IDTA/Addendum, other approved safeguards). Provider will implement supplementary measures where required.
7. Breach Notification. Provider will notify Customer without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Customer Data. Notification will include the nature of the breach, categories and approximate number of data subjects, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed.
8. Data Subject Requests. Provider will assist Customer in responding to data subject requests and regulatory inquiries, and will promptly notify Customer upon receipt of any such requests directly.
9. Audit and Compliance. Provider will make available relevant records and certifications (e.g., ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 report if available) and allow Customer or its auditor, under confidentiality and upon reasonable notice, to verify compliance no more than annually, or more frequently in response to a verified incident or regulator request.
10. Retention and Deletion. Upon termination or upon instruction, Provider will return or securely delete Customer Personal Data, except to the extent retention is required by law. Deletion will be certified upon request.
11. Privacy by Design. Provider will ensure privacy by design and default, limiting Personal Data to what is necessary for the services.

## 11. Regulatory and Legal Compliance
1. ISO 27001. Provider will maintain an ISO/IEC 27001-compliant Information Security Management System (ISMS). ISO 27001 compliance is mandatory.
2. Security Frameworks. Provider will operate in alignment with NIST CSF and industry best practices relevant to SOC and SIEM operations.
3. Laws and Standards. Provider will comply with Applicable Law, including: (a) anti-bribery and corruption (FCPA, UK Bribery Act); (b) export control and sanctions (EAR, ITAR, OFAC) as applicable; (c) labor and human rights laws; and (d) accessibility standards where applicable.
4. Government or Sector Requirements. If services involve regulated sectors (e.g., public sector, healthcare, financial services), Provider will comply with sector-specific requirements (e.g., HIPAA, PCI DSS) as expressly stated in the SOW.
5. Records and Retention. Provider will maintain accurate records evidencing compliance for at least 7 years or as required by law.

## 12. Security Obligations
1. SOC Operations. Provider will deliver 24/7/365 SOC monitoring, alert triage, threat hunting, and incident response per SLAs.
2. SIEM Implementation. Provider will implement and operate SIEM including log collection, normalization, correlation, use-case development, tuning, and dashboarding.
3. Incident Response. Provider will provide initial response within 1 hour of a qualifying security incident, coordinate containment, eradication, and recovery, and deliver post-incident reports with root cause and lessons learned.
4. Logging and Retention. Provider will maintain logs per SOW (recommended: minimum 365 days hot/warm retention; multi-year cold storage as required by Customer or regulation).
5. Vulnerability and Patch Management. Provider will scan critical assets at least monthly; critical patches applied within 14 days, high within 30 days, unless risk-assessed.
6. Access Management. Least privilege, MFA for administrative access, privileged access monitoring, and timely deprovisioning.
7. Business Continuity and DR. Provider will maintain and test business continuity and disaster recovery plans annually; target RTO ≤ 4 hours, RPO ≤ 1 hour for SOC tooling, unless otherwise specified in the SOW.

## 13. Service Level Agreements (SLAs)

### 13.1 Core Service Metrics
| Metric | Target | Measurement Window | Definition | Service Credit | Exclusions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOC Coverage | 24/7/365 continuous monitoring | Monthly | Continuous staffing and monitoring of designated environments | 5% of monthly fee if any unplanned gap >15 minutes; additional 5% for each additional gap (cap 20%) | Planned maintenance with 7 days’ notice; Force Majeure |
| Incident Response – Initial Acknowledgment (Critical) | ≤ 15 minutes | Per incident | Time from alert creation to Provider acknowledgment | 2% per breach (cap 20%) | Customer-caused delays; third-party outage |
| Incident Response – Initial Action (Critical) | ≤ 1 hour | Per incident | Time from alert creation to containment action or documented plan | 5% per breach (cap 25%) | As above |
| SIEM Availability | ≥ 99.9% uptime | Monthly | Availability of SIEM ingestion, correlation, and dashboarding | 5% if <99.9% and ≥99.5%; 10% if <99.5% (cap 25%) | Planned maintenance (≤4 hrs/month) |
| Alert Triage (High Severity) | ≤ 30 minutes | Monthly (95th percentile) | Time from alert creation to triage disposition | 2% per month breached (cap 15%) | Excessive false positives due to Customer configuration |
| Use Case/Rule Deployment | ≤ 5 business days | Per request | Time to design, test, and deploy mutually agreed detection rule | 1% per day late (cap 10%) | Dependencies on Customer systems |
| Monthly Reporting | By 5th business day | Monthly | Delivery of SLA, KPI, incident and threat intel report | 1% per business day late (cap 10%) | Force Majeure |

### 13.2 Severity Definitions and Response Targets
1. Critical: Active compromise or imminent threat to critical systems or regulated data. Acknowledgment ≤ 15 minutes; initial action ≤ 1 hour; containment target ≤ 4 hours.
2. High: Significant threat with potential lateral movement. Acknowledgment ≤ 30 minutes; initial action ≤ 2 hours; containment target ≤ 8 hours.
3. Medium/Low: Non-critical findings or hygiene tasks. Response per agreed backlog prioritization.

### 13.3 SLA Administration
1. Measurement and Reporting. Provider will provide monthly SLA reports with evidence. Disputes must be raised within 15 days of report issuance.
2. Service Credits. Credits apply to the affected service’s monthly recurring fees, are Customer’s sole monetary remedy for SLA failures, and do not preclude termination rights. Credits are not cumulative beyond the stated caps and not payable as cash unless mandated by law.
3. Chronic Failure. Two consecutive months of SLA shortfalls on the same metric triggers a joint corrective action plan.

## 14. Liability and Indemnification
1. Mutual Indemnity. Each Party will defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the other Party and its affiliates against third-party claims to the extent arising from: (a) bodily injury or tangible property damage caused by the indemnifying Party’s negligence or willful misconduct; (b) violation of law; or (c) breach of confidentiality or data protection obligations by the indemnifying Party.
2. IP Indemnity by Provider. Provider will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or Deliverables (excluding Customer Materials and Third-Party Materials) infringe intellectual property rights, and will, at its option and expense: (a) modify or replace to be non-infringing while maintaining materially equivalent functionality; (b) obtain a license; or (c) if neither (a) nor (b) is commercially reasonable, refund prepaid fees for the infringing portion on a pro-rata basis.
3. Exclusions. The IP indemnity does not apply to claims arising from: (a) Customer modifications not authorized by Provider; (b) combination with items not provided by Provider where the claim would not exist but for the combination; or (c) Customer’s use not in accordance with the Agreement.
4. Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party’s aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement will not exceed an amount equal to the fees paid or payable by Customer to Provider for the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim for the affected services.
5. Excluded Claims. The foregoing cap does not apply to: (a) breach of confidentiality; (b) IP infringement indemnity obligations; (c) death, bodily injury, or tangible property damage caused by a Party’s negligence or willful misconduct; or (d) fraud. For Personal Data Breach caused by Provider’s failure to comply with its data protection obligations, liability is capped at two times (2x) the 12-month fees for the affected services.
6. Exclusion of Consequential Damages. Neither Party will be liable for consequential, incidental, special, indirect, punitive, or exemplary damages, lost profits, or loss of business, even if advised of the possibility, except to the extent such limitation is prohibited by Applicable Law.

## 15. Audit, Verification, and Right to Inspect
1. Customer Audit. On reasonable notice and during normal business hours, Customer may audit Provider’s compliance no more than annually, or more frequently in response to a substantiated incident or regulator request. Audits will minimize disruption and protect Provider confidentiality and security.
2. Certifications. Provider will maintain relevant certifications (e.g., ISO 27001) and provide summaries or attestations (e.g., SOC 2 Type II if available) under NDA upon request.
3. Remediation. Provider will promptly remediate material findings within agreed timelines.

## 16. Subcontracting and Personnel
1. Subcontracting. Provider may subcontract portions of the services with prior written notice to Customer. Provider remains fully responsible for subcontractors’ performance.
2. Personnel. Provider will ensure personnel are qualified, have executed appropriate confidentiality agreements, and have passed background checks proportional to role sensitivity.

## 17. Insurance
1. Coverage. Provider will maintain insurance with reputable insurers: (a) Commercial General Liability: $2,000,000 per occurrence; (b) Professional/Technology E&O: $5,000,000 aggregate; (c) Cyber Liability/Privacy: $5,000,000 aggregate, including incident response and regulatory defense; (d) Workers’ Compensation and Employer’s Liability per statute.
2. Evidence. Certificates of insurance will be provided on request. Provider will notify Customer of material changes or cancellations within 30 days where feasible.

## 18. Anti-Corruption, Sanctions, and Ethical Conduct
1. Anti-Bribery. Each Party will comply with applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws and maintain internal controls to prevent improper payments.
2. Sanctions and Export. Each Party will comply with applicable export control and sanctions laws. Provider will not process data from embargoed jurisdictions or sanctioned parties in violation of law.
3. Code of Conduct. Provider will adhere to ethical business practices, non-discrimination, and modern slavery prevention requirements.

## 19. Force Majeure
1. Suspension. A Party is not liable for delay or failure to perform due to a Force Majeure Event. The affected Party will notify the other promptly and use reasonable efforts to mitigate. Performance timelines will be extended by the duration of the event.
2. Termination. If inability to perform continues for more than 30 days, the non-affected Party may terminate the impacted services without penalty.

## 20. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
1. Good-Faith Negotiation. The Parties will attempt to resolve disputes through good-faith negotiations, escalating to the Steering Committee and then to executive leadership (including Customer’s CISO/Legal) before formal proceedings.
2. Mediation. If unresolved after 30 days, the Parties will engage in non-binding mediation with a mutually agreed mediator.
3. Venue and Law. Subject to mediation, disputes will be finally resolved by [arbitration in City, Country under Rules] or [courts of Jurisdiction], and governed by the laws of [Governing Law Jurisdiction], excluding conflict-of-law rules. Either Party may seek injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect IP or Confidential Information.

## 21. Notices
1. Notices. Formal notices will be in writing and delivered by courier, certified mail, or email with confirmation to the addresses specified in the SOW. Operational notices may be via designated ticketing systems.

## 22. Assignment; Entire Agreement; Severability; Waiver
1. Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party’s consent, except to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee assumes all obligations.
2. Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with the SOW(s) and incorporated schedules, constitutes the entire agreement and supersedes prior agreements regarding its subject matter.
3. Severability. If any provision is invalid, the remainder remains enforceable; the Parties will replace invalid provisions with valid ones that reflect the original intent.
4. Waiver. No waiver of any breach is a waiver of any other breach. Waivers must be in writing.

# Compliance Requirements

## 1. Mandatory Requirements Compliance Matrix
| Requirement | Compliance Status | Evidence/Certification | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Contract Terms and Conditions
1. Definitions
   1. “Customer” means the buyer identified in the RFP and resulting contract.
   2. “Supplier” means the respondent providing 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation, and incident response services.
   3. “Services” means the cybersecurity services, deliverables, support, and related professional services described in the Statement(s) of Work (SOW).
   4. “Deliverables” means all reports, configurations, playbooks, integrations, and documentation produced under the SOW.
   5. “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by either Party that is identified as confidential or should reasonably be understood as confidential.
2. Term
   1. The Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for the initial term specified in the SOW, with renewal terms as mutually agreed in writing.
3. Order of Precedence
   1. In case of conflict: (1) the main body of the Master Services Agreement (MSA); (2) Data Processing Addendum (DPA); (3) SOW(s); (4) Service Level Agreement (SLA); (5) other exhibits or policies referenced. Customer purchase orders are for administrative purposes and do not modify terms unless expressly accepted in writing.
4. Acceptance of Deliverables
   1. Supplier will submit Deliverables for Customer review. Customer has 10 business days to accept or reject with specific defects. Supplier will remediate defects and resubmit within a commercially reasonable timeframe. Deliverables are deemed accepted if no written rejection is provided within the review period.
5. Change Control
   1. Material changes to scope, timing, or cost require a mutually executed change order before implementation. Emergency changes for security risk mitigation may be implemented promptly with post-change documentation and Customer notification.
6. Governance and Stakeholders
   1. Governance includes representation by Customer’s CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal Department, and Procurement Team.
   2. A joint steering committee meets monthly during implementation and quarterly thereafter to review performance, risks, compliance, and continuous improvement.
7. Records and Audit
   1. Supplier will maintain accurate records of Services and security controls for at least 7 years or as required by law.
   2. Upon 30 days’ notice, and no more than annually (or more frequently following a Security Incident or material non-conformance), Customer or its auditor may conduct a reasonable audit of relevant controls, subject to confidentiality and security restrictions.
8. Subcontracting
   1. Supplier remains fully liable for subcontractors and will not engage subcontractors that process Customer Data without Customer’s written consent. Subcontractors must meet or exceed the security, confidentiality, and data protection obligations herein.
9. Publicity
   1. Neither Party will use the other’s name, logos, or marks in publicity without prior written consent, except as required by law.

## 2. Payment Terms and Pricing
1. Invoicing and Payment
   1. Invoices are issued upon achievement of SOW milestones and monthly in arrears for recurring Services.
   2. Payment terms are Net 30 days after invoice approval. Customer may withhold amounts disputed in good faith.
   3. A 10% retention will be applied to milestone-based fees and released upon project completion and acceptance.
2. Performance-Based Payment
   1. Payments are contingent upon meeting performance milestones defined in the SOW. Failure to meet milestones permits Customer to defer payment for the affected milestone until completion.
3. Taxes
   1. Fees exclude applicable taxes. Each Party is responsible for taxes based on its income or net worth. Supplier will itemize any indirect taxes and provide valid tax invoices.
4. Late Payment
   1. Late, undisputed amounts accrue interest at the lesser of 1% per month or the maximum rate permitted by law.
5. Expenses
   1. Pre-approved, reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses will be reimbursed at cost, in accordance with Customer policy.

## 3. Service Levels and Performance Management
1. Service Availability
   1. SIEM platform availability: 99.9% monthly uptime, excluding approved maintenance windows (with 5 business days’ notice for planned maintenance; emergency maintenance with prompt notice).
2. Response and Resolution Targets
   1. 24/7/365 SOC monitoring and triage.
   2. Initial acknowledgement (P1): ≤ 15 minutes; Containment action initiation (P1): ≤ 1 hour from detection/notification.
   3. Initial acknowledgement (P2): ≤ 1 hour; Containment (P2): ≤ 4 hours.
3. Metrics and Reporting
   1. Monthly SLA reports including availability, MTTA, MTTR, incident volumes, false-positive rates, use case coverage, and patching status for tools under Supplier control.
   2. Quarterly service review with trend analysis and continuous improvement plan.
4. Service Credits
   1. Service credits apply to monthly recurring charges for the affected service, capped at 15% of the monthly fee. Credits are not a penalty and do not limit other remedies for data breaches or wilful misconduct.

### 3.1 SLA Metrics Table
| Metric | Target | Measurement Window | Credit Trigger | Credit Amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SIEM Availability | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Calendar month | < 99.9% | 5% of monthly fee for 99.0–99.89%; 10% for 98.0–98.99%; 15% for < 98.0% |
| SOC Coverage | 100% 24/7 monitoring | Calendar month | Any uncovered period > 15 minutes | 5% per event, max 15% |
| P1 MTTA | ≤ 15 minutes | Per incident | > 15 minutes | 2% per incident, max 10% |
| P1 Containment Start | ≤ 1 hour | Per incident | > 1 hour | 5% per incident, max 15% |
| P2 MTTA | ≤ 1 hour | Per incident | > 1 hour | 1% per incident, max 5% |
| P2 Containment Start | ≤ 4 hours | Per incident | > 4 hours | 2% per incident, max 10% |
| Incident Reporting | RCA within 5 business days | Per P1 | RCA late | 2% per delayed RCA |
| Change Notifications | 5 days notice for planned maintenance | Per change | < 5 days notice | 1% per occurrence |

### 3.2 Incident Priority Definitions
1. P1 (Critical): Active compromise or material business disruption, high likelihood of data exfiltration, or critical system outage.
2. P2 (High): Confirmed malicious activity with limited scope or significant vulnerability exposure without evidence of exploitation.
3. P3 (Medium): Suspicious activity requiring investigation; non-critical vulnerability remediation.
4. P4 (Low): Informational alerts, tuning, and maintenance tasks.

## 4. Data Protection and Privacy
1. Roles and Scope
   1. For Customer Data, Customer is Controller and Supplier is Processor (or Service Provider under applicable law).
2. Data Processing Addendum
   1. Parties will execute a DPA incorporating Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or other approved transfer mechanisms for cross-border data flows.
3. Compliance with Laws
   1. Supplier will comply with applicable data protection laws, including GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, PIPEDA, and other local laws where Services are provided.
4. Security Measures
   1. ISO/IEC 27001: Supplier will maintain an active ISO 27001 certification or equivalent ISMS, with annual surveillance audits.
   2. Technical controls include: encryption at rest and in transit (industry-standard algorithms), MFA for administrative access, least-privilege access, EDR on endpoints under Supplier control, vulnerability management, SIEM logging and monitoring, and secure software development practices for any tooling.
5. Data Location and Sovereignty
   1. Customer Data will be stored and processed within regions approved in writing by Customer. Supplier will not move data outside approved regions without consent.
6. Sub-processing
   1. Supplier will maintain an up-to-date list of sub-processors, provide prior notice of changes, and allow Customer objection for reasonable, documented grounds.
7. Breach Notification
   1. Supplier will notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of a confirmed Security Incident involving Customer Data, providing the nature of the incident, scope, mitigation, and contact details.
8. Data Subject Rights and Cooperation
   1. Supplier will assist Customer in responding to data subject requests, DPIAs, and consultations with supervisory authorities, as applicable.
9. Retention and Deletion
   1. Upon termination or upon Customer request, Supplier will return or securely delete Customer Data within 30 days, except as required by law, and certify deletion.
10. Confidentiality
   1. Supplier personnel are bound by confidentiality obligations and undergo annual privacy and security training.
11. Anonymization and Telemetry
   1. Any analytics or benchmarking uses of Customer Data require prior written consent and must use de-identified or aggregated data.

## 5. Information Security and Regulatory Compliance
1. Security Frameworks
   1. Mandatory: ISO/IEC 27001 (certified). Alignment: NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-61 (IR), NIST SP 800-53 (selected controls), CIS Controls, and CSA CCM where cloud services are in scope.
2. Regulatory Coverage (as applicable)
   1. Industry-specific: PCI DSS for cardholder data; HIPAA/HITECH for PHI; SOX-relevant ITGCs; FedRAMP or equivalent where required by government customers.
3. Secure Operations
   1. 24/7 SOC with documented runbooks, playbooks aligned to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, and case management with full audit trails.
4. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
   1. Supplier maintains tested BCP/DR plans with at least annual exercises. Target RTO ≤ 8 hours and RPO ≤ 15 minutes for logging pipelines under Supplier control.
5. Access Management
   1. Role-based access control, unique IDs, MFA, session timeouts, and quarterly access reviews for systems handling Customer Data.
6. Logging and Monitoring
   1. Centralized logging to SIEM, immutable storage options, time synchronization, and retention consistent with Customer policy or legal requirements.
7. Secure Integrations
   1. APIs and collectors secured via mTLS/OAuth2, keys rotated at least every 90 days, and secrets stored in a vault.

## 6. Intellectual Property Rights
1. Pre-Existing IP
   1. Each Party retains all rights in its pre-existing IP and tools, including methodologies and know-how.
2. Deliverables
   1. Upon full payment, Customer receives a worldwide, perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use, copy, modify, and create derivative works of Deliverables for its internal business purposes.
3. Supplier Tools
   1. Supplier’s standard tools, runbooks, content libraries, and platforms remain Supplier IP. Supplier grants Customer a license to use such tools as embedded in Deliverables for the term of the Agreement.
4. Open Source
   1. Supplier will identify open-source components in Deliverables and comply with applicable licenses. No copyleft code will be introduced into Customer environments without prior written approval.
5. IP Indemnity
   1. Supplier will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe IP rights, and will procure rights, modify, or replace infringing items. Exclusions apply for Customer-provided materials or unauthorized modifications.

## 7. Liability and Indemnification
1. Mutual Indemnities
   1. Each Party will indemnify the other against third-party claims for bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by its negligence or willful misconduct.
2. Data Protection Indemnity
   1. Supplier will indemnify Customer for third-party claims arising from Supplier’s breach of data protection obligations or Security Incidents caused by Supplier’s failure to comply with the Agreement’s security requirements.
3. Limitation of Liability
   1. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party’s aggregate liability is limited to the greater of (a) 12 months of fees paid or payable under the applicable SOW, or (b) [Currency][Amount] as mutually agreed.
   2. Excluded Claims: breach of confidentiality, IP infringement, data protection breaches caused by a Party, gross negligence, fraud, or wilful misconduct.
4. No Indirect Damages
   1. Neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or loss of profits, revenue, or data, except to the extent such exclusion is prohibited by law.

## 8. Insurance
1. Supplier will maintain, at its own expense:
   1. Commercial General Liability: ≥ [Currency]2,000,000 per occurrence.
   2. Professional/Technology E&O: ≥ [Currency]5,000,000 aggregate.
   3. Cyber Liability/Privacy: ≥ [Currency]5,000,000 aggregate, including incident response, notification, forensics, regulatory defense, and fines/penalties where insurable.
   4. Workers’ Compensation and Employers’ Liability as required by law.
2. Certificates of insurance will be provided upon request; policies shall include Customer as additional insured where applicable and provide 30 days’ notice of cancellation.

## 9. Subcontracting and Personnel
1. Personnel
   1. Supplier personnel assigned to Services will be qualified, trained, and subject to background checks commensurate with job duties and applicable law.
2. Key Personnel
   1. Replacement of key personnel requires prior notice and mutual agreement, not to be unreasonably withheld.
3. Non-Solicitation
   1. Neither Party will solicit employment of the other Party’s assigned personnel during the term and for 6 months thereafter, excluding general solicitations.

## 10. Confidentiality
1. Obligations
   1. Recipient will use Confidential Information solely to perform under the Agreement, protect it with at least the same care it uses for its own similar information (not less than reasonable care), and disclose only to those with a need to know under confidentiality obligations.
2. Exceptions
   1. Information that is public, independently developed, or rightfully obtained without restriction is not Confidential.
3. Compelled Disclosure
   1. Recipient may disclose as required by law with prompt notice to the Discloser (where lawful) and reasonable cooperation to seek protective measures.

## 11. Audit and Compliance Verification
1. Compliance Evidence
   1. Supplier will provide upon request: ISO 27001 certificate and SoA, recent SOC 2 Type II report (or equivalent independent assessment), penetration test executive summaries, vulnerability scan summaries, and remediation plans.
2. Regulatory Inquiries
   1. Supplier will promptly notify Customer of regulatory inquiries that materially impact the Services and cooperate with Customer in responses related to Customer Data.

1. Planned Maintenance
   1. Conducted during agreed windows with at least 5 business days’ notice; emergency maintenance with prompt notice and post-incident report.

   1. Changes tracked in a CMDB or equivalent, with approvals, rollback plans, and logs retained for 12 months minimum.

1. Termination for Convenience
   1. Customer may terminate any SOW for convenience with 30 days’ written notice. Customer will pay for Services performed through the effective termination date, excluding unperformed future services and unrecoverable third-party costs not pre-approved.

   1. Either Party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days after written notice (10 days for undisputed non-payment).

   1. Supplier may suspend Services for undisputed, materially overdue payments after 10 days’ notice and opportunity to cure, provided suspension does not create unreasonable security risk.

   1. For up to 90 days post-termination, Supplier will provide reasonable transition assistance at then-current rates, including data export, runbook turnover, and knowledge transfer.

1. Escalation
   1. Disputes will first be escalated to project managers, then to the steering committee.

   1. Unresolved disputes will be resolved by arbitration under [Arbitration Rules] in [Seat/Venue], or by courts of [Jurisdiction], as specified in the SOW.

   1. The Agreement is governed by the laws of [Jurisdiction], excluding conflicts-of-law principles.

Neither Party is liable for delay or failure due to events beyond reasonable control (including cyberattacks not caused by a Party’s negligence, natural disasters, labor disputes, pandemics, governmental actions), provided the impacted Party uses diligent efforts to mitigate and resumes performance promptly.

   1. Supplier warrants Deliverables do not knowingly infringe third-party IP and will not introduce malicious code.

2. Recommended/Aligned
   1. NIST CSF; SOC 2 Type II; ISO 27017/27018 for cloud; PCI DSS (if applicable); HIPAA (if applicable); local privacy regulations.

   1. If any provision is invalid, the remainder remains enforceable.

   1. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement and supersedes prior discussions. Amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties.
