# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Definitions
1.1 “Agreement” means the contract formed between the Parties comprised of this document, the Statement(s) of Work (SOW), and any referenced schedules, annexes, or addenda.  
1.2 “Client” means the procuring entity identified in the RFP and its Affiliates.  
1.3 “Provider” means the Respondent and its Affiliates providing the Services.  
1.4 “Services” means the cybersecurity services described in the SOW, including 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation and operations, and incident response.  
1.5 “Deliverables” means all reports, configurations, rules, playbooks, documentation, and other work product created specifically for Client under the Agreement.  
1.6 “Confidential Information” means all non-public information disclosed by a Party, including security information, personal data, trade secrets, pricing, and technical documentation.  
1.7 “Personal Data” means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person processed in connection with the Services.  
1.8 “Security Incident” means any actual or suspected compromise of the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Client systems or data processed by Provider.  
1.9 “SLA” means the service levels, measurements, and service credits set out in Section 12.  
1.10 “ISO 27001” means ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and applicable controls in ISO/IEC 27002, as updated.

## 2. Scope of Services
2.1 Provider shall deliver 24/7/365 Security Operations Center (SOC) monitoring, SIEM implementation and management, threat detection and response, and incident response with a response time of one (1) hour for Priority 1 events.  
2.2 Provider shall supply and maintain a SIEM platform, integrations, content (use cases, rules, dashboards), and continuous tuning.  
2.3 Provider shall provide onboarding, asset and log source discovery, runbooks/playbooks, and knowledge transfer to Client personnel.  
2.4 Provider shall provide regulatory and executive reporting, including monthly KPI/KRI reporting and quarterly service reviews.  
2.5 Provider shall collaborate with Client stakeholders, including the CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal Department, and Procurement Team, for governance, risk, and compliance alignment.

## 3. Term; Renewal
3.1 Initial Term: [12/24/36] months from the Effective Date.  
3.2 Renewal: Auto-renews for successive 12-month terms unless a Party gives 60 days’ prior written notice of non-renewal.  
3.3 Any renewal will be on then-current terms, subject to mutually agreed pricing.

## 4. Fees, Invoicing, and Payment
4.1 Fees are as set forth in the pricing schedule and tied to performance milestones.  
4.2 Invoicing: Provider shall invoice following achievement of agreed milestones.  
4.3 Payment Terms: Net thirty (30) days after invoice approval by Client.  
4.4 Retention: Client shall retain ten percent (10%) of fees until project completion and acceptance, after which the retention shall be released.  
4.5 Late Payment: Interest accrues at the lesser of 1% per month or the maximum allowable by law.  
4.6 Taxes: Fees exclude applicable taxes; Client is responsible for taxes except those based on Provider’s income.  
4.7 No Purchase-Money Security Interest is created by retention; title to Deliverables is governed by Section 10.

## 5. Acceptance and Milestones
5.1 Acceptance Criteria: Each Deliverable shall be subject to acceptance against documented criteria in the SOW.  
5.2 Testing Period: Client has 10 business days to test and accept or reject with a written defect list; Provider will remedy defects within a commercially reasonable period.  
5.3 Milestone Completion: Payment milestones are deemed met upon acceptance of associated Deliverables.  
5.4 Failure to Meet Milestones: Client may withhold milestone payment proportionate to unmet deliverables until remedied.

## 6. Changes and Governance
6.1 Change Control: Any change to scope, schedule, or cost shall be governed by a written change order executed by both Parties.  
6.2 Steering and Escalation: A joint governance forum including Client’s CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, and Provider’s Engagement Lead will meet monthly; an escalation matrix is maintained in the runbook.  
6.3 Records: Provider will maintain project documentation, architecture diagrams, runbooks, and as-built documentation, kept current.

## 7. Warranties
7.1 Services Warranty: Provider warrants Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry best practices.  
7.2 Compliance Warranty: Provider warrants compliance with applicable laws, ISO 27001, and the requirements in Section 11.  
7.3 No Malicious Code: Provider will not introduce malware or timebombs into Client environment.  
7.4 Remedy: For breach of warranty, Provider will re-perform nonconforming Services; if not cured within 30 days, Client may seek appropriate remedies, including fee credits proportionate to the impact.

## 8. Confidentiality
8.1 Each Party shall protect the other’s Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own, and no less than a reasonable standard of care.  
8.2 Use/Disclosure: Confidential Information may be used only to perform the Agreement and disclosed only to those with a need to know and subject to confidentiality obligations.  
8.3 Compelled Disclosure: A Party may disclose Confidential Information when legally compelled, with prior notice where lawful.  
8.4 Survival: Confidentiality obligations survive for five (5) years after termination; trade secrets survive as long as they remain trade secrets.

## 9. Data Protection and Privacy
9.1 Roles: Client is the controller; Provider is the processor (or service provider under applicable laws).  
9.2 Processing Instructions: Provider shall process Personal Data solely on documented instructions from Client, including regarding international transfers.  
9.3 Security Measures: Provider will implement appropriate technical and organizational measures consistent with ISO 27001 and Section 11, including encryption in transit and at rest, access controls, logging, and vulnerability management.  
9.4 Subprocessors: Provider may engage subprocessors only with prior written authorization from Client and shall flow down equivalent data protection obligations; Provider remains liable for subprocessor acts and omissions.  
9.5 Data Subject Rights: Provider will assist Client in responding to data subject requests and regulatory inquiries.  
9.6 Breach Notification: Provider shall notify Client without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after confirming a Personal Data Breach, providing details of the nature of the breach, affected records, mitigation, and corrective actions.  
9.7 International Transfers: Where applicable, Provider shall use lawful transfer mechanisms (e.g., EU SCCs, UK IDTA/Addendum) and maintain supplementary measures.  
9.8 Data Retention and Deletion: Upon termination or at Client’s request, Provider will securely return or delete Personal Data (at Client’s option) within 30 days, except where retention is required by law.  
9.9 Privacy by Design: Provider will incorporate privacy by design and by default into SIEM use cases, data minimization, and retention settings.  
9.10 Audits: Provider shall provide audit reports (e.g., ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 Type II if available) and allow reasonable on-site or remote audits annually and for cause, subject to confidentiality and safety requirements.  
9.11 Cross-Border Government Access: Provider will promptly notify Client of any government request for Client data (where lawful) and challenge overbroad requests.

## 10. Intellectual Property Rights
10.1 Background IP: Each Party retains all right, title, and interest in its pre-existing intellectual property and tools.  
10.2 Foreground IP/Deliverables: Upon payment, Provider grants Client a perpetual, worldwide, irrevocable, non-exclusive license to use, copy, modify, and create derivative works of the Deliverables for Client’s internal business purposes.  
10.3 Provider Tools: Provider retains ownership of its generic tools, methodologies, templates, and know-how; Provider grants Client a perpetual, non-exclusive license to use any embedded Provider Tools solely as part of the Deliverables.  
10.4 Open Source: Provider shall comply with applicable open-source licenses, provide a bill of materials upon request, and ensure no copyleft obligations are triggered on Client systems by the Deliverables.  
10.5 Third-Party Materials: Provider shall secure necessary rights for third-party components used in the Services.

## 11. Regulatory and Standards Compliance
11.1 ISO 27001: Provider shall maintain ISO 27001 compliance and, upon request, provide a current certificate or alignment evidence and remediate audit findings promptly.  
11.2 Cybersecurity Frameworks: Provider will align controls with ISO 27001/27002 and map to NIST CSF where applicable.  
11.3 Privacy Laws: Provider shall comply with applicable data protection laws, including GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and other local privacy statutes relevant to the processing and locations.  
11.4 Sectoral Standards: Where applicable, Provider will comply with HIPAA, PCI DSS, and other mandated security/privacy standards relevant to Client’s environment.  
11.5 Export/Sanctions: Provider and its personnel will comply with export controls and sanctions (e.g., EAR, OFAC, UK/EU regimes).  
11.6 Anti-Corruption: Provider shall comply with anti-bribery laws (e.g., FCPA, UK Bribery Act) and maintain related policies and training.  
11.7 Accessibility: Deliverables (e.g., dashboards, reports) will conform to WCAG 2.1 AA where reasonably applicable.  
11.8 Records Retention: Provider will retain records of Services, security logs, and incident reports for at least [12–24] months or as required by law or the SOW.

## 12. Service Level Agreement (SLA)

### 12.1 Definitions and Measurement
1) Service Window: 24/7/365 for SOC monitoring, alert triage, and incident response.  
2) Measurement Period: Monthly calendar period unless stated otherwise.  
3) Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance with 7 days’ notice, emergency maintenance with as much notice as practicable, events of Force Majeure, Client-caused outages, and third-party failures outside Provider’s control.

### 12.2 SLA Metrics and Credits

| Metric | Target | Measurement Window | Exclusions | Service Credits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SIEM Platform Availability | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Uptime % per month | Planned maintenance (≤4 hrs/month), force majeure | 2% of monthly fee per 0.1% below target, cap 15% |
| SOC Coverage | 24/7/365 continuous monitoring | Monthly | Force majeure | 5% monthly fee if any gap > 30 minutes (per incident), cap 20% |
| P1 Alert MTTA (acknowledge) | ≤ 15 minutes | Monthly | False positives confirmed by Client | 3% monthly fee if >15 min median, +1% each additional 5 min, cap 15% |
| P1 Incident Engagement | ≤ 1 hour to engage incident responder | Per incident | Force majeure | 5% monthly fee per breach, cap 25% |
| P1 Containment Time | ≤ 4 hours from engagement | Per incident | Requires Client action not provided | 2% per hour beyond target, cap 15% |
| P2 Alert MTTA | ≤ 30 minutes | Monthly | As above | 1% monthly fee if >30 min median, cap 10% |
| True Positive Rate (use-case efficacy) | ≥ 95% of validated incidents detected | Quarterly | Novel zero-day | 3% quarterly fee for <95% (linear to floor 85%), cap 15% |
| Monthly Reporting Timeliness | Reports delivered ≤ 5 business days after month-end | Monthly | Client delays | 1% monthly fee per late report, cap 5% |
| Change/Rule Deployment | Standard changes within 3 business days | Monthly | Emergency changes | 1% monthly fee if <95% on-time, cap 5% |

Notes:
- Service credits are applied against the next invoice for the impacted service tower and are without prejudice to termination rights for chronic failure (≥3 months of material SLA breach in any rolling 6-month period).
- Credits are not payable as cash unless the Agreement is terminated and no further invoices are due.

### 12.3 Incident Priorities
1) Priority 1 (P1): Active compromise, ransomware, data exfiltration, critical system outage, widespread malware.  
2) Priority 2 (P2): High-risk IOC/IOA without confirmed compromise, targeted phishing with credential exposure.  
3) Priority 3 (P3): Medium-risk alerts, suspicious activity requiring investigation.  
4) Priority 4 (P4): Low-risk events, tuning, and informational notifications.

### 12.4 Escalation
1) P1: Notify Client CISO and on-call leadership immediately; hourly updates until containment.  
2) P2: Updates every 4 hours until mitigation; daily thereafter.  
3) P3–P4: Updates per agreed cadence in the runbook.

## 13. Security Obligations
13.1 Controls: Provider will implement administrative, technical, and physical safeguards aligned to ISO 27001, including identity and access management (MFA), least privilege, network segmentation, encryption (TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest), secure software development, and continuous monitoring.  
13.2 Logging: All administrative and security-relevant activities on SIEM/SOC systems are logged, time-synchronized, immutable, and retained per Section 11.8.  
13.3 Vulnerability Management: Monthly scanning of relevant components; critical vulnerabilities remediated within 15 days; high within 30 days.  
13.4 Penetration Testing: Annual penetration test of externally exposed SOC/SIEM components; remediation plan within 30 days for critical findings.  
13.5 Background Checks: SOC analysts and engineers undergo background screening consistent with law and Client policy.  
13.6 Secure Access: Provider’s access to Client systems uses VPN or zero-trust controls with MFA and session recording where feasible.  
13.7 Tooling and EDR Integration: Provider will integrate with Client-approved EDR/NDR and ticketing systems under change control.

## 14. Indemnification
14.1 IP Infringement: Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Client against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe IP rights, and pay damages, costs, and reasonable attorneys’ fees awarded or agreed in settlement. Provider may procure rights, modify, or replace to avoid infringement; if not feasible, Client may terminate affected Services for a pro-rata refund.  
14.2 Data Security: Provider shall defend and indemnify Client against third-party claims to the extent arising from Provider’s failure to comply with Section 9 or 13, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of Personal Data or Client Confidential Information.  
14.3 Client Indemnity: Client shall defend and indemnify Provider against third-party claims arising from Client-provided data, instructions, or unlawful use of the Services.  
14.4 Conditions: Indemnification is conditioned on prompt notice, control of defense by indemnifying Party, and reasonable cooperation by the other Party.

## 15. Limitation of Liability
15.1 Cap: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party’s aggregate liability arising out of or related to the Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Client to Provider in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability.  
15.2 Excluded Claims: The cap does not apply to (a) death or personal injury caused by negligence, (b) willful misconduct or fraud, (c) IP infringement indemnity (Section 14.1), (d) breach of confidentiality (Section 8), and (e) data protection breaches caused by a Party’s failure to implement required security measures (Sections 9 and 13).  
15.3 Exclusions: Neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, loss of profit or revenue, or loss of data, except to the extent such limitation is prohibited by law.  
15.4 Proportional Fault: Liability will be proportionate to each Party’s comparative fault.

## 16. Insurance
16.1 Provider will maintain insurance with reputable carriers:  
1) Technology Errors & Omissions, including Cyber Liability: minimum [USD/EUR] 5,000,000 per claim and in the aggregate.  
2) Commercial General Liability: minimum [USD/EUR] 2,000,000 per occurrence.  
3) Workers’ Compensation and Employers’ Liability: statutory limits.  
4) Professional Liability: minimum [USD/EUR] 2,000,000 per claim.  
16.2 Certificates of Insurance will be provided upon request; policies will include Client as additional insured where customary and permissible.

## 17. Audit and Compliance Verification
17.1 Client may audit Provider’s compliance once per contract year and for cause with 10 business days’ notice (or shorter for security incidents).  
17.2 Provider will remediate material findings within agreed timelines and provide evidence of closure.  
17.3 No audit shall unreasonably disrupt Provider operations or compromise third-party confidentiality.

## 18. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
18.1 Provider shall maintain documented BCDR plans covering SIEM and SOC operations, test them at least annually, and provide test summaries upon request.  
18.2 Recovery Objectives: RTO ≤ 8 hours; RPO ≤ 1 hour for SIEM data critical to monitoring continuity.

## 19. Subcontracting and Assignment
19.1 Subcontracting is permitted with Client’s prior written consent for material portions of the Services; Provider remains fully responsible for subcontractor performance.  
19.2 Assignment: Neither Party may assign the Agreement without the other Party’s consent, except to an Affiliate or in connection with a merger or sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee assumes all obligations.

## 20. Service Management and Reporting
20.1 Reporting: Monthly operational reports and quarterly executive reviews will include SLA performance, incidents, root cause analyses, threat trends, and improvement plans.  
20.2 Knowledge Transfer: Provider will deliver training and documentation enabling Client’s teams to understand operations, playbooks, and dashboards.  
20.3 Continuous Improvement: Provider will propose quarterly enhancements to detections, use cases, and response procedures.

## 21. Termination; Exit and Transition
21.1 Termination for Cause: Either Party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days after written notice (10 days for payment breaches).  
21.2 Termination for Convenience: Client may terminate for convenience on 30 days’ written notice; Client will pay for Services performed through the effective date and reasonable, pre-approved demobilization costs.  
21.3 Insolvency: Either Party may terminate immediately if the other becomes insolvent, enters bankruptcy, or ceases business.  
21.4 Effect of Termination: Provider will promptly cease Services, deliver work-in-progress, return or delete Client data per Section 9.8, and cooperate in transitioning Services to Client or a replacement provider.  
21.5 Transition Assistance: For up to 60 days post-termination, Provider will provide transition support at agreed rates not exceeding those in the Agreement.  
21.6 Retention Release: Upon successful completion or termination for convenience, any retained amounts for accepted Deliverables will be released, less any undisputed offsets.

## 22. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
22.1 Good Faith Negotiations: Senior representatives shall attempt to resolve disputes within 15 business days of notice.  
22.2 Mediation/Arbitration: If unresolved, the Parties will attempt mediation; failing that, disputes shall be resolved by [court of competent jurisdiction/arbitration under (e.g., ICC, AAA) rules] in [Governing Law: State/Province/Country], without regard to conflict-of-law principles.  
22.3 Injunctive Relief: Either Party may seek injunctive or equitable relief for breaches of confidentiality, IP infringement, or data protection obligations.  
22.4 Language: The governing language of the Agreement is English unless otherwise agreed.

## 23. Force Majeure
23.1 Neither Party is liable for failure to perform due to events beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, war, terrorism, labor actions (excluding those of the affected Party’s workforce), or internet backbone failures. The affected Party shall use reasonable efforts to mitigate and resume performance.

## 24. Notices
24.1 Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, courier, or certified mail to the addresses designated by each Party, with copies to Legal Departments. Email notices are permitted for operational communications and incident notices.

## 25. Order of Precedence
25.1 In case of conflict, the following order applies: (1) Data Protection Addendum (if separate); (2) this Agreement; (3) SOW; (4) RFP and Provider Response; (5) Purchase Orders.

## 26. Miscellaneous
26.1 Entire Agreement: This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement and supersedes prior understandings on the subject matter.  
26.2 Amendments: Must be in writing and signed by both Parties.  
26.3 Severability: Invalid provisions will be modified to be enforceable without changing intent; remaining provisions remain in force.  
26.4 No Waiver: Failure to enforce any provision is not a waiver.  
26.5 Independent Contractors: The Parties are independent contractors; no agency, partnership, or joint venture is created.  
26.6 Publicity: No use of the other Party’s name or marks without prior written consent.  
26.7 Counterparts: This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including electronically.

# Service Level Exhibit (Detail)

## A. Ticketing and Communications
1. Ticket Creation: All alerts and incidents tracked in Client-approved ticketing system with unique IDs.  
2. Update Cadence: P1 hourly; P2 every 4 hours; P3 daily; P4 weekly or as agreed.  
3. RCA: For P1 and chronic P2 incidents, Provider delivers an RCA within 5 business days of containment.  
4. Reporting: Monthly operational report and quarterly executive review with trend analysis.

## B. Maintenance Windows
1. Planned Maintenance: Up to 4 hours per month, scheduled with 7 days’ notice, during agreed low-traffic windows.  
2. Emergency Maintenance: Notice provided as soon as practicable; post-activity report within 24 hours.

## C. Service Credit Claims
1. Submission: Client submits claim within 30 days of the month-end with supporting evidence.  
2. Processing: Provider reviews within 15 days; undisputed credits applied to next invoice.

# Data Processing Addendum (Summary Terms)

1. Subject Matter: SOC/SIEM monitoring and incident response for Client systems.

# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Parties, Scope, and Order of Precedence
1.1 Parties. This Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into between [Customer Legal Name], with principal place of business at [Customer Address] (“Customer”), and [Vendor Legal Name], with principal place of business at [Vendor Address] (“Vendor”), collectively the “Parties,” and each a “Party.”
1.2 Scope of Services. Vendor shall provide managed cybersecurity services including: (a) 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) monitoring; (b) Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) implementation, configuration, and operation; and (c) incident detection, triage, and response initiation within one (1) hour of alert confirmation. Ancillary services may include threat intelligence, vulnerability management, log management, compliance reporting, and security advisory services as specified in the Statement(s) of Work (“SOW”).
1.3 Order of Precedence. In the event of conflict, the following order prevails: (1) an executed DPA or data protection addendum; (2) the SOW (including SLA schedule); (3) this Agreement; (4) any exhibits or attachments; (5) Vendor policies referenced for information only (non-binding unless expressly stated).

## 2. Definitions
2.1 Confidential Information: Non-public information disclosed by a Party that is designated as confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential, including security architecture, pricing, roadmaps, and Personal Data.  
2.2 Customer Data: All data provided by or collected on behalf of Customer through the Services, including logs, alerts, configurations, content, and Personal Data.  
2.3 Personal Data: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, as defined by applicable Data Protection Laws.  
2.4 Data Protection Laws: All applicable privacy and security laws and regulations, including, where applicable, GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA, GLBA, and similar laws.  
2.5 Security Incident: A confirmed unauthorized access to, acquisition of, or disclosure of Customer Data in Vendor’s possession or control, or a material compromise of systems that process Customer Data.  
2.6 Services: The managed cybersecurity services, software, deliverables, and support provided by Vendor under this Agreement and any SOW(s).  
2.7 Deliverables: Any work product, reports, configurations, runbooks, documentation, and other outputs created for Customer under an SOW.

## 3. Term
3.1 Term. The term of this Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for the duration specified in the SOW, unless terminated earlier per Section 16.  
3.2 Renewal. Unless otherwise stated in the SOW, the Agreement renews for successive one-year terms unless either Party provides at least sixty (60) days’ prior written notice of non-renewal.

## 4. Fees, Invoicing, and Payment
4.1 Fees. Fees are set forth in the applicable SOW or Order Form and may include one-time implementation fees, recurring subscription or managed services fees, and usage-based charges.  
4.2 Invoicing and Payment Terms. Invoices shall be issued per milestone or monthly in arrears, as stated in the SOW. Payment terms are Net 30 days after invoice approval by Customer.  
4.3 Performance Milestones and Retention. Payments are conditioned on Vendor meeting agreed performance milestones. Customer shall retain ten percent (10%) of amounts payable until project completion and Customer’s written acceptance of final deliverables.  
4.4 Disputed Amounts. Customer may withhold disputed amounts by providing written notice with reasonable detail within ten (10) days of receipt; undisputed amounts remain due. Parties will work in good faith to resolve disputes within thirty (30) days.  
4.5 Taxes. Fees exclude taxes. Vendor is responsible for taxes on its income, property, and employees; Customer is responsible for applicable sales/use taxes unless a valid exemption applies.

## 5. Service Levels and Performance Management
5.1 Service Levels. Vendor will meet or exceed the Service Level Metrics set forth in the SLA Schedule (see Section 14).  
5.2 Measurement and Reporting. Vendor will provide monthly SLA reports and root-cause analyses (RCAs) for P1/P2 incidents.  
5.3 Service Credits. Service Credits shall be applied as set forth in the SLA Schedule and are Customer’s primary remedy for SLA failures, without limiting Customer’s other rights for persistent or material breaches.  
5.4 Continuous Improvement. Vendor will maintain an ISO 27001-certified Information Security Management System (ISMS) and perform annual control reviews, implementing corrective actions and enhancements.

## 6. Security and Data Protection
6.1 ISO 27001. Vendor shall maintain ISO/IEC 27001 certification during the Term and provide current certificates upon request.  
6.2 Security Controls. Vendor shall implement administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, including:  
  1) Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256 or equivalent).  
  2) Role-based access control, MFA for privileged access, just-in-time access where feasible.  
  3) Vulnerability management with monthly scanning and remediation per risk: Critical ≤ 7 days; High ≤ 15 days; Medium ≤ 30 days; Low per risk acceptance.  
  4) Secure software development practices, code review, and change control.  
  5) Logging and monitoring across SIEM/SOAR with time-synchronized clocks and tamper-evident logs.  
  6) Segregation of Customer environments and data.  
  7) Annual penetration testing and remediation tracking.  
6.3 Incident Response and Notification.  
  1) Detection and Triage: Initiate incident triage within one (1) hour of alert confirmation, 24/7.  
  2) Containment and Eradication: Execute playbooks appropriate to severity; engage Customer within agreed RACI.  
  3) Notification: Notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after confirmation of a Security Incident that affects Customer Data; for Personal Data Breaches subject to GDPR, notify without undue delay and in any case within seventy-two (72) hours of becoming aware.  
  4) Cooperation: Provide timely updates, indicators of compromise, forensics artifacts, and post-incident reports, and assist with regulatory notifications as required.  
6.4 Data Processing Roles. The Parties acknowledge that, for Personal Data processed in connection with the Services, Customer acts as Controller and Vendor acts as Processor (or equivalent under applicable law). A Data Processing Addendum (DPA) forms part of this Agreement.  
6.5 Subprocessors. Vendor will maintain a list of Subprocessors, ensure written contracts with equivalent data protection obligations, and provide at least thirty (30) days’ notice prior to engaging new Subprocessors, allowing Customer objection for reasonable, documented grounds.  
6.6 Data Location and Transfers. Vendor will process Customer Data in approved regions as specified in the SOW. Cross-border transfers shall be governed by recognized transfer mechanisms (e.g., EU Standard Contractual Clauses and supplementary safeguards).  
6.7 Data Retention and Deletion. Vendor will retain Customer Data only as necessary for the Services and legal obligations. Upon termination or at Customer’s request, Vendor will return and securely delete Customer Data within thirty (30) days, certifying deletion.  
6.8 Privacy by Design. Vendor will assist Customer with data protection impact assessments, records of processing, and responding to data subject requests, to the extent applicable.

## 7. Intellectual Property Rights
7.1 Pre-Existing IP. Each Party retains all right, title, and interest in its pre-existing materials, methodologies, tools, software, and know-how (“Background IP”).  
7.2 Deliverables. Except as stated otherwise in the SOW:  
  1) Customer-Owned Deliverables: Custom reports, configurations, runbooks, and documentation created specifically for Customer shall be owned by Customer upon payment, excluding Vendor Background IP.  
  2) License to Background IP: Vendor grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use Vendor Background IP embedded in the Deliverables solely to the extent necessary to use, maintain, and modify the Deliverables.  
7.3 Software and Services. For Vendor’s software or managed platform, Vendor grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, limited right to access and use during the Term in accordance with the Agreement.  
7.4 Open Source. Vendor shall comply with applicable open-source licenses and provide notice of open-source components used; no copyleft terms shall impose obligations on Customer’s proprietary systems.  
7.5 Residuals. Use of general knowledge and skills retained in unaided memory is permitted, provided no Confidential Information is disclosed and no IP rights are infringed.

## 8. Confidentiality
8.1 Obligations. The receiving Party shall: (a) protect Confidential Information using at least industry-standard measures; (b) not disclose it to third parties except on a need-to-know basis under confidentiality obligations; and (c) use it solely to perform under this Agreement.  
8.2 Exclusions. Information that is public, independently developed, rightfully received from a third party, or previously known without restriction is not Confidential Information.  
8.3 Compelled Disclosure. A Party may disclose Confidential Information when legally compelled, providing prompt notice and cooperating to seek protective orders where lawful.  
8.4 Return/Destruction. Upon request or termination, the receiving Party will return or destroy Confidential Information, except one archival copy may be retained for legal compliance.

## 9. Warranties and Disclaimers
9.1 Vendor Warranties. Vendor warrants that:  
  1) The Services will conform in all material respects to the SOW, documentation, and SLAs.  
  2) It will perform Services in a professional and workmanlike manner using appropriately qualified personnel.  
  3) It will comply with applicable laws and maintain ISO 27001 certification.  
  4) Deliverables will be free of material defects and malware at delivery.  
9.2 Mutual Warranties. Each Party represents that it has the authority to enter into this Agreement.  
9.3 Remedies. For breach of warranty, Vendor shall re-perform non-conforming Services, repair/replace non-conforming Deliverables, or provide a pro-rata refund for the affected portion if not cured within thirty (30) days.  
9.4 Disclaimers. Except as expressly stated, neither Party makes any other warranties, express or implied, including merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose.

## 10. Liability and Indemnification
10.1 Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party’s aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable by Customer to Vendor in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.  
10.2 Excluded Claims. The limitations in Section 10.1 do not apply to: (a) breach of confidentiality; (b) infringement of IP rights; (c) Vendor’s data protection obligations for Security Incidents caused by Vendor’s breach of this Agreement; (d) fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence; (e) bodily injury or property damage to tangible property caused by a Party.  
10.3 Exclusion of Consequential Damages. Neither Party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special, punitive, or consequential damages, or loss of profits or revenues, except to the extent arising from Excluded Claims.  
10.4 Vendor Indemnity. Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims, damages, fines, penalties, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) arising from:  
  1) Alleged infringement or misappropriation of third-party IP rights by the Services or Deliverables (excluding Customer-provided materials).  
  2) Security Incidents to the extent caused by Vendor’s failure to comply with this Agreement.  
  3) Bodily injury or tangible property damage caused by Vendor.  
10.5 Customer Indemnity. Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor against third-party claims arising from Customer-provided data or materials that infringe IP or violate law.  
10.6 Indemnification Process. The indemnified Party will: (a) provide prompt notice; (b) grant control of defense to the indemnifying Party; and (c) reasonably cooperate. The indemnifying Party shall not settle any claim that imposes obligations or admissions on the indemnified Party without its prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld).  
10.7 IP Remedies. In case of an infringement claim, Vendor may: (a) obtain the right for Customer to continue using the Services/Deliverables; (b) modify to be non-infringing without materially reducing functionality; or (c) if not feasible, terminate the affected Services and refund prepaid fees for the unused period.

## 11. Insurance
11.1 Coverage. Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense:  
  1) Commercial General Liability: $2,000,000 aggregate.  
  2) Professional Liability/Errors & Omissions (including technology and cyber): $5,000,000 aggregate.  
  3) Cyber Liability/Privacy: $5,000,000 aggregate, including data breach costs, regulatory defense, and PCI assessment coverage if applicable.  
  4) Workers’ Compensation and Employers’ Liability as required by law.  
  5) Automobile Liability: $1,000,000 combined single limit (if vehicles are used in performance).  
11.2 Certificates. Certificates of insurance will be provided upon request; coverage shall not be materially reduced without thirty (30) days’ prior notice to Customer.

## 12. Subcontracting and Personnel
12.1 Subcontractors. Vendor may use qualified subcontractors with Customer’s prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), remaining fully responsible for their acts and omissions.  
12.2 Background Checks. Personnel with access to Customer environments or data shall undergo appropriate background checks and security training.  
12.3 Key Personnel. Vendor will assign key personnel for critical roles; replacement requires equivalently qualified resources with reasonable continuity planning.

## 13. Compliance and Regulatory Requirements
13.1 General Compliance. Vendor shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including data protection, cybersecurity, export controls, sanctions, anti-bribery, and labor laws.  
13.2 Information Security Standards. ISO/IEC 27001 compliance is mandatory. Where applicable, Vendor will align with NIST CSF, CIS Controls, and, if in scope, SOC 2 Type II.  
13.3 Sectoral Regulations (as applicable).  
  1) GDPR (EU/EEA), UK GDPR, and ePrivacy.  
  2) CCPA/CPRA (California) and analogous U.S. state privacy laws.  
  3) HIPAA (health data), GLBA (financial), PCI DSS (payment data).  
  4) Export controls (EAR), trade sanctions (OFAC), anti-bribery (FCPA, UK Bribery Act).  
13.4 Accessibility and Procurement. Vendor will comply with applicable accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG 2.1 AA), and public-sector procurement rules, if applicable.  
13.5 Records. Vendor will maintain accurate records demonstrating compliance and make them available for audit per Section 15.

## 14. Service Level Agreement (SLA) Metrics
| Metric | Target | Measurement Method | Reporting Frequency | Service Credits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOC Monitoring Coverage | 24/7/365 continuous monitoring | Monitoring schedules, staffing rosters, tooling availability | Monthly | 2% of monthly fee per hour of outage beyond 30 minutes, capped at 10% |
| SIEM Platform Uptime | ≥ 99.9% monthly | System telemetry and uptime monitors | Monthly | 5% of monthly SIEM fee per 0.1% below target, capped at 20% |
| Alert Triage Initiation (P1/P2) | ≤ 1 hour from alert confirmation | Ticket timestamps; audit logs | Monthly | 5% of monthly fee for any month with >2 breaches, capped at 20% |
| Initial Customer Notification (P1) | ≤ 1 hour from triage start | Ticket and comms logs | Monthly | 2% per breach beyond first, capped at 10% |
| Mean Time to Contain (P1) | ≤ 4 hours | Incident records and RCA | Monthly | 3% per breach beyond first, capped at 15% |
| Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) | ≤ 15 minutes for critical alerts | SIEM/SOAR metrics | Monthly | 2% if monthly average exceeds target by >50%, capped at 10% |
| Mean Time to Respond (MTTR) | ≤ 2 hours (P1), ≤ 8 hours (P2) | Ticketing system timestamps | Monthly | 3% if exceeded in a month, capped at 10% |
| Vulnerability Remediation | Critical ≤ 7 days; High ≤ 15 days | Scanner results; exceptions register | Monthly | 2% if >5% of items exceed SLA without approved exception |
| Reporting Delivery | Monthly ops and SLA reports by Day 5 | Report delivery confirmations | Monthly | 1% per late report, capped at 5% |
| Change Window Adherence | ≥ 99% adherence to CAB-approved changes | Change control logs | Monthly | 1% if below target |

Notes:  
- Exclusions: Planned maintenance (with 7 days’ notice), emergency maintenance (with 24 hours’ notice), Customer-caused outages, force majeure.  
- Chronic Failure: Three (3) consecutive months or four (4) months in any rolling twelve (12) below target for the same metric constitutes material breach, enabling termination for cause under Section 16.

## 15. Audit, Assessment, and Reporting
15.1 Audit Rights. No more than once annually (and additionally after a material Security Incident), Customer or its independent auditor may audit Vendor’s compliance on reasonable notice, during business hours, without undue disruption.  
15.2 Remediation. Vendor shall promptly remedy material deficiencies identified and provide a corrective action plan with timelines.  
15.3 Certifications and Reports. Vendor will provide current ISO 27001 certificate, summary of SOA, pen test executive summaries, SOC 2 Type II report (if available), and vulnerability summary reports under NDA.

## 16. Termination and Transition
16.1 Termination for Convenience. Either Party may terminate Services or an SOW for convenience with thirty (30) days’ prior written notice after the initial term specified in the SOW.  
16.2 Termination for Cause. Either Party may terminate immediately upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure within thirty (30) days (ten (10) days for undisputed payment defaults).  
16.3 Insolvency. Either Party may terminate upon written notice if the other becomes insolvent, enters bankruptcy, or ceases business operations.  
16.4 Effect of Termination. Upon termination, Vendor shall cease Services, invoice any accrued, undisputed fees, and return or delete Customer Data per Section 6.7.  
16.5 Transition Assistance. For up to ninety (90) days post-termination (or as agreed), Vendor will provide reasonable transition assistance, including knowledge transfer, handover of runbooks, and data export at rates not to exceed those in the SOW.

## 17. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
17.1 Escalation. Disputes will be escalated to the governance committee (Section 20). If unresolved within fifteen (15) business days, the Parties will proceed to mediation.  
17.2 Mediation. Non-binding mediation shall occur in [City, State/Country] with a mutually agreed mediator.  
17.3 Venue; Governing Law. If mediation fails, disputes shall be resolved by [binding arbitration under the rules of [Arbitration Body]] or [exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of [Jurisdiction]], governed by the laws of [Governing Law Jurisdiction], excluding conflict-of-law principles.  
17.4 Injunctive Relief. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking urgent injunctive or equitable relief to protect Confidential Information or IP.

## 18. Force Majeure
18.1 Neither Party is liable for delays or failures due to events beyond reasonable control, including natural disasters, war, terrorism, labor disputes, government actions, or widespread outages (“Force Majeure”). The affected Party shall notify the other and use diligent efforts to mitigate impact and resume performance.

## 19. Notices
19.1 Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, overnight courier, or email with confirmation to the addresses set forth in the SOW or as updated by notice.

## 20. Governance and Key Stakeholders
20.1 Stakeholders. The governance structure includes at minimum:  
  1) Customer: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); IT Operations Manager; Compliance Officer; Legal Department; Procurement Team.  
  2) Vendor: Account Executive; Service Delivery Manager; SOC Manager; Security Architect; Privacy Officer.  
20.2 Meetings.  
  1) Weekly operational reviews (tickets, incidents, changes).  
  2) Monthly service reviews (SLAs, KPIs, risk register, improvement plan).  
  3) Quarterly executive steering meetings (strategy, roadmap, contractual and commercial matters).  
20.3 RACI. Incident response and change control RACI matrices will be included in the SOW and maintained jointly.

## 21. Change Management
21.1 Changes to scope, deliverables, or assumptions require a mutually signed Change Order specifying impact on fees, timeline, and SLAs.  
21.2 Emergency changes affecting security posture shall be promptly communicated and documented post-implementation.

## 22. Acceptance and Milestones
22.1 Acceptance Criteria. Deliverables will be deemed accepted upon the earlier of: (a) Customer’s written acceptance; or (b) ten (10) business days after delivery without documented rejection specifying nonconformities.  
22.2 Re-performance. Vendor will remediate nonconformities within a reasonable period (not to exceed fifteen (15) business days) and resubmit for acceptance.  
22.3 Milestone Payments. Payment is tied to milestone acceptance as specified in the SOW, subject to retention under Section 4.3.

## 23. Ethics and Anti-Corruption
23.1 Vendor shall comply with anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws (including FCPA and UK Bribery Act), maintain accurate books and records, and avoid conflicts of interest.  
23.2 Gifts and Hospitality. Vendor will not offer anything of value to Customer employees to improperly influence decisions.

## 24. Export and Sanctions
24.1 Vendor will not provide Services in violation of export control or sanctions laws and will screen against restricted party lists.  
24.2 Customer shall not export or re-export any Vendor technology contrary to applicable law.

## 25. Miscellaneous
25.1 Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other’s consent, except to an Affiliate or successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee assumes all obligations.  
25.2 Independent Contractors. The Parties are independent contractors.  
25.3 Entire Agreement; Amendments. This Agreement, including SOWs and addenda, constitutes the entire agreement and may be amended only in a signed writing.  
25.4 Severability; Waiver. If any provision is unenforceable, the remainder remains in effect. No waiver is effective unless in writing.  
25.5 Publicity. Vendor shall not use Customer’s name or marks without prior written consent, except as required by law.

# Regulatory and Standards Compliance Matrix

## 1. Mandatory and Applicable Standards
| Requirement | Source | Applicability | Compliance Status | Evidence/Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 27001 certification | RFP Requirement | Mandatory | Compliant | Current certificate and SOA provided annually |
| 24/7 SOC monitoring | RFP Requirement | Mandatory | Compliant | SOC staffing model and coverage schedule |
| SIEM implementation | RFP Requirement | Mandatory | Compliant | SIEM architecture, parsing, correlation rules |
| Incident response ≤ 1 hour | RFP Requirement | Mandatory | Compliant | IR playbooks; SLA metric defined |
| GDPR/UK GDPR | If processing EU/UK Personal Data | Conditional | Compliant | DPA; SCCs; 72-hour breach notification |
| CCPA/CPRA | If processing CA residents’ data | Conditional | Compliant | No sale/share; CPRA addendum; consumer rights support |
| HIPAA | If PHI in scope | Conditional | Compliant | Business Associate Agreement; HIPAA safeguards |
| PCI DSS | If cardholder data in scope | Conditional | Compliant | ROC/AoC if applicable; segmentation |
| NIST CSF alignment | Best Practice | Recommended | Compliant | Policy mappings and CSF profile |
| SOC 2 Type II | Best Practice | Recommended | Compliant/Planned | Report under NDA when available |
| Export controls/sanctions | Legal | Mandatory | Compliant | Screening and export controls program |

## 2. Payment and Commercial Terms Compliance
| Requirement | Source | Applicability | Compliance Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Net 30 after invoice approval | Contract Baseline | Mandatory | Compliant | Invoicing per SOW |
| Milestone-based payments | Contract Baseline | Mandatory | Compliant | Acceptance criteria in Section 22 |
| 10% retention until completion | Contract Baseline | Mandatory | Compliant | Released at final acceptance |

# Data Protection and Privacy Addendum (Summary)

## 1. Roles and Processing Details
1.1 Roles. Customer is Controller; Vendor is Processor.  
1.2 Subject Matter and Duration. Managed SOC/SIEM services for the Term.  
1.3 Nature and Purpose. Monitoring, detection, response, and reporting.  
1.4 Categories of Data Subjects. Customer employees, contractors, and users; possibly customers or end-users.  
1.5 Categories of Personal Data. Identifiers, contact details, user IDs, IPs, device telemetry, log data; no special categories unless expressly authorized.  
1.6 Instructions. Vendor shall process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Customer.

## 2. Processor Obligations
2.1 Confidentiality and Training of personnel.  
2.2 Security Measures per Section 6 and Annex (on request).  
2.3 Subprocessor engagement and notice per Section 6.5.  
2.4 Assistance with data subject requests, DPIAs, and breach notifications.  
2.5 Deletion or return of Personal Data upon termination.  
2.6 Records of processing; audits per Section 15.

## 3. International Transfers
3.1 Standard Contractual Clauses and supplementary measures used where required.  
3.2 Data localization as agreed in the SOW.

## 4. Breach Management
4.1 Notify Customer without undue delay; include scope, impact, measures taken, and contact point.  
4.2 Cooperate with investigations, regulators, and notifications.

# Service Level Schedule (Detailed)

## 1. Severity Definitions
1.1 P1 (Critical): Active compromise, widespread outage, or imminent threat to regulated data.  
1.2 P2 (High): Serious security event with limited scope or elevated risk requiring prompt action.  
1.3 P3 (Medium): Non-urgent security issue; routine request.  
1.4 P4 (Low): Informational request or minor issue.

## 2. Response and Resolution Targets
2.1 Acknowledge P1 within 15 minutes; triage start within 1 hour; containment target within 4 hours; eradication and recovery per RCA plan.  
2.2 P2 acknowledge within 30 minutes; triage start within 1 hour; resolution target within 8 hours.  
2.3 P3 acknowledge within 4 business hours; resolution per change window.  
2.4 P4 acknowledge within 1 business day; resolution as scheduled.

## 3. Maintenance Windows
3.1 Planned Maintenance: Weekly standard window with seven (7) days’ notice; not to exceed four (4) hours/month.  
3.2 Emergency Maintenance: As needed with at least twenty-four (24) hours’ notice where practicable.

## 4. Reporting and Reviews
4.1 Monthly operational report: incidents, trends, vulnerabilities, patch status, SLA metrics.  
4.2 Quarterly security posture review: risk register, control maturity, roadmap, and improvement plan.

# Termination and Dispute Resolution

## 1. Termination Rights (Summary)
1.1 Convenience: 30 days’ notice after initial term.  
1.2 Cause: Material breach uncured within cure period; insolvency events; chronic SLA failure.  
1.3 Effects: Wind-down, data return/deletion, service credits reconciliation, and transition assistance up to 90 days.

## 2. Dispute Resolution (Summary)
2.1 Escalation to stakeholder governance.  
2.2 Mediation in [City, State/Country].  
2.3 Arbitration or court as designated; governing law of [Jurisdiction].  
2.4 Equitable relief preserved.

# Liability and Indemnification (Detailed)

## 1. Caps and Carve-Outs
1.1 Cap: Fees paid/payable in prior 12 months.  
1.2 Carve-outs: Confidentiality breaches, IP infringement, data protection obligations for Vendor-caused Security Incidents, fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, bodily injury, or tangible property damage.  
1.3 No indirect damages except for Excluded Claims.

## 2. Third-Party Claims
2.1 Vendor defends IP, data breach, and bodily injury/property claims as set forth in Section 10.  
2.2 Customer defends claims arising from Customer Data or instructions.

# Compliance Implementation Plan

## 1. Onboarding and Mobilization
1.1 Kickoff with governance stakeholders (CISO, IT Ops, Compliance, Legal, Procurement).  
1.2 Finalize runbooks, playbooks, RACI, and escalation paths.  
1.3 SIEM onboarding: data sources, parsing, correlation rules, and tuning.

## 2. Security Hardening and Testing
2.1 Baseline hardening standards applied; vulnerability scan and remediation plan.  
2.2 Pen test schedule and remediation tracking.

## 3. Continuous Compliance
3.1 ISO 27001 surveillance audits; evidence collection cadence.  
3.2 Monthly compliance dashboard; quarterly audits readiness review.

# Exhibits and Schedules
- Exhibit A: Statement(s) of Work (SOW) with milestones, fees, and acceptance criteria.  
- Exhibit B: Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and SCCs (if applicable).  
- Exhibit C: Security Controls Annex (detailed technical measures).  
- Exhibit D: SLA Measurement Methodology and Reporting Templates.  
- Exhibit E: Subprocessor List and Change Notification Process.  
- Exhibit F: Change Control Procedure and CAB Charter.

End of Document.

# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Definitions
1.1 “Agreement” means the master agreement, this RFP response, and all incorporated documents, including Statements of Work (SOWs), SLAs, and Data Processing Addendum (DPA).  
1.2 “Customer” means the entity issuing the RFP.  
1.3 “Provider” means the responding service provider delivering the Services.  
1.4 “Services” means 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation and operations, and incident response services as described in the Scope.  
1.5 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by either party, including security, technical, operational, commercial, and personal data.  
1.6 “Personal Data” means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, as defined by applicable data protection laws.  
1.7 “Security Incident” means any actual or suspected compromise of the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Customer’s systems or data under Provider’s control.  
1.8 “Personal Data Breach” has the meaning under GDPR Article 4(12) or analogous law.  
1.9 “Deliverables” means any configurations, documentation, reports, playbooks, detections, and other outputs produced under this Agreement.  
1.10 “Work Product” means Deliverables excluding Provider Background IP and Third-Party Materials.  
1.11 “Background IP” means IP owned or controlled by a party prior to or outside the scope of this Agreement.  
1.12 “Stakeholders” means Customer’s CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal Department, and Procurement Team.

## 2. Scope of Services
2.1 Provider will deliver:
1) 24/7/365 SOC monitoring by qualified analysts.  
2) SIEM implementation, tuning, correlation rule development, and ongoing operations.  
3) Incident response with initial engagement for Critical incidents within 1 hour of detection or Customer notification.  
4) Threat hunting, vulnerability and exposure monitoring, and security event triage.  
5) Monthly and quarterly reporting, executive briefings, and continuous improvement recommendations.  
6) Integration with ticketing and notification systems, and runbooks/playbooks aligned to NIST/ISO standards.

2.2 Provider will align controls with ISO/IEC 27001 (mandatory), NIST CSF/800-53 as applicable, and maintain an Information Security Management System (ISMS).

## 3. Contract Terms and Conditions
3.1 Term and Renewal  
1) Initial Term: [12–36] months from Effective Date.  
2) Renewal: Automatic 12-month renewals unless either party provides 60 days’ prior written notice.  
3) Pricing for renewal subject to annual uplift not to exceed [3%] unless otherwise agreed.

3.2 Fees, Payment, and Retention  
1) Invoices: Issued upon milestone acceptance or monthly in arrears for recurring services.  
2) Payment Terms: Net 30 days after invoice approval (mandatory per RFP).  
3) Milestones: Payments contingent upon achievement and Customer acceptance of milestones.  
4) Retention: 10% holdback on milestone/implementation fees until project completion and acceptance.  
5) Disputed Amounts: Must be raised within 10 business days of receipt; undisputed amounts remain payable. Parties will cooperate in good faith to resolve disputes within 20 business days.  
6) Taxes: Fees exclude taxes; Customer is responsible for applicable taxes other than Provider’s income taxes.  
7) Late Payment: The lesser of 1% per month or the maximum allowed by law on undisputed overdue balances.  
8) Suspension: Provider may suspend services for undisputed amounts overdue >30 days after written notice and a 10-day cure period, provided suspension does not compromise security posture; Provider will coordinate to minimize risk.

3.3 Acceptance  
1) Deliverables deemed accepted upon the earlier of (a) Customer’s written acceptance or (b) 10 business days after delivery absent written rejection specifying material nonconformities.  
2) Provider will remedy nonconformities without additional cost and resubmit for acceptance.

3.4 Change Control  
1) All changes to scope, deliverables, or timelines will be managed via a mutually agreed change order describing impact on cost, timeline, and risk.

3.5 Personnel, Subcontractors, and Background Checks  
1) Provider assigns appropriately skilled, background-screened personnel; replacements will be comparably qualified.  
2) Subcontractors require Customer’s prior written approval; Provider remains fully responsible.  
3) All personnel will adhere to Customer policies when on Customer premises or systems.

3.6 Governance and Reporting  
1) Steering: Quarterly governance meetings with Stakeholders (CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal, Procurement).  
2) Operational Cadence: Weekly/bi-weekly service reviews, monthly performance and SLA reports, and quarterly executive summaries.  
3) KPIs: As defined in the SLA.

3.7 Records and Audit  
1) Provider will maintain records of services, security controls, and processing activities for at least [7] years or as required by law.  
2) Subject to reasonable notice (≥10 business days) and confidentiality, Customer or its third-party auditor may audit Provider’s relevant facilities, controls, and records once annually or following a material Security Incident.  
3) Provider will provide current ISO 27001 certificate and SOC 2 Type II or equivalent reports upon request, with appropriate redactions.

3.8 Order of Precedence  
1) In case of conflict: (a) DPA and security addenda, (b) SOW, (c) this legal terms document, (d) Provider’s standard terms (if any), unless otherwise agreed.

## 4. Service Level Agreements (SLAs)
### 4.1 Metrics and Targets

| SLA Metric | Target/Threshold | Measurement Method | Measurement Window | Service Credit Trigger and Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOC Monitoring Coverage | 24/7/365 staffed coverage | Staffing schedules, duty rosters, and call logs | Monthly | Any unstaffed gap >15 minutes: 2% of monthly recurring fees (MRF) per occurrence, capped at 10% |
| SIEM Platform Availability | ≥ 99.90% uptime | Synthetic and real-user monitoring, excluding approved maintenance | Monthly | 99.0–99.89%: 5% MRF; 98.0–98.99%: 10% MRF; <98.0%: 15% MRF |
| Critical Incident Response Time | ≤ 1 hour to qualified analyst engagement (95th percentile) | Time from alert creation or Customer notification to analyst engagement | Monthly | For each 1% below 95% threshold: 2% MRF, capped at 10% |
| High Severity Triage | ≤ 4 hours to triage (95th percentile) | Ticket system timestamps | Monthly | 2% MRF if threshold missed |
| Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) | ≤ 15 minutes post-ingestion (median) | SIEM event and alert timestamps | Monthly | 2% MRF if exceeded |
| Mean Time to Contain (MTTC) for Critical | ≤ 4 hours (median) | IR case documentation | Monthly | 3% MRF if exceeded |
| Log Ingestion Lag | ≤ 5 minutes (95th percentile) | Pipeline telemetry | Monthly | 2% MRF if exceeded |
| Reporting Timeliness | Monthly reports within 5 business days of month-end; incident report within 72 hours of containment | Delivery timestamps | Monthly/Per-incident | 1% MRF per late report, up to 5% |

Notes:
- Total monthly credits capped at 20% MRF. Credits are Customer’s sole monetary remedy for SLA shortfalls, excluding breaches of confidentiality, data protection violations, or willful misconduct.
- Chronic Failure: 3 consecutive months or 4 months in any rolling 6-month period of SLA failure allows Customer to terminate affected services for cause without penalty and receive transition assistance.

### 4.2 Scheduled Maintenance and Exclusions
1) Maintenance: ≥72 hours’ notice for planned maintenance; maintenance windows not to exceed [4] hours per event and occur during off-peak hours where feasible.  
2) Exclusions: Force majeure, Customer-caused outages, Customer’s third-party failures (unless managed by Provider), and emergency security patching (with notice) are excluded from uptime calculations.

## 5. Data Protection and Privacy
5.1 Roles and Instructions  
1) Parties acknowledge Customer as Controller and Provider as Processor (or Service Provider under CCPA/CPRA).  
2) Provider will process Personal Data solely per Customer’s documented instructions and the DPA.

5.2 Legal Compliance  
1) Provider will comply with GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD, PIPEDA, and other applicable data protection laws.  
2) Provider will support Customer’s obligations, including record-keeping, DPIAs, and security assessments.

5.3 Security Controls  
1) Provider maintains an ISO/IEC 27001 certified ISMS; controls aligned to ISO 27002 and NIST CSF.  
2) Encryption: Data in transit via TLS 1.2+; data at rest with AES-256 or equivalent; managed key lifecycle; keys segregated from data where feasible.  
3) Access: MFA for administrative access; least privilege; role-based access control; quarterly access reviews; privileged access logging.  
4) Vulnerability Management: Authenticated scanning monthly; critical/high remediation within 15/30 days respectively; penetration tests at least annually.  
5) Segmentation and Hardening: Network segmentation, secure baselines, EDR on endpoints.  
6) BCP/DR: Documented plans with at least RTO ≤ 4 hours and RPO ≤ 15 minutes for SIEM/SOC tooling supporting the Services.

5.4 Incident and Breach Notification  
1) Security Incident: Initial notification to Customer within 1 hour of validation for incidents impacting Customer.  
2) Personal Data Breach: Notify Customer without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware; Provider to supply details required for regulatory notifications (GDPR 33/34) and assist with responses.  
3) Forensic Cooperation: Preserve evidence, provide incident report within 72 hours of containment, and support root cause analysis and corrective actions.

5.5 Data Subject Rights and Assistance  
1) Provider will promptly assist Customer in responding to data subject requests, regulatory inquiries, and DPIAs within legally required timeframes.

5.6 Data Location, Transfers, and Subprocessors  
1) Data Residency: Process data in approved regions agreed in the SOW.  
2) Cross-Border Transfers: Use appropriate safeguard mechanisms (e.g., EU Standard Contractual Clauses, UK IDTA/Addendum).  
3) Subprocessors: Maintain a current list; obtain Customer’s prior written approval for new subprocessors; flow down DPA obligations; provide at least 30 days’ notice for changes.

5.7 Retention and Deletion  
1) Retain Personal Data only as needed for Services or legal obligations; upon termination, securely delete or return data within 30 days, certifying deletion.

5.8 Confidentiality and Minimization  
1) Limit access to personnel with need-to-know, subject to confidentiality obligations; minimize collection and processing to what is necessary.

## 6. Security Requirements
6.1 Certifications and Attestations  
1) ISO/IEC 27001 certification (mandatory), annually renewed; provide certificate and SoA.  
2) SOC 2 Type II or equivalent upon request.  
3) Evidence of continuous monitoring and security testing.

6.2 Logging and Monitoring  
1) Centralized log collection; time-synchronized; retention: hot logs ≥ 12 months, archived ≥ 7 years (unless otherwise agreed).  
2) Tamper-evident storage for security logs; access logged and reviewed.

6.3 Secure Engineering and Change Management  
1) Secure SDLC for any custom content; peer review of detection logic; change approvals; back-out plans.  
2) Infrastructure changes tracked with tickets; emergency changes reviewed within 24 hours post-implementation.

6.4 Personnel Security  
1) Background checks consistent with local law; mandatory security awareness and role-based training at least annually.

6.5 Supply Chain  
1) Third-party risk assessments for critical suppliers; contractual security flow-downs; software integrity verification.

## 7. Intellectual Property Rights
7.1 Ownership  
1) Customer Materials remain Customer’s property.  
2) Provider Background IP remains Provider’s property.  
3) Work Product: Upon full payment, Customer owns Work Product created specifically for Customer, excluding Background IP and Third-Party Materials.

7.2 License to Background IP  
1) Provider grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use, copy, modify, and create derivative works of Provider Background IP solely as embedded in or necessary to use the Work Product.

7.3 Third-Party Materials and OSS  
1) Provider will disclose third-party components and comply with license terms; no copyleft obligations will be imposed on Customer’s systems or proprietary materials.  
2) Provider will manage OSS notices and provide SBOMs where feasible.

7.4 Feedback and Trademarks  
1) Customer grants Provider a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Feedback to improve services, without disclosing Customer Confidential Information.  
2) Use of either party’s name or marks requires prior written consent.

## 8. Liability, Indemnification, and Insurance
8.1 Indemnification by Provider  
Provider will defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its affiliates, and their officers, directors, and employees from third-party claims, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) arising from:  
1) Alleged infringement or misappropriation by the Services or Deliverables (excluding Customer-provided specifications).  
2) Provider’s breach of confidentiality or data protection obligations; Security Incidents caused by Provider’s failure to comply with this Agreement or applicable law.  
3) Bodily injury or tangible property damage caused by Provider’s negligence or willful misconduct.  
4) Provider’s violation of applicable law (including data protection and anti-bribery laws).

8.2 Customer Indemnification  
Customer will indemnify Provider against third-party claims arising from Customer-provided materials or instructions that violate law or infringe IP, except to the extent caused by Provider.

8.3 Infringement Remedies  
If the Services or Deliverables are alleged to infringe, Provider will, at its expense and option: (1) procure rights to continue use; (2) modify to be non-infringing without material reduction of functionality; or (3) replace with equivalent functionality. If none are commercially reasonable, Customer may terminate the affected Services and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

8.4 Limitation of Liability  
1) Cap: Except for Exclusions, each party’s aggregate liability arising out of or related to the Agreement will not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer for the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to liability.  
2) Exclusions: The cap does not apply to (a) indemnification obligations; (b) breach of confidentiality; (c) data protection violations resulting from a party’s failure to comply with this Agreement; (d) gross negligence or willful misconduct; (e) amounts owed for fees.  
3) No Consequential Damages: Neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, punitive, or consequential damages, or lost profits, revenue, or data, except to the extent such damages are payable to a third party under an indemnified claim.

8.5 Insurance  
Provider will maintain throughout the Term:  
1) Commercial General Liability: ≥ USD $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate.  
2) Technology E&O/Professional Liability: ≥ USD $2,000,000 per claim and aggregate.  
3) Cyber Liability (including privacy, network security, incident response, regulatory defense, and media): ≥ USD $5,000,000 per claim and aggregate.  
4) Workers’ Compensation/Employer’s Liability: As required by law.  
Certificates of insurance will be provided upon request; Customer may be named as additional insured where applicable.

## 9. Regulatory and Standards Compliance
9.1 Mandatory Standards  
1) ISO/IEC 27001: Provider maintains certification.  
2) Alignment with NIST CSF and, where relevant, NIST SP 800-53, PCI DSS (if card data is processed), HIPAA (if PHI is processed), GLBA (if financial data), and SOX support upon request.

9.2 Legal and Ethical Compliance  
1) Data Protection Laws: GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD, PIPEDA as applicable.  
2) Export/Trade: U.S. and international export control and sanctions laws (e.g., EAR, OFAC).  
3) Anti-Bribery/Corruption: FCPA, UK Bribery Act, and analogous local laws.  
4) Human Rights/Modern Slavery: Compliance with applicable modern slavery and human trafficking laws.  
5) Accessibility and Non-Discrimination: Compliance with applicable accessibility and equal opportunity laws for provided user interfaces and documentation.

## 10. Termination and Transition
10.1 Termination for Cause  
1) Either party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days of written notice.  
2) Immediate termination for insolvency, bankruptcy, or unlawful conduct.

10.2 Termination for Convenience  
1) Customer may terminate for convenience upon 30 days’ written notice; Customer will pay for Services rendered up to the effective termination date and reasonable, pre-approved demobilization costs.  
2) Provider may terminate for convenience only upon 90 days’ notice and must provide transition assistance as below; no termination during active incident response except by mutual consent.

10.3 Transition Assistance  
1) Up to 90 days of transition support at contracted rates to ensure orderly handover, including data export in commonly used formats, knowledge transfer, runbooks, and open issue remediation.  
2) Provider will return or securely destroy Customer data and certify deletion within 30 days.

10.4 Effect of Termination  
1) Accrued rights and obligations survive; sections on confidentiality, data protection, IP, liability, and dispute resolution survive termination.

## 11. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
11.1 Escalation  
1) Operational leads confer; if unresolved within 10 business days, escalate to executive sponsors; if unresolved within 20 business days, proceed to mediation.

11.2 Mediation and Arbitration/Court  
1) Non-binding mediation in [City, State/Country].  
2) If unresolved within 30 days post-mediation, disputes will be resolved by [binding arbitration under AAA Rules/courts of competent jurisdiction] in [Venue], under the laws of [Governing Law Jurisdiction], excluding conflict of law rules.  
3) Injunctive Relief: Either party may seek injunctive or equitable relief to protect IP or Confidential Information without first pursuing mediation/arbitration.

## 12. Confidentiality
12.1 Each party will protect the other’s Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own (and no less than reasonable care).  
12.2 Disclosure only to personnel and subcontractors with a need to know and under confidentiality obligations.  
12.3 Exclusions: Information that is public, independently developed, or rightfully received from a third party without duty of confidentiality.  
12.4 Compelled Disclosure: Allowed to the extent required by law with prompt notice to seek protective orders.  
12.5 Survival: 5 years post-termination, or longer where trade secrets or personal data are involved.

## 13. Compliance Matrix (Key RFP Requirements)

| Requirement | Commitment | Evidence/Control | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24/7 SOC Monitoring | Continuous staffed monitoring | Staffing rosters, on-call schedules, escalation matrix | Compliant |
| SIEM Implementation | Architecture, deployment, tuning, correlation rules | SIEM design docs, runbooks, change records | Compliant |
| Incident Response Within 1 Hour | Critical incident engagement ≤ 1 hour (95th percentile) | Ticket and alert timestamps, SLA reports | Compliant |
| ISO/IEC 27001 Compliance | Maintain certification; provide certificate and SoA | Current ISO certificate, surveillance audit reports | Compliant |
| Net 30 Payment After Approval | Adhere to Customer payment terms | Contract clause and invoicing process | Compliant |
| Performance Milestones Required for Payment | Milestone-based acceptance and payment | SOW milestones and acceptance criteria | Compliant |
| 10% Retention Until Completion | Retain 10% on implementation fees until acceptance | Contract clause and invoice detail | Compliant |

## 14. Warranties
14.1 Services Warranty: Provider warrants Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, consistent with industry standards.  
14.2 Compliance Warranty: Provider warrants ongoing compliance with applicable laws, this Agreement, and ISO 27001.  
14.3 Malware and Backdoor Warranty: Deliverables will be free of time bombs, backdoors, and known malware at delivery.  
14.4 No High-Risk Software Warranty: No code or content will intentionally degrade Customer systems.  
14.5 Disclaimer: Except as expressly stated, Services are provided “as is” to the extent permitted by law; no implied warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, or non-infringement.

## 15. Notices
15.1 Notices sent to the contacts designated by each party in the SOW, via email with confirmation, reputable courier, or certified mail.  
15.2 Notice Addresses:  
- Customer: [Name/Title, Address, Email]  
- Provider: [Name/Title, Address, Email]  
- With copies to Legal for both parties.

## 16. Publicity and References
16.1 No use of the other party’s name, logo, or trademarks in marketing without prior written consent.  
16.2 Case studies and references require Customer approval.

## 17. Assignment
17.1 Neither party may assign the Agreement without the other’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, except to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets with notice.  
17.2 Any prohibited assignment is void.

## 18. Non-Solicitation
18.1 During the Term and for 6 months thereafter, neither party will solicit for employment the other party’s personnel who directly provided or oversaw the Services, except via general advertisements.

## 19. Force Majeure
19.1 Neither party is liable for failure to perform due to events beyond reasonable control (including natural disasters, war, terrorism, labor disputes, widespread internet outages) provided it uses reasonable efforts to mitigate and resumes performance promptly.

## 20. Severability; Waiver; Entire Agreement; Counterparts
20.1 If any provision is invalid, the remainder remains in effect; parties will replace invalid terms with lawful ones closest to original intent.  
20.2 Failure to enforce is not a waiver.  
20.3 This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement regarding the subject matter and supersedes prior understandings.  
20.4 May be executed in counterparts and via electronic signature.

## 21. Exhibit A – SLA Service Credit Claim Procedure
1) Customer to submit claim within 30 days after month-end with supporting evidence.  
2) Provider will validate within 15 business days; approved credits applied to next invoice.  
3) Disputed claims handled under Dispute Resolution.

## 22. Exhibit B – Data Processing Addendum (Summary)
1) Subject Matter: Processing Personal Data for SOC/SIEM/IR services.  
2) Duration: Term of the Agreement plus certified deletion period.  
3) Nature and Purpose: Monitoring, detection, response, and reporting.  
4) Categories of Data: Logs, security telemetry, user identifiers, system metadata; no intentional processing of special categories unless explicitly authorized.  
5) Data Subjects: Customer employees, contractors, users, and other individuals present in logs.  
6) Security Measures: As specified in Section 5 and Provider’s technical and organizational measures (TOMs).  
7) Subprocessors: Listed at [URL/Annex]; notice and objection process included.  
8) International Transfers: SCCs/IDTA as applicable with transfer impact assessments.  
9) Assistance: Data subject requests, DPIAs, breach notifications, and regulator inquiries.  
10) Deletion/Return: As per Section 5.7, with certification.

## 23. Exhibit C – Governance and Reporting Cadence
1) Weekly/Bi-weekly operations meeting: Tickets, alerts, rules tuning, backlog, and changes.  
2) Monthly service review: SLA performance, incidents, improvements, and risk register.  
3) Quarterly executive review: Strategy, metrics trends, roadmap, and budget alignment.  
4) Stakeholders: CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal, and Procurement.

## 24. Exhibit D – Optional Add-On Services
1) Purple teaming and adversary emulation.  
2) Threat modeling and tabletop exercises.  
3) Extended detection and response (XDR) integration.  
4) Cloud posture management and IaC security reviews.

End of Legal Terms and Compliance.
