# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Parties, Scope, and Structure
1.1 Parties. These terms govern the provision of cybersecurity monitoring, SIEM implementation, and incident response services (the “Services”) by [Provider Legal Name] (“Provider”) to [Customer Legal Name] (“Customer”) pursuant to the RFP and resulting contract documents.  
1.2 Scope. The Services include: (a) 24/7/365 SOC monitoring; (b) SIEM platform implementation, configuration, and content development; (c) incident detection, triage, and response with a 1-hour engagement target for critical incidents; and (d) related professional services as set forth in the Statement(s) of Work (“SOW”).  
1.3 Contract Documents. The contract consists of, in order of precedence: (1) the Master Services Agreement (MSA); (2) the Data Processing Agreement (DPA); (3) the SOW(s); (4) the Service Level Agreement (SLA); (5) the RFP and addenda; (6) Provider’s proposal; and (7) any Purchase Orders (collectively, the “Agreement”).  
1.4 Stakeholders and Governance. Governance will include representation from: Customer’s CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal Department, and Procurement Team, and Provider’s Delivery Manager and Security Lead.

## 2. Definitions
2.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by a Party that is designated confidential or reasonably should be understood as confidential.  
2.2 “Controller,” “Processor,” “Personal Data,” “Processing,” and “Data Subject” have the meanings given under applicable data protection laws.  
2.3 “Deliverables” means reports, configurations, rules, dashboards, runbooks, and other work products developed for Customer under an SOW.  
2.4 “Force Majeure Event” means an event beyond a Party’s reasonable control.  
2.5 “Incident” means a confirmed or suspected compromise, disruption, or unauthorized access requiring security response activities.  
2.6 “Monthly Recurring Charge (MRC)” means recurring fees for managed services.  
2.7 “Scheduled Maintenance” means maintenance windows agreed in advance that may affect service availability.  
2.8 “SIEM” means security information and event management platform as specified in the SOW.  
2.9 “SOC” means security operations center providing monitoring and response services.  
2.10 “SLA Credit” means a service credit applied to the MRC for verified SLA nonconformance.

## 3. Term, Delivery, and Acceptance
3.1 Term. The initial term is [36] months from Effective Date, with [12]-month auto-renewals unless either Party gives 60 days’ prior written notice of non-renewal.  
3.2 Delivery. Provider will deliver Services per the agreed project plan and SOW milestones.  
3.3 Acceptance. Customer will have 10 business days to accept or reject each milestone Deliverable with written, specific reasons for any rejection. Provider will remediate within a commercially reasonable period and resubmit for acceptance. Absent timely rejection, Deliverables are deemed accepted.  
3.4 Retention. A 10% retention applies to milestone payments and is released upon final project completion and acceptance of all Deliverables.

## 4. Fees, Invoicing, and Payment
4.1 Fees. Fees are as set forth in the SOW, including one-time implementation fees and MRC for managed services.  
4.2 Invoicing. Provider will invoice upon milestone acceptance (for project fees) and monthly in arrears for MRC, unless otherwise stated in the SOW.  
4.3 Payment Terms. Net 30 days after invoice approval by Customer.  
4.4 Milestone Performance. Payment is contingent on achievement of performance milestones per the SOW.  
4.5 Taxes and Expenses. Fees exclude taxes, which will be itemized. Pre-approved, reasonable travel and out-of-pocket expenses will be invoiced at cost.  
4.6 Disputed Invoices. Customer must notify Provider of bona fide disputes within 10 business days of receipt with details; undisputed amounts remain payable.  
4.7 Late Payment. Late amounts may accrue interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum allowed by law.  
4.8 Price Changes. MRC is fixed for the initial term, except for mutually agreed changes or usage-based overages specified in the SOW.

## 5. Service Levels and Performance Management
5.1 General. Provider will operate a 24/7/365 SOC, implement and manage the SIEM, and deliver incident response (IR) services consistent with ISO/IEC 27001.  
5.2 Severity Definitions.  
1) Severity 1 (Critical): Active compromise or outage causing material business impact.  
2) Severity 2 (High): Significant degradation or elevated risk without confirmed compromise.  
3) Severity 3 (Medium): Limited impact or potential issue.  
4) Severity 4 (Low): Informational or routine service request.  
5.3 Measurement. Unless stated otherwise, measurements are monthly, exclude Scheduled Maintenance, Customer-caused issues, and Force Majeure Events, and are derived from Provider’s monitoring systems and ticketing data, available to Customer upon request.  
5.4 Service Credits. Credits are calculated as a percentage of the monthly fee for the impacted service, capped at 15% of the total MRC per month. Credits are Customer’s exclusive monetary remedy for SLA shortfalls, except for chronic failure as defined below.  
5.5 Chronic Failure. Three (3) consecutive months or four (4) months in any rolling six (6)-month period with SLA failure for the same metric constitutes chronic failure, permitting Customer to terminate the affected service for cause on 30 days’ notice if not cured.

### 5.6 SLA Metrics
| Metric | Target | Measurement Window | Evidence/Source | SLA Credit Trigger | Credit Amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOC Coverage | 24/7/365 (100%) | Monthly | Staffing schedules, ticketing | Any period without coverage > 30 min | 5% per event (cap 15%) |
| SIEM Platform Availability | ≥ 99.90% | Monthly | Uptime monitoring | < 99.90% >= 99.50% | 5% |
| SIEM Platform Availability |  |  |  | < 99.50% >= 99.00% | 10% |
| SIEM Platform Availability |  |  |  | < 99.00% | 15% |
| Event Ingestion Pipeline Availability | ≥ 99.90% | Monthly | Telemetry/log pipeline monitors | Same tiers as SIEM | Same credits as SIEM |
| Alert Acknowledgment (Sev 1) | ≤ 5 minutes | 95th percentile, monthly | Ticket timestamps | Any instance > 15 minutes | 2% per occurrence (cap 10%) |
| Alert Acknowledgment (Sev 2) | ≤ 15 minutes | 95th percentile | Ticket timestamps | Any instance > 30 minutes | 1% per occurrence (cap 10%) |
| IR Engagement (Sev 1) | IR Lead engaged ≤ 60 minutes from detection | Per incident | War room/ticket logs | Any instance > 60 minutes | 3% per occurrence (cap 10%) |
| MTTD for Critical Detections | ≤ 15 minutes from event generation | Monthly average | SIEM alerting data | Monthly average > 15 minutes | 5% |
| Time to Containment (Sev 1) | ≤ 4 hours from detection (when Customer grants access) | Per incident | Incident timeline | Any instance > 6 hours | 2% per occurrence (cap 10%) |
| Vulnerability Remediation (Critical CVSS ≥ 9) | ≤ 15 days (Provider-managed assets) | Per finding | Ticketing/scan reports | Any instance > 25 days | 2% per instance (cap 10%) |
| Reporting Delivery | Monthly executive report by 5th business day | Monthly | Report delivery receipts | Late by > 2 business days | 1% |

Notes: (a) IR timelines assume Customer provides necessary system access and decision-makers; (b) remediation SLAs apply only to Provider-managed systems as defined in the SOW; (c) maintenance windows will be coordinated at least 5 business days in advance.

## 6. Security and ISO 27001 Compliance
6.1 ISO 27001. Provider shall maintain ISO/IEC 27001 certification throughout the term, provide current certificates and SoA upon request, and notify Customer of any suspension or material nonconformity.  
6.2 Security Controls. Provider will implement and maintain controls aligned to ISO 27001 Annex A and industry practices, including:  
1) Identity and Access Management: MFA for privileged access; least privilege; quarterly access reviews.  
2) Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest; key management with separation of duties.  
3) Logging and Monitoring: Centralized log collection; time synchronization; tamper detection; retention per SOW (minimum 365 days searchable, 365 days archive unless otherwise specified).  
4) Vulnerability and Patch Management: Authenticated scanning monthly; critical patches within 15 days, high within 30 days, medium within 60 days.  
5) Secure Configuration: Baselines (CIS/NIST) with drift monitoring.  
6) Secure Development/Content: Peer-reviewed SIEM rules/runbooks with version control and change approval.  
7) Network Security: Segmentation, EDR/AV on managed endpoints, IDS/IPS as applicable.  
8) Physical Security: Data center security controls consistent with ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II where applicable.  
9) Business Continuity/DR: Documented BCDR with annual testing; target RTO ≤ 8 hours, RPO ≤ 1 hour for managed SIEM (unless otherwise in SOW).  
10) Personnel: Background checks as permitted by law; security training at hire and annually.

6.3 Incident Management. Provider will maintain an incident response plan with 24/7 on-call coverage, conduct tabletop exercises at least annually, and coordinate with Customer during incidents.  
6.4 Security Change Control. Material security changes require documented change requests and Customer approval where the change may materially impact risk.

## 7. Data Protection and Privacy (DPA)
7.1 Roles. For Personal Data in Customer logs and environments, Customer is the Controller and Provider is the Processor (or Service Provider/Processor under applicable laws).  
7.2 Instructions. Provider will process Personal Data solely on documented instructions from Customer and for the purposes of delivering the Services.  
7.3 Lawful Basis and Minimization. Customer determines lawful basis. Provider will minimize Personal Data processing to what is strictly necessary.  
7.4 Subprocessors. Provider may engage subprocessors for hosting, telemetry, and support subject to: (a) prior written notice and opportunity to object on reasonable grounds; (b) written contracts with equivalent data protection obligations; and (c) Provider’s liability for subprocessor acts/omissions.  
7.5 Cross-Border Transfers. Transfers will comply with applicable laws using recognized mechanisms (e.g., EU SCCs, UK IDTA/Addendum). Data residency requirements will be honored where specified in the SOW.  
7.6 Security Measures. Technical and organizational measures are described in Section 6 and Annex [Security Measures] and will be maintained and not materially reduced during the term.  
7.7 Data Subject Rights. Provider will assist Customer in responding to requests to access, correct, delete, restrict, or port Personal Data, within timelines required by law.  
7.8 Breach Notification. Provider will notify Customer without undue delay and in no event later than 24 hours after confirmation of a Personal Data Breach affecting Customer data, providing available details and regular updates until containment.  
7.9 Confidentiality. Personnel processing Personal Data are bound by confidentiality obligations.  
7.10 Records and Audits. Provider will maintain records of processing and, upon reasonable notice, make available audit reports (e.g., ISO certificate, SOC 2 report if available) and facilitate audits per Section 12.  
7.11 Return/Deletion. Upon termination or at Customer’s request, Provider will return Customer Data in a commonly used format and securely delete all copies within 30 days, subject to legal retention requirements and documented certificates of destruction.  
7.12 Government Requests. Provider will notify Customer of government or law enforcement requests unless legally prohibited and will challenge overbroad requests where reasonable.

## 8. Regulatory Compliance
8.1 General. Provider will comply with all applicable laws and regulations related to information security, privacy, sanctions, export controls, anti-bribery/anti-corruption, and labor.  
8.2 Standards Alignment. Provider’s controls align to ISO 27001 and, where applicable to Customer’s environment, NIST CSF and NIST SP 800-53 control families for monitoring and IR functions.  
8.3 Sectoral and Geographic Laws. As applicable and defined in the SOW or compliance profile: GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA (if PHI is processed), GLBA, SOX, PCI DSS for cardholder data, and local data retention laws.

### 8.4 Compliance Matrix
| Requirement/Standard | Applicability | Provider Status | Evidence | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 27001 | Mandatory | Certified | Certificate + SoA | Maintain throughout term |
| 24/7 SOC Monitoring | Mandatory | Compliant | Staffing and runbooks | Continuous coverage |
| SIEM Implementation | Mandatory | Compliant | Project plan, configs | Per SOW |
| Incident Response ≤ 1 hr (Sev 1 engage) | Mandatory | Compliant | Ticket/war room logs | See SLA 5.6 |
| NIST CSF | Recommended | Aligned | Control mapping | On request |
| SOC 2 Type II | If required | Available/Planned [Y/N] | SOC 2 report | If in scope |
| PCI DSS | If CHD | Upon request | AOC/ROC | Limited to in-scope systems |
| HIPAA | If PHI | Program in place | Policies/BAA | Execute BAA if applicable |
| GDPR/UK GDPR | If EEA/UK data | Compliant | DPA + SCCs | Data transfer mechanisms |
| CCPA/CPRA | If CA data | Service Provider | DPA Addendum | No sale/share of data |

## 9. Intellectual Property Rights
9.1 Background IP. Each Party retains ownership of its pre-existing IP and any improvements thereto.  
9.2 Deliverables. Upon full payment, Customer owns Deliverables specifically created for Customer, excluding Provider Tools.  
9.3 Provider Tools. Provider retains ownership of its methodologies, templates, rule libraries, correlation logic, playbooks, and software (“Provider Tools”). Provider grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Provider Tools solely as embedded in the Deliverables for Customer’s internal use.  
9.4 Open Source. Provider will comply with applicable open-source licenses and will not include copyleft code in Deliverables in a manner that subjects Customer’s systems to license obligations.  
9.5 Customer Data. Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; Provider’s use is limited to providing the Services.  
9.6 Feedback. Customer grants Provider a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use suggestions to improve services, without disclosing Customer Confidential Information.

## 10. Confidentiality
10.1 Obligations. Receiving Party will protect Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information with at least the same care it uses to protect its own confidential information, and not less than reasonable care, and use it solely to perform the Agreement.  
10.2 Exclusions. Confidential Information excludes information that is public, known without restriction before disclosure, independently developed, or rightfully received from a third party without duty of confidentiality.  
10.3 Compelled Disclosure. Receiving Party may disclose as required by law with prompt notice to Disclosing Party (if legally permitted) and reasonable cooperation.  
10.4 Injunctive Relief. Breach of confidentiality may cause irreparable harm; Disclosing Party may seek equitable relief in addition to other remedies.

## 11. Warranties
11.1 Services Warranty. Provider warrants Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards.  
11.2 Compliance Warranty. Provider warrants that it will comply with applicable laws and Section 6 security commitments.  
11.3 Non-Infringement. Provider warrants Deliverables and Provider Tools (as used in accordance with the Agreement) do not knowingly infringe third-party IP rights.  
11.4 Malware-Free. Deliverables will not intentionally include malicious code.  
11.5 Disclaimer. Except as expressly warranted, Services are provided “as is” and Provider disclaims implied warranties to the maximum extent permitted by law.  
11.6 Remedies. Provider will re-perform nonconforming Services or repair/replace nonconforming Deliverables; if unable to do so within a reasonable time, Customer may receive a refund of fees paid for the nonconforming Services/Deliverables.

## 12. Audit, Monitoring, and Reporting
12.1 Right to Audit. Upon 30 days’ notice and not more than annually (unless required by law or due to a verified incident), Customer may audit Provider’s compliance through: (a) review of third-party certifications and reports; (b) written responses to security questionnaires; and (c) on-site/virtual audits limited to systems and facilities relevant to Customer’s Services.  
12.2 Constraints. Audits must not unreasonably disrupt operations, must protect other customers’ confidentiality, and may be subject to reasonable facility rules.  
12.3 Remediation. Provider will address material findings within agreed timelines commensurate with risk, typically: critical ≤ 30 days; high ≤ 60 days.  
12.4 Reporting. Provider will provide: (a) daily or weekly SOC summaries; (b) monthly executive reports; (c) quarterly business reviews (QBRs) with KPI/KRI analysis.

## 13. Indemnification
13.1 By Provider. Provider will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging: (a) IP infringement by Deliverables or Provider Tools (as used in accordance with the Agreement); (b) bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Provider’s negligence or willful misconduct; and (c) Provider’s violation of applicable data protection laws resulting in a third-party claim.  
13.2 IP Remedies. If a Deliverable is alleged to infringe, Provider may procure a license, modify to be non-infringing without material loss of functionality, or replace with substantially equivalent functionality. If none are commercially reasonable, Customer may terminate the affected Service and receive a refund of prepaid, unused fees.  
13.3 By Customer. Customer will defend and indemnify Provider against third-party claims arising from Customer’s data, instructions, or use of the Services in violation of the Agreement.  
13.4 Procedure. The indemnified Party must provide prompt notice, reasonable cooperation, and grant control of the defense to the indemnifying Party, subject to approval of counsel (not unreasonably withheld). No settlement admitting fault or imposing obligations on the indemnified Party without consent.

## 14. Limitation of Liability
14.1 Cap. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party’s aggregate liability arising out of or related to the Agreement will not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer to Provider for the 12 months preceding the first claim.  
14.2 Excluded Claims. The above cap does not apply to: (a) breach of confidentiality; (b) IP infringement indemnity; (c) violation of data protection obligations resulting in a Personal Data Breach caused by Provider’s failure to comply with Section 7; (d) gross negligence or willful misconduct; or (e) amounts owed for fees.  
14.3 Exclusion of Certain Damages. Neither Party will be liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or loss of profits, revenues, or data, except to the extent such damages are awarded to a third party in a covered indemnity claim.  
14.4 Super Cap (Optional). For confirmed Personal Data Breaches caused by Provider, liability shall be capped at [2x] the amount in Section 14.1. [To be negotiated.]

## 15. Insurance
15.1 Coverage. Provider will maintain during the term:  
1) Commercial General Liability: $2,000,000 per occurrence.  
2) Professional/Technology E&O (including Network Security & Privacy): $5,000,000 aggregate.  
3) Cyber Liability (including incident response, notification, forensics, regulatory defense): $5,000,000 aggregate.  
4) Workers’ Compensation and Employers’ Liability: statutory/$1,000,000.  
5) Umbrella/Excess Liability: $5,000,000 aggregate.  
15.2 Proof. Certificates of insurance will be provided upon request; Customer may be named as additional insured where applicable.

## 16. Change Management
16.1 Change Control. Material changes to scope, SLAs, or fees require a written Change Request (CR) signed by both Parties.  
16.2 Emergency Changes. Provider may implement emergency changes to address security threats, notifying Customer promptly and documenting changes post-implementation.

## 17. Subcontracting and Personnel
17.1 Subcontractors. Provider may subcontract with prior written notice; Provider remains fully responsible for subcontractor performance.  
17.2 Personnel. Provider will assign qualified, background-checked personnel. Replacement of key personnel requires prior Customer approval and will be with personnel of equal or greater qualifications.  
17.3 Non-Solicitation. Neither Party will solicit employment of the other’s employees directly engaged under this Agreement during the term and for 6 months thereafter, excluding general solicitations.

## 18. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
18.1 Plans. Provider will maintain and annually test BCDR plans supporting SIEM and SOC services.  
18.2 Targets. Unless otherwise agreed, target RTO ≤ 8 hours and RPO ≤ 1 hour for managed SIEM and SOC case management systems.  
18.3 Communications. Provider will communicate material disruptions and restoration timelines to Customer within 2 hours of awareness.

## 19. Governance and Communications
19.1 Steering and Cadence.

## 20. Termination, Suspension, and Exit
20.1 Termination for Cause. Either Party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days of written notice (10 days for payment breaches).  
20.2 Termination for Convenience. Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 days’ written notice; Customer will pay for Services performed through the effective date and any non-cancellable commitments disclosed in advance.

20.4 Termination Assistance. For up to 60 days post-termination (at then-current rates), Provider will provide transition assistance, including data export, runbook handover, and knowledge transfer.  
20.5 Data Return/Deletion. As per Section 7.11, Customer Data will be returned and deleted with certification.  
20.6 Survival. Sections concerning payment obligations, confidentiality, IP, indemnities, limitations of liability, audit rights, and dispute resolution survive termination.

## 21. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
21.1 Good-Faith Negotiation. The Parties will escalate disputes to senior executives and negotiate in good faith for at least 15 days.  
21.2 Mediation. If unresolved, the Parties will attempt non-binding mediation with a mutually agreed mediator within 30 days.  
21.3 Venue. If still unresolved, disputes will be resolved by [binding arbitration administered by [Institution]] seated in [City, State/Country], or by courts located in [Venue], under the laws of [Governing Law State/Country], excluding conflict-of-law rules.

## 22. Miscellaneous
22.1 Order of Precedence. As stated in Section 1.3; conflicts are resolved by the highest-ranked document.  
22.2 Assignment. Neither Party may assign without the other’s consent, except to an Affiliate or in connection with a merger or sale of substantially all assets with notice.  
22.3 Independent Contractors. The Parties are independent contractors; no agency or partnership is created.  
22.4 Force Majeure. Neither Party is liable for delays due to Force Majeure Events; affected obligations are suspended for the duration of the event.  
22.5 Notices. Notices must be in writing and delivered to the addresses below or as updated by notice:  
- Customer: [Name/Title/Address/Email]  
- Provider: [Name/Title/Address/Email]  
22.6 Entire Agreement; Amendments. This Agreement is the entire understanding; amendments must be in writing and signed by both Parties.  
22.7 Severability; Waiver. Invalid provisions are severed; failure to enforce is not a waiver.  
22.8 Publicity. Neither Party may use the other’s name or marks without prior written consent, except as required by law.

# Service Level Agreement (Detailed)

## A. Severity and Response Matrix
1. Severity Classification will be assigned by the SOC based on business impact and risk, validated with Customer.  
2. Response activities include triage, containment guidance, eradication support, and recovery validation, with continuous updates in the incident ticket/war room.

## B. Service Credit Claims
1. Filing. Customer must file claims within 30 days of the end of the month with supporting evidence.  
2. Verification. Credits are applied to the next invoice after verification.  
3. Exclusivity. Credits are the sole monetary remedy for SLA breaches, except for chronic failure and Excluded Claims.

## C. Maintenance and Exclusions
1. Scheduled Maintenance: Up to [4] hours per month, during low-impact windows agreed at least 5 business days in advance.  
2. Emergency Maintenance: Notice provided as soon as practicable; reasonable efforts to minimize impact.  
3. Exclusions: Customer-caused outages; third-party failures outside Provider’s control; Force Majeure.

# Data Processing Agreement (Key Terms)

## A. Processing Details

## B. Technical and Organizational Measures (Annex Summary)

1.3 10% retention until project completion and final acceptance.

# Governance and Stakeholder Engagement

1.3 Compliance Officer: Regulatory alignment, audit coordination, and evidence reviews.  
1.4 Legal Department: Contract interpretation, DPA/BAA, and dispute management.  
1.5 Procurement Team: Commercial compliance, invoice approval, and retention tracking.

## 2. Reporting Cadence and Artifacts

2.2 Deliverables: Use cases catalog, detection coverage map, runbooks, asset onboarding lists, and architecture diagrams.

# Termination and Dispute Resolution

## 2. Dispute Steps

# Compliance Exhibits

# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Definitions
1.1 “Agreement” means the executed master agreement, together with all Statements of Work (SOWs), schedules, annexes, exhibits, and incorporated policies.  
1.2 “Customer” means the procuring entity identified in the RFP and any affiliates expressly included in scope.  
1.3 “Supplier” means the proposing vendor and its permitted affiliates and subcontractors.  
1.4 “Services” means the professional, managed, hosted, or support services described in the SOW(s).  
1.5 “Deliverables” means any reports, software configurations, documents, or other work product produced under the Agreement.  
1.6 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by either party that is identified as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential.  
1.7 “Personal Data” means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, as defined by applicable data protection laws.  
1.8 “Security Incident” means any confirmed unauthorized access to, or acquisition of, Customer Data or systems in Supplier’s control, excluding unsuccessful attempts or activities that do not compromise data.  
1.9 “Availability” means the percentage of time the production service is usable by end-users, excluding Scheduled Maintenance.  
1.10 “SLA” means the service level commitments and related credits set forth herein.

## 2. Contract Terms and Conditions
2.1 Scope and SOWs  
(1) The Services and Deliverables are defined in one or more SOWs.  
(2) Each SOW specifies scope, milestones, acceptance criteria, fees, timelines, and dependencies.  
(3) Conflicts among documents are resolved per the Order of Precedence.

2.2 Order of Precedence  
(1) The following order applies unless a document expressly states otherwise: (a) Change Orders; (b) DPA and Information Security Addendum; (c) Master Agreement; (d) SOW(s); (e) RFP and clarifications; (f) Supplier proposal; (g) Supplier policies referenced.  
(2) Where mandatory law requires otherwise, such law prevails.

2.3 Term and Renewal  
(1) The initial term and renewal periods are specified in the Master Agreement or SOW.  
(2) Auto-renewal occurs unless either party gives written non-renewal notice at least 60 days prior to term end.

2.4 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes  
(1) Fees are as stated in the SOW; time-and-materials (T&M) billed monthly in arrears; fixed fee per milestone or schedule.  
(2) Payment terms: net 30 days from undisputed invoice receipt.  
(3) Supplier will itemize taxes; Customer is responsible for applicable sales/use/VAT except on Supplier’s income.  
(4) No charge for travel unless pre-approved in writing; travel billed at actual cost in accordance with Customer policy where applicable.  
(5) Withholding tax gross-up handled per applicable law and treaty relief procedures.

2.5 Changes and Governance  
(1) Changes are managed via written Change Orders signed by both parties.  
(2) A joint governance committee will review performance, risks, and improvements at least quarterly.  
(3) Key Personnel require Customer approval; replacements must be of equal or greater qualifications.

2.6 Acceptance  
(1) Deliverables are subject to acceptance testing against SOW criteria.  
(2) Customer will accept, reject with reasons, or request remediation within the review period (typically 10–15 business days).  
(3) Silence after the review period constitutes deemed acceptance only where Deliverables materially conform to criteria.

2.7 Warranties  
(1) Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards.  
(2) Deliverables will materially conform to the SOW and documentation for 90 days post-acceptance.  
(3) Supplier warrants it holds all necessary rights to grant licenses herein and that Deliverables do not knowingly infringe third-party IP.  
(4) Supplier will comply with applicable laws and obtain required permits and licenses.  
(5) EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED, NO OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

2.8 Subcontracting and Personnel  
(1) Supplier may use subcontractors with Customer’s prior written consent for material portions of work.  
(2) Supplier remains fully responsible for subcontractor performance.  
(3) Background checks will be conducted in accordance with law for personnel with access to Customer facilities or sensitive data.

2.9 Confidentiality  
(1) Each party will protect the other’s Confidential Information using no less than reasonable care.  
(2) Disclosure is limited to personnel with a need to know, bound by confidentiality obligations.  
(3) Exclusions include information that is public, independently developed, or rightfully received without duty of confidentiality.  
(4) Compelled disclosure permitted with prompt notice and cooperation in seeking protective measures.  
(5) Upon termination, Confidential Information will be returned or securely destroyed, except for archival copies maintained under legal hold.

2.10 Insurance  
(1) Supplier will maintain:  
    (a) Commercial General Liability: USD 2,000,000 per occurrence;  
    (b) Professional/Technology E&O: USD 2,000,000 per claim;  
    (c) Cyber Liability (including privacy, breach response, network security, media liability): USD 5,000,000 aggregate;  
    (d) Workers’ Compensation/Employer’s Liability as required by law;  
    (e) Automobile Liability (if on-site travel): USD 1,000,000 combined single limit.  
(2) Certificates of insurance provided upon request; Customer named as additional insured where customary for CGL; waiver of subrogation where permitted.

2.11 Records, Audit, and Inspection  
(1) Supplier will maintain accurate records related to fees, security, and compliance for at least 6 years (or as required by law).  
(2) Customer or its designee may audit during normal business hours with reasonable notice, not more than once annually, or more frequently for cause or regulator request.  
(3) Audits will minimize disruption; each party bears its own costs unless material non-compliance (>5% overcharge or material breach) is found.

2.12 Publicity and Branding  
(1) Use of the other party’s name or marks requires prior written approval.  
(2) Case studies and press releases require mutual consent.

2.13 Assignment and Novation  
(1) Neither party may assign without the other’s consent, except to an affiliate or in a merger/sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee assumes obligations and is not a competitor of the non-assigning party without consent.

2.14 Export Controls and Sanctions  
(1) Each party will comply with applicable export, re-export, and sanctions laws (e.g., U.S. EAR, ITAR, OFAC; UK and EU regimes).  
(2) Customer will not export or allow access to Services in violation of such laws.

2.15 Accessibility  
(1) Supplier will align with WCAG 2.1 AA for applicable user-facing components and provide a current VPAT upon request.  
(2) Accessibility defects will be remediated within mutually agreed timelines.

2.16 Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG)  
(1) Supplier prohibits forced, compulsory, or child labor and complies with applicable modern slavery laws.  
(2) Supplier follows a code of conduct addressing anti-bribery (FCPA/UK Bribery Act), conflicts of interest, equal opportunity, and environmental stewardship.  
(3) Sustainability practices, including e-waste management and energy efficiency, will be used where applicable.

2.17 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery  
(1) Supplier maintains tested BCDR plans annually, covering facilities, personnel, systems, and critical suppliers.  
(2) Target metrics: RTO and RPO as set out in the SLA table; evidence available upon request.

2.18 Open Source  
(1) Supplier will disclose Open Source Software (OSS) components in Deliverables and comply with applicable OSS licenses.  
(2) No copyleft obligations will be imposed on Customer IP without express written consent.

2.19 Miscellaneous  
(1) Force Majeure: Neither party liable for delays due to events beyond reasonable control; duties resume promptly after cessation.  
(2) Severability, Waiver, and Entire Agreement: Standard provisions apply; no waiver unless in writing; Agreement is the entire understanding.  
(3) Counterparts and Electronic Signatures: Valid and enforceable.

# Intellectual Property Rights

## 1. Ownership and License
1.1 Pre-existing IP  
(1) Each party retains ownership of its pre-existing materials, tools, methodologies, and know-how.  
1.2 Deliverables  
(1) Unless otherwise stated in the SOW, Customer will own Deliverables specifically developed for Customer under a Customer-funded SOW upon full payment.  
(2) Supplier retains ownership of its underlying tools and reusable components; Supplier grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use such embedded components as necessary to use the Deliverables.  
1.3 Supplier Materials  
(1) For Supplier software provided as a service (SaaS), Customer receives a non-exclusive, non-transferable, term-limited license to access and use the service per the Agreement.  
1.4 Feedback  
(1) Supplier may use suggestions and feedback to improve the Services without obligation, provided no Customer Confidential Information is disclosed.

## 2. Infringement Indemnity
2.1 Supplier will defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe IP rights, and pay damages, costs, and reasonable attorney fees finally awarded or approved in settlement.  
2.2 Remedies  
(1) Supplier may: (a) procure the right to continue use; (b) modify to be non-infringing without material degradation; or (c) replace with equivalent functionality.  
(2) If not feasible, Customer may terminate the affected Services for a refund of prepaid, unused fees and, for perpetual Deliverables, a pro-rata refund over a 36-month straight-line period.  
2.3 Exclusions  
(1) Claims arising from Customer’s modifications not authorized by Supplier, combination with non-Supplier items where the claim would not exist absent such combination, or use not in accordance with documentation.

## 3. Escrow (If Applicable)
3.1 For critical on-premises software Deliverables, Supplier will enter a source code escrow with a reputable agent; release conditions include insolvency, material breach of support obligations, or discontinuance of support.

# Data Protection and Privacy

## 1. Roles and Compliance
1.1 Roles  
(1) For SaaS/managed services, Supplier acts as Processor and Customer as Controller; for certain diagnostics, Supplier may act as independent Controller for limited metadata as necessary for security and compliance.  
1.2 Compliance  
(1) Supplier will comply with GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD, PIPEDA, and other applicable data protection laws.  
(2) A Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), UK Addendum, and Swiss Addendum (as applicable) is incorporated by reference.

## 2. Processing Instructions and Scope
2.1 Supplier will process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Customer and solely for the purposes stated in the Agreement.  
2.2 Supplier will ensure personnel are bound by confidentiality and trained in data protection.

## 3. Technical and Organizational Measures
3.1 Supplier implements appropriate TOMs, including:  
(1) Access control (least privilege, MFA for admin access);  
(2) Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256 or equivalent);  
(3) Network security (segmentation, firewalls, IDS/IPS);  
(4) Vulnerability management (monthly scans, timely patching);  
(5) Secure SDLC, code review, and supply chain security;  
(6) Logging, monitoring, and anomaly detection;  
(7) Backup and recovery aligned with RPO/RTO;  
(8) Annual penetration testing and remediation.

## 4. Subprocessors
4.1 Supplier will obtain Customer’s general authorization for subprocessors and maintain a public/current list.  
4.2 Supplier will flow down data protection obligations and remain fully liable for subprocessors.  
4.3 Customer may object on reasonable privacy/security grounds; parties will work in good faith toward alternatives.

## 5. Data Subject Rights and Cooperation
5.1 Supplier will assist Customer with DSARs, DPIAs, and consultations with regulators, taking into account the nature of processing.  
5.2 Supplier will provide data portability exports in commonly used formats upon request.

## 6. Security Incidents
6.1 Supplier will notify Customer without undue delay and no later than 72 hours after confirmation of a Personal Data breach impacting Customer Data.  
6.2 Notification will include nature of breach, data categories, likely consequences, and measures taken.  
6.3 Supplier will cooperate with investigations, mitigation, and notifications required by law or Customer direction.

## 7. Cross-Border Transfers
7.1 International transfers will be governed by applicable SCCs and transfer impact assessments; supplementary measures will be implemented where required.  
7.2 Data residency options will be provided where available.

## 8. Retention and Deletion
8.1 Supplier will retain Personal Data only as necessary and delete or return all Personal Data upon termination or at Customer’s instruction, subject to legal retention requirements.  
8.2 Backups containing Personal Data will be overwritten per standard cycles.

# Security and Regulatory Compliance

## 1. Security Standards and Certifications
1.1 Supplier aligns with recognized frameworks: ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST CSF.  
1.2 Evidence (certificates, reports under NDA, or summary letters) will be provided upon request.

## 2. Physical and Logical Security
2.1 Data centers certified to ISO 27001/SSAE 18 or equivalent.  
2.2 Logical access via role-based access control, MFA, and periodic access recertification.

## 3. Vulnerability and Patch Management
3.1 Critical vulnerabilities remediated within 14 days; high within 30 days; medium within 90 days, unless compensating controls are in place.

## 4. Secure Development
4.1 Threat modeling, SAST/DAST, dependency scanning, SBOM maintenance, and change control with segregation of duties.

## 5. Incident Management
5.1 Documented IR plan with 24x7 monitoring for production systems; post-incident reports provided within 10 business days for Severity 1–2 incidents.

## 6. Compliance Matrix

| Regulation/Standard | Applicability | Compliance Approach | Evidence/Artifacts | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GDPR/UK GDPR | If Personal Data of EU/UK residents processed | DPA with SCCs/UK Addendum; lawful basis via Customer; TOMs; DPIA support | DPA, TOMs summary, SOC 2/ISO 27001, TIA | Supplier (Processor), Customer (Controller) |
| CCPA/CPRA | If CA resident data processed | Service provider terms; limited use; delete/return on request; opt-out support | CPRA addendum, Data maps | Supplier/Customer |
| HIPAA | If PHI processed | Business Associate Agreement; HIPAA safeguards | BAA, policies, training | Supplier (BA) / Customer (CE) |
| PCI DSS | If cardholder data processed | Outsource to PCI compliant gateway; network segmentation | AOC/SAQ | Supplier/Third-Party |
| ISO 27001 | For ISMS governance | Certified ISMS covering in-scope services | Certificate/SOA | Supplier |
| SOC 2 Type II | Trust principles: Security, Availability, Confidentiality | Independent audits, annual | SOC 2 report (under NDA) | Supplier |
| FedRAMP/StateRAMP | If U.S. public sector cloud | Authorized or aligning baseline; boundary definition | ATO package or roadmap | Supplier |
| WCAG 2.1 AA | For user-facing components | Accessibility-by-design, VPAT | VPAT, test reports | Supplier |
| Export/Sanctions | All cross-border operations | Screening, export classifications, sanctions compliance | Policies, screening logs | Both |

# Service Level Agreements (SLAs)

## 1. Service Availability
1.1 Target Availability (Monthly): 99.9% (SaaS production).  
1.2 Exclusions: Scheduled Maintenance (with 72-hour notice, conducted during off-peak windows), force majeure, Customer-caused outages, and third-party failures beyond Supplier control where commercially reasonable mitigation is in place.

## 2. Incident Classification and Response

| Severity | Example Impact | Initial Response Time | Workaround Target | Resolution Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sev 1 (Critical) | Complete outage; critical security incident | 30 minutes (24x7) | 4 hours | 8 hours |
| Sev 2 (High) | Major functionality degraded; significant business impact | 1 hour (24x7) | 8 hours | 24 hours |
| Sev 3 (Medium) | Partial impact; acceptable workaround | 4 business hours | 2 business days | 5 business days |
| Sev 4 (Low) | Minor defect; cosmetic | 1 business day | N/A | Next planned release |

## 3. Support Coverage and Channels
3.1 Coverage: 24x7 for Sev 1–2; business hours for Sev 3–4 based on Customer primary time zone.  
3.2 Channels: Support portal, email, and phone hotline; ticketing with unique IDs and status tracking.  
3.3 Escalation: Automatic escalation to management if targets are at risk; executive escalation for repeated breaches.

## 4. Maintenance Windows
4.1 Standard weekly maintenance window of up to 2 hours; emergency maintenance for critical patches with as much advance notice as practicable.  
4.2 Zero-downtime deployment practices used where feasible.

## 5. Reporting and Reviews
5.1 Monthly service reports: uptime, incidents, MTTR, security events, capacity, and change metrics.  
5.2 Quarterly service reviews: KPI review, continuous improvement plan, risk register updates.

## 6. Backup, DR, and Continuity

| Control | Target |
|---|---|
| Backup Frequency | Daily incremental; weekly full |
| Backup Retention | 30 days (configurable per SOW) |
| RPO (Data Loss Window) | ≤ 4 hours |
| RTO (Service Restoration) | ≤ 8 hours for critical components |
| DR Testing | At least annually, with results shared upon request |

## 7. Service Credits

| Metric | Threshold | Credit (as % of Monthly Recurring Fee for affected service) |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly Availability | < 99.9% to ≥ 99.5% | 5% |
| Monthly Availability | < 99.5% to ≥ 99.0% | 10% |
| Monthly Availability | < 99.0% | 20% |
| Sev 1 Resolution Target Missed | Each verified miss | 2% per incident (cap 10%) |

7.1 Credits are Customer’s sole monetary remedy for SLA breaches, without prejudice to termination rights for chronic failure.  
7.2 Credits applied to the next invoice; not to exceed 25% of the monthly fee for the affected service.

## 8. Chronic Failure
8.1 “Chronic Failure” means three (3) months in any rolling six (6) month period with either availability below 99.5% or two or more missed Sev 1 resolution targets. Customer may terminate the affected service for cause without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

# Liability and Indemnification

## 1. Mutual Indemnification
1.1 Each party will defend, indemnify, and hold the other harmless from third-party claims to the extent arising from:  
(1) Bodily injury or tangible property damage caused by the indemnifying party’s negligence or willful misconduct;  
(2) Violation of applicable law by the indemnifying party;  
(3) Employee compensation claims where required by law.

## 2. Data and Security Indemnity
2.1 Supplier will indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Supplier’s breach of the DPA or failure to maintain appropriate security measures resulting in a Personal Data breach, to the extent caused by Supplier.

## 3. Limitation of Liability
3.1 EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY’S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY UNDER THE AGREEMENT WILL NOT EXCEED 12 MONTHS OF FEES PAID OR PAYABLE UNDER THE APPLICABLE SOW GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.  
3.2 EXCLUDED CLAIMS: (1) IP infringement indemnity; (2) breach of confidentiality; (3) data protection indemnity; (4) willful misconduct or fraud; (5) amounts owed for fees. For Excluded Claims, liability is capped at 2x the amount in Section 3.1, unless prohibited by law.  
3.3 NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR LOST PROFITS, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY, EXCEPT TO THE EXTENT SUCH LIMITATION IS PROHIBITED BY LAW.  
3.4 NOTHING LIMITS LIABILITY FOR DEATH OR PERSONAL INJURY CAUSED BY NEGLIGENCE, OR OTHER LIABILITY THAT CANNOT BE LIMITED UNDER APPLICABLE LAW.

# Termination and Dispute Resolution

## 1. Termination
1.1 For Convenience: Either party may terminate an SOW or the Agreement, in whole or part, upon 60 days’ prior written notice after the initial term, unless otherwise stated in the SOW.  
1.2 For Cause: Either party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days of written notice (10 days for non-payment).  
1.3 Insolvency: Either party may terminate if the other becomes insolvent, enters liquidation, or similar proceedings.  
1.4 Change in Law: If performance becomes unlawful or materially non-compliant due to a change in law, parties will negotiate adjustments; if unresolved within 30 days, either party may terminate the affected portions without penalty.

## 2. Effect of Termination and Transition
2.1 Supplier will provide transition assistance for up to 90 days at T&M rates (or as specified) to facilitate orderly transition.  
2.2 Customer will pay for Services performed through the effective termination date; prepaid unused fees will be refunded on a pro-rata basis for terminated services.  
2.3 Data Return/Deletion: Supplier will provide a final export of Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format and delete remaining copies per the DPA.

## 3. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
3.1 Escalation: Disputes escalate to senior management for good-faith resolution within 15 business days.  
3.2 Mediation: If unresolved, parties agree to non-binding mediation before litigation/arbitration.  
3.3 Forum and Law: Governed by the laws and courts/arbitration forum specified in the Master Agreement or Customer’s RFP terms, excluding conflict of laws.  
3.4 Injunctive Relief: Either party may seek injunctive relief to prevent misuse of IP or Confidential Information pending resolution.

## 1. Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption
1.1 Parties comply with FCPA, UK Bribery Act, and applicable anti-corruption laws; no facilitation payments; accurate books and records maintained.

## 2. Competition and Trade Compliance
2.1 Compliance with antitrust and competition laws; no anti-competitive conduct.  
2.2 Export controls and sanctions compliance per Section 2.14.

## 3. Sector-Specific Compliance (If Applicable)
3.1 Healthcare: HIPAA/BAA; minimum necessary, audit logging, and safeguards for PHI.  
3.2 Payments: PCI DSS compliance through certified payment processors; no storage of sensitive authentication data unless expressly agreed.  
3.3 Public Sector: FedRAMP/StateRAMP for in-scope cloud services; CJIS where applicable.

## 4. Records Retention

## 5. Equal Opportunity and Supplier Diversity

# Compliance Requirements Summary

## 1. Legal and Regulatory Requirements

# Term-Specific Schedules (To Be Finalized in SOW)

This comprehensive legal and compliance framework is designed to be clear, balanced, and aligned with applicable regulations and industry best practices, while protecting both parties’ interests and ensuring accountable, auditable service delivery.

# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Parties, Purpose, and Definitions
1. Parties. This RFP proposal content is intended to form the legal and compliance framework for the definitive agreement(s) between Customer and Provider (together, the Parties).
2. Purpose. The Parties intend to establish a secure, compliant cybersecurity service encompassing 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) monitoring, Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) implementation, and incident response services aligned to ISO/IEC 27001.
3. Key Definitions.
   1. Confidential Information: Non-public information disclosed by a Party, including security architectures, customer data, pricing, and trade secrets.
   2. Customer Data: All data provided by or on behalf of Customer, including Personal Data.
   3. Personal Data: Information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, as defined by applicable law (e.g., GDPR, CCPA).
   4. Security Incident: A confirmed adverse event impacting the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of services or data.
   5. Breach: A personal data breach as defined by applicable privacy law.
   6. Deliverables: All work products specified in the Statement(s) of Work (SOW), excluding Provider Background IP.
   7. Provider Background IP: Intellectual property owned or controlled by Provider prior to or independent of this engagement.

## 2. Scope of Services
1. 24/7 SOC Monitoring. Continuous monitoring, triage, and escalation of security events.
2. SIEM Implementation. Design, configuration, integration of log sources, detection use-cases, dashboards, and reporting.
3. Incident Response. On-call incident responders for triage, containment, eradication, and recovery in accordance with the SLA.
4. Governance and Reporting. Regular security reporting, metrics reviews, and executive briefings.
5. Compliance Alignment. Operation of services under an ISO/IEC 27001-compliant Information Security Management System (ISMS).

## 3. Governance and Stakeholders
1. Customer Stakeholders. The following roles shall participate in governance, approvals, and escalations:
   1. Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
   2. IT Operations Manager
   3. Compliance Officer
   4. Legal Department
   5. Procurement Team
2. Provider Stakeholders. Provider will designate an Engagement Executive, Security Lead, and Service Delivery Manager.
3. Governance Cadence.
   1. Weekly operational reviews (tickets, incidents, changes).
   2. Monthly KPI/SLA reviews and risk register updates.
   3. Quarterly executive steering committee meetings.
4. RACI and Approvals. A RACI matrix will be maintained within the SOW. Changes to scope, SLAs, or security posture require joint approval by the Customer CISO (or delegate) and Provider Engagement Executive.

# Commercial Terms

## 4. Term and Renewal
1. Initial Term. The initial term shall be [12–36] months from the Effective Date, as defined in the Master Services Agreement (MSA) or SOW.
2. Renewal. The agreement will auto-renew for successive 12-month terms unless either Party provides 60 days’ prior written notice of non-renewal.

## 5. Fees, Invoicing, and Payment
1. Pricing. Fees will be as set forth in the SOW, including any onboarding, recurring, and usage-based components.
2. Payment Terms. Net 30 days after invoice approval by Customer.
3. Milestone-Based Payments. Payments are contingent on the achievement of performance milestones as specified in the SOW; no invoice shall be approved unless the associated milestone is met.
4. Retention. Ten percent (10%) of fees shall be retained until project completion and formal acceptance of all deliverables; retention is released within 15 days following acceptance.
5. Disputed Amounts. Customer may withhold reasonably disputed invoice amounts with written notice; undisputed portions remain payable per the payment terms.
6. Taxes. Fees exclude applicable taxes; each Party is responsible for taxes based on its income. Provider will collect and remit transaction taxes when legally required.

## 6. Expenses
1. Pre-approved, reasonable, and documented travel and out-of-pocket expenses shall be reimbursable at cost per Customer policy, if applicable.

# Service Levels and Performance

## 7. Service Level Agreement (SLA)
1. Measurement Windows. Unless stated otherwise, availability is measured monthly, and response/restore times by incident.
2. Exclusions. Scheduled maintenance with at least 72 hours’ notice (not to exceed 4 hours per maintenance window and 8 hours/month) and force majeure events are excluded from availability calculations.
3. Escalation. SLA breaches escalate to the Service Delivery Manager within 4 hours and to the Engagement Executive and Customer CISO within 1 business day.

### 7.1 SLA Metrics, Targets, and Credits

| Metric | Target | Measurement | Service Credit | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24/7 SOC Monitoring Coverage | Continuous coverage; staffing to meet volume | Staffing schedule, monitoring telemetry | 2% of monthly SOC fee per uncovered hour, cap 10% | SDM immediate; Exec within 1 BD |
| SIEM Platform Availability | ≥ 99.9% monthly uptime | Synthetic checks/log ingestion telemetry | 5% of monthly SIEM fee if <99.9% and ≥99.0%; 10% if <99.0% and ≥98.0%; 15% if <98.0% | SDM 2h; Exec 1 BD |
| P1 Security Incident Response Time | ≤ 1 hour from alert detection to qualified responder engagement | Ticket timestamps, IR pager logs | 2% of monthly fee per miss, cap 15% | Immediate Exec + CISO |
| P2 Security Incident Response Time | ≤ 4 hours | Ticketing | 1% per miss, cap 10% | SDM 4h |
| MTTR (P1 median) | As agreed in IR Plan; target ≤ 12 hours | Incident records | 5% of monthly fee if target missed in 2 consecutive months | Exec + CISO review |
| Onboarding/Implementation Milestone | Per SOW timeline | Project plan baselines | 5% of onboarding fee per full week of delay caused by Provider, cap 15% | PMO + Exec |
| Detection Use-Case Deployment | New high-priority use-cases within 5 BD of approval | Change records | 1% per miss, cap 10% | SDM 1 BD |
| Weekly/Monthly Reporting Delivery | On-time reports | Delivery logs | 1% per missed report, cap 5% | SDM 1 BD |

Notes:
- Credits are applied to the next invoice and are the sole and exclusive remedy for SLA shortfalls, absent willful misconduct or gross negligence.
- Chronic Failure. Customer may terminate for chronic SLA failure if: (a) three consecutive months of SLA credits ≥ 10%, or (b) five P1 response breaches within any rolling 90-day period, after a 30-day cure period.

# Security, Data Protection, and Privacy

## 8. Security Program
1. ISMS. Provider shall maintain an ISO/IEC 27001-compliant ISMS; certification evidence and Statement of Applicability shall be provided upon request.
2. Security Controls. Provider shall implement:
   1. Access Control: MFA for privileged access; least privilege; periodic access reviews (quarterly).
   2. Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for logs and customer data.
   3. Vulnerability Management: Authenticated scanning monthly; critical patches within 7 days; high within 14 days.
   4. Secure Development: SDLC with code review and SAST/DAST for tooling where applicable.
   5. Network Security: Segmentation, IDS/IPS, firewall change control.
   6. Logging & Monitoring: Centralized logging; time sync; tamper-evident storage; log retention per Section 10.5.
   7. Business Continuity/DR: Documented plans; annual testing; defined RTO/RPO in SOW (e.g., RTO ≤ 4 hours, RPO ≤ 1 hour for SIEM).
   8. Personnel: Background checks as permitted by law; security awareness training annually; confidentiality agreements.

## 9. Data Protection (DPA Terms)
1. Roles. Customer is the Controller; Provider is the Processor (or Service Provider under CCPA) when processing Personal Data on Customer’s behalf.
2. Processing Instructions. Provider shall process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Customer and for the purposes set out in the SOW and this Agreement.
3. Subprocessors.
   1. Provider shall maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors.
   2. Customer will receive at least 30 days’ advance notice of new subprocessors and may object on reasonable data protection grounds.
   3. Provider shall impose data protection obligations on subprocessors equivalent to these terms and remains liable for their acts/omissions.
4. International Transfers.
   1. Cross-border transfers shall rely on valid transfer mechanisms (e.g., EU Standard Contractual Clauses, UK IDTA/Addendum).
   2. Provider will conduct transfer impact assessments as required.
5. Data Subject Rights. Provider shall assist Customer in fulfilling requests under applicable law within 10 business days.
6. Confidentiality and Access. Provider shall ensure personnel are bound by confidentiality and access data only as necessary to perform services.
7. Security Incidents and Breaches.
   1. Security Incident Triage: P1 incidents shall engage responders within 1 hour per SLA.
   2. Personal Data Breach Notice: Provider shall notify Customer without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of a Breach, providing details to support regulatory notifications.
8. Return/Deletion. Upon termination or at Customer’s request, Provider shall return Customer Data in a commonly used format and securely delete all Customer Data, except as required by law, certifying deletion upon request.
9. Privacy by Design. Provider will implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to risk and support DPIAs.

## 10. Information Handling and Records
1. Classification. Customer Data will be handled per Customer’s data classification policy if provided; otherwise per Provider’s classification policy aligned to ISO/IEC 27001.
2. Data Minimization. Collect/process only what is necessary to deliver services.
3. Retention. Retain Customer Data only for the period necessary to meet contractual or legal obligations.
4. Backups. Encrypted backups with tested restoration; access restricted.
5. Log Retention. Security logs retained for minimum 365 days online/searchable and up to 7 years archived if required by SOW or regulation.
6. Secure Disposal. Media sanitization per NIST 800-88 or equivalent.

## 11. Audit and Compliance
1. Audit Rights. With 10 business days’ notice (or immediately in the event of a material incident), Customer may audit Provider’s compliance via:
   1. Independent third-party attestations (e.g., ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 reports).
   2. Remote or on-site audits up to annually, during business hours, not unreasonably disruptive.
2. Remediation. Provider will address material audit findings under a mutually agreed remediation plan and timeline.

# Intellectual Property

## 12. Ownership and License
1. Background IP. Each Party retains ownership of its Background IP.
2. Deliverables.
   1. Customer Ownership Model (preferred). Except for Provider Background IP, all Deliverables created specifically for Customer under the SOW are owned by Customer upon payment.
   2. Embedded Background IP. To the extent Deliverables incorporate Provider Background IP, Provider grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use, copy, modify, and create derivative works of such Background IP solely as embedded in or necessary to use the Deliverables.
3. Tooling and Know-How. Provider retains ownership of its generalized know-how, methods, and tools, with no restriction on use, provided no Confidential Information or Customer Data is disclosed.
4. Open Source. Provider will comply with applicable open-source licenses and will not incorporate copyleft code that would impose reciprocal licensing on Deliverables without Customer’s prior written consent.

## 13. IP Indemnity
1. Provider Indemnity. Provider will defend, indemnify, and hold Customer harmless from third-party claims alleging that the services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights, and pay damages, costs, and reasonable attorneys’ fees awarded by a court or agreed in settlement.
2. Remedies. If a claim arises, Provider may: (a) procure rights; (b) replace/modify to be non-infringing with no material degradation of functionality; or (c) if (a) or (b) are not commercially reasonable, terminate the affected services and refund prepaid fees for the unused portion.
3. Exclusions. No indemnity for claims arising from Customer materials, unauthorized modifications, or use not in accordance with documentation.

# Confidentiality

## 14. Confidential Information and Protection
1. Use and Disclosure. Confidential Information may be used solely to perform under this Agreement and disclosed only to personnel with a need to know bound by confidentiality obligations.
2. Safeguards. Each Party will protect the other’s Confidential Information with at least the same care it uses to protect its own confidential information and not less than reasonable care.
3. Compelled Disclosure. Permitted with prompt notice (unless legally prohibited) to allow protective measures.
4. Duration. Confidentiality obligations survive for five (5) years after termination; trade secrets remain protected while they qualify as trade secrets.
5. Injunctive Relief. Breach may cause irreparable harm; injunctive relief is available without posting bond.

# Warranties

## 15. Representations and Warranties
1. Authority. Each Party has the authority to enter into and perform under the Agreement.
2. Conformity and Care. Provider warrants services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel in accordance with the SOW and industry standards.
3. Compliance. Provider warrants it will comply with applicable laws and regulations, including ISO 27001-aligned controls.
4. Non-Infringement. Provider warrants Deliverables do not knowingly infringe third-party IP.
5. Malware. Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure Deliverables are free from known malicious code.
6. Disclaimer. Except as expressly stated, services are provided “as is” and Provider disclaims implied warranties to the maximum extent permitted by law.

# Regulatory and Standards Compliance

## 16. Regulatory Compliance
1. Information Security Standards: ISO/IEC 27001 compliance is mandatory for the services provided; Provider will maintain certification or demonstrably equivalent controls with annual independent assessment.
2. Privacy: Provider will comply with applicable privacy laws, including (as applicable) GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and other regional data protection statutes relevant to the processing performed.
3. Cybersecurity: Compliance with applicable cybersecurity obligations under sectoral laws/regulations (e.g., NIS2, state breach notification laws) where relevant to service delivery.
4. Export Controls and Sanctions: Each Party shall comply with applicable export control and economic sanctions laws; neither Party will use the services in violation thereof.

## 17. Compliance Matrix

| Requirement | Source/Standard | Responsibility | Evidence/Deliverable | Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 27001-aligned ISMS (certification or equivalent) | ISO/IEC 27001 | Provider | Certificate/SoA, audit report | Annual |
| 24/7 SOC monitoring | RFP Requirement | Provider | Staffing rosters, monitoring telemetry | Continuous; monthly attestation |
| SIEM implementation per SOW | RFP Requirement | Provider | Architecture, runbooks, acceptance sign-off | Once per onboarding; updates as needed |
| P1 incident response ≤ 1 hour | RFP SLA | Provider | Ticket/alert timestamps | Continuous; monthly reporting |
| Data Processing Agreement in force | Privacy Laws | Both | Executed DPA | Prior to processing; reviewed annually |
| Subprocessor transparency and notice | GDPR Art. 28 | Provider | Subprocessor list; change notices | Ongoing |
| Breach notice within 24 hours | Privacy Laws | Provider | Incident reports | As needed |
| Log retention ≥ 365 days searchable | Security Best Practice | Provider | Retention policy/config | Annual |
| Vulnerability remediation timelines | Policy/Best Practice | Provider | Patch reports | Monthly |
| Access reviews (privileged) | ISO 27001 A.9 | Provider | Quarterly access review reports | Quarterly |
| DR testing and RTO/RPO | Business Continuity | Provider | Test results; plan updates | Annual |
| Audit rights and evidence | Contractual | Both | SOC 2/ISO reports; audit reports | Annual |
| Employee background checks/training | ISO 27001 A.7 | Provider | HR attestation; training records | Annual |

# Liability and Indemnification

## 18. Indemnification
1. Provider Indemnity. In addition to IP indemnity (Section 13), Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold Customer harmless from third-party claims arising from: (a) Provider’s breach of data protection or confidentiality obligations resulting in a Breach; (b) bodily injury or tangible property damage caused by Provider’s negligence or willful misconduct.
2. Customer Indemnity. Customer shall indemnify Provider for third-party claims arising from Customer’s data, instructions, or materials infringing third-party rights or violating law.

## 19. Limitation of Liability
1. Cap. Except for Exclusions, each Party’s aggregate liability arising out of or related to the Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer to Provider for the 12 months preceding the first event giving rise to liability.
2. Enhanced Cap. For IP infringement indemnity and data protection/confidentiality breaches caused by a Party’s negligence or willful misconduct, the cap shall be two (2) times the amount in Section 19.1.
3. Exclusions. The above caps do not apply to: (a) death or personal injury; (b) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation; (c) willful misconduct; (d) amounts owed under Section 5 (Fees) or service credits.
4. Exclusion of Certain Damages. Neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or loss of profits, revenues, or data, except to the extent such damages are payable to a third party under indemnity obligations.

# Insurance

## 20. Insurance Requirements
1. Provider shall maintain, at its own expense:
   1. Technology Errors & Omissions/Cyber Liability: not less than $5,000,000 aggregate.
   2. Commercial General Liability: $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate.
   3. Workers’ Compensation: statutory limits; Employers Liability $1,000,000.
   4. Professional Liability: $5,000,000 aggregate (may be satisfied via Tech E&O).
2. Certificates of insurance shall be provided upon request; policies shall name Customer as additional insured where customary for liability coverages.

# Subcontracting and Personnel

## 21. Subcontractors
1. No subcontracting of material obligations without Customer’s prior written consent; approved subprocessors are permitted per the DPA.
2. Provider remains fully responsible for subcontractor performance.

## 22. Key Personnel
1. Replacement of key personnel requires prior consultation and a transition plan to avoid material impact on services.

# Change Management and Acceptance

## 23. Change Control
1. All changes will be governed by a written Change Request detailing scope, impacts, schedule, and pricing; no change is effective until executed by both Parties.

## 24. Deliverable Acceptance
1. Acceptance Criteria. Defined in the SOW for each milestone and deliverable.
2. Review Period. Customer has 10 business days to accept or reject with detailed reasons; Provider will promptly cure and resubmit within a mutually agreed timeframe.
3. Deemed Acceptance. If no rejection notice is provided within the review period, deliverables are deemed accepted.

# Termination and Exit

## 25. Termination
1. For Convenience. Either Party may terminate for convenience on 60 days’ prior written notice after the initial term, unless otherwise stated in the SOW.
2. For Cause. Either Party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days of written notice (10 days for non-payment of undisputed amounts).
3. Insolvency. Immediate termination upon insolvency events as defined by applicable law.
4. Chronic SLA Failure. Termination permitted per Section 7 notes.

## 26. Exit, Transition, and Data Return
1. Transition Assistance. For up to 60 days post-termination (or as specified in the SOW), Provider will provide reasonable transition services at then-current rates.
2. Data Return/Deletion. As per Section 9.8; Provider will ensure secure transfer and deletion with certification.
3. License Survival. Rights necessary to use Deliverables (including embedded Background IP licenses) survive termination.

# Dispute Resolution and Governing Law

## 27. Dispute Resolution
1. Good-Faith Negotiation. Escalate to executives (Customer CISO/Legal and Provider Engagement Executive/Legal) for 10 business days.
2. Mediation. If unresolved, proceed to confidential mediation with a mutually agreed mediator within 30 days.
3. Litigation/Arbitration. If still unresolved, the dispute may be brought in the courts of [Jurisdiction] or resolved by binding arbitration under [Rules] seated in [Seat], as specified in the MSA.
4. Injunctive Relief. Either Party may seek injunctive or equitable relief for IP or confidentiality breaches without first mediating.

## 28. Governing Law and Venue
1. The Agreement will be governed by the laws of [Jurisdiction], excluding conflict of law provisions; venue and jurisdiction shall lie exclusively in the courts of [Venue], unless arbitration is selected.

# Additional Legal Provisions

## 29. Force Majeure
1. Neither Party is liable for delays or failures due to events beyond reasonable control (e.g., natural disasters, war, labor disputes, widespread cloud provider outages), provided the affected Party: (a) promptly notifies the other Party; (b) uses diligent efforts to mitigate; and (c) resumes performance promptly.

## 30. Notices
1. Notices must be in writing and delivered by certified mail, courier, or email with confirmation to the addresses designated in the MSA/SOW.

## 31. Assignment
1. Neither Party may assign without the other Party’s consent, except to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee is not a direct competitor and assumes all obligations.

## 32. Order of Precedence
1. In case of conflict: (1) DPA (for data protection matters) and security addenda; (2) MSA; (3) SOW; (4) this RFP Legal Terms; (5) policies referenced by URL.

## 33. Severability; Waiver; Entire Agreement
1. If any provision is held invalid, the remainder remains effective; failures to enforce are not waivers. The definitive signed agreements constitute the entire agreement with respect to their subject matter.

# Alignment With RFP Requirements

## 34. Specific RFP Compliance Commitments
1. 24/7 SOC Monitoring. Committed per Sections 2 and 7, with measurable coverage and staffing metrics.
2. SIEM Implementation. Committed per Section 2; acceptance, timelines, and onboarding credits per Section 7.1.
3. Incident Response Within 1 Hour. Committed per SLA P1 metric, with escalation protocols.
4. ISO 27001 Compliance. Mandatory and affirmed per Section 8 and Compliance Matrix.
5. Payment Terms and Milestones. Net 30 after invoice approval; milestone-based payments; 10% retention until project completion and acceptance, per Section 5.

# Service Appendices (To be finalized in SOW)

## Appendix A: Security Runbooks
1. Incident classification, P1/P2/P3 criteria.
2. Communications plan and RACI.
3. Forensics and evidence handling procedures.
4. Threat hunting and use-case catalog lifecycle.

## Appendix B: Reporting and KPIs
1. Weekly operational summaries (tickets, alerts, changes).
2. Monthly KPI/SLA dashboards; executive summary.
3. Quarterly risk assessment updates and roadmap.

## Appendix C: Onboarding Plan
1. Environment discovery and log source onboarding schedule.
2. SIEM architecture diagrams and capacity plan.
3. Use-case backlog and prioritization.
4. Acceptance criteria and test plans.
