   5) Retention: 10% retention withheld until project completion and acceptance (mandatory).
   6) Taxes: Fees exclude taxes; Client responsible for applicable taxes, excluding Provider’s income taxes.
3. Acceptance and Milestones.
   1) Provider will submit deliverables/milestones for review with acceptance criteria defined in the SOW.
   2) Client shall accept or reject with detailed deficiencies within 10 business days; silent lapse equals deemed acceptance.
   3) Upon rejection, Provider will remediate and resubmit within a mutually agreed timeframe.
4. Changes (Change Control).
   1) Changes to scope, schedule, or costs require a mutually executed Change Order.
   2) Emergency changes for security risk mitigation may be implemented promptly with retrospective approval within 5 business days.
5. Personnel and Background Checks.
   1) Provider personnel accessing Client systems shall undergo background checks permitted by law and complete security awareness training.
   2) Key personnel changes require prior notice and backfill with equivalently qualified staff.
6. Subcontracting.
   1) Subcontractors require Client’s prior written consent.
   2) Provider remains fully responsible and shall flow down data protection, confidentiality, and security obligations to all subcontractors.
7. Tools and Open Source.
   1) Provider may use tools, scripts, and pre-existing materials subject to licensing terms.
   2) Any open-source components will be appropriately licensed and disclosed where embedded in Deliverables.
8. Confidentiality.
   1) Each Party will use Confidential Information solely to perform under this Agreement and protect it using industry-standard safeguards.
   2) Exclusions: Information that is public, independently developed, or rightfully obtained from a third party without restriction.
   3) Duration: Confidentiality obligations survive for five (5) years; trade secrets survive so long as they remain trade secrets.

## 4. Data Protection and Privacy
1. Roles and Instructions.
   1) Client is the controller (or business); Provider is the processor (or service provider) where applicable.
   2) Provider will process Client Data only per Client’s documented instructions in the Agreement and SOWs.
2. Lawful Basis and Compliance.
   1) Provider shall comply with applicable data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, UK DPA), as applicable to the services.
   2) Client shall ensure a lawful basis for processing Client Data and provide required notices to data subjects.
3. Security Measures.
   1) Provider shall implement technical and organizational measures aligned to ISO/IEC 27001, including:
      a) Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256 or equivalent).
      b) Access controls, MFA, least privilege, and role-based access.
      c) Network segregation, vulnerability management, and secure configurations.
      d) Logging, monitoring, and SIEM-driven anomaly detection.
      e) Secure software development and change management practices.
   2) Data Minimization: Limit collection and retention to what is necessary for defined purposes.
4. Data Location and Transfers.
   1) Data residency will comply with Client’s specified region(s); cross-border transfers will use approved transfer mechanisms (e.g., SCCs) where required.
5. Subprocessors.
   1) Provider will maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors and notify Client in advance of changes.
   2) Client may reasonably object to proposed subprocessors; Parties will work in good faith on alternatives.
6. Data Subject Rights and Assistance.
   1) Provider will assist Client with DSRs (access, deletion, correction) and DPIAs, as applicable.
7. Incident Notification.
   1) Provider shall notify Client without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach and in accordance with applicable law (not to exceed 72 hours where law imposes such a timeline).
8. Data Return/Deletion.
   1) Upon termination or upon request, Provider will return Client Data and securely delete all copies, subject to legal retention requirements, and provide deletion certification upon request.

## 5. Information Security Requirements
1. ISO Certification.
   1) Provider shall maintain ISO/IEC 27001 certification (mandatory) or equivalent controls with external attestation (e.g., SOC 2 Type II) if agreed by Client.
2. Secure Access.
   1) Use of named accounts, MFA, and PAM for privileged operations.
   2) No shared administrative credentials; access reviews at least quarterly.
3. Logging and Monitoring.
   1) Centralized log collection into SIEM, with time synchronization and integrity protection.
   2) Retention: Minimum 12 months online or per Client requirement.
4. Vulnerability and Patch Management.
   1) Critical vulnerabilities remediated within 7 days; high within 30 days; medium within 60 days unless otherwise risk-accepted by Client.
5. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery.
   1) Documented BCP/DR plans with annual testing; target RTO/RPO aligned in the SOW.
6. Secure Data Handling.
   1) Use of secure file transfer; prohibition on unapproved removable media.
7. Physical Security.
   1) Data center controls consistent with ISO 27001 Annex A and relevant certifications of hosting providers.

## 6. Regulatory and Standards Compliance
1. Mandatory Standards.
   1) ISO/IEC 27001 compliance is mandatory.
2. Industry Frameworks (as applicable).
   1) SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-61 (IR guidance), CIS Controls.
3. Privacy Laws (as applicable).
   1) GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD, PIPEDA, or other applicable privacy laws based on processing context.
4. Sectoral Requirements (as applicable).
   1) HIPAA, PCI DSS, GLBA or other industry standards if Client’s environment requires them.
5. Export Controls and Sanctions.
   1) Compliance with applicable trade sanctions and export control regulations (e.g., U.S. EAR, OFAC, EU/UK regimes).
6. Ethics and Anti-Corruption.
   1) Compliance with anti-bribery laws (e.g., FCPA, UK Bribery Act) and Provider’s Code of Conduct.

## 7. Service Levels and Reporting (SLA)
1. General.
   1) Service Credits: Applied to the next invoice; total credits in a month capped at 15% of the monthly fee.
   2) Chronic Failure: Three consecutive months of any Priority 1 SLA misses triggers right to initiate a service improvement plan (SIP) and potential termination for chronic failure.
2. SLA Metrics.

| Metric | Definition | Target | Measurement Window | Service Credit | Evidence/Report | Exceptions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOC Monitoring Availability | Availability of 24/7 SOC monitoring capability | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Calendar month | 2% monthly fee per 0.1% below target (max 10%) | Uptime reports; staffing rosters | Force majeure; Client-caused outages |
| SIEM Platform Uptime | Availability of SIEM ingestion, correlation, and dashboards | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Calendar month | 2% monthly fee per 0.1% below target (max 10%) | SIEM health metrics | Planned maintenance with 72h notice |
| Event Ingestion Latency | Time from log generation to SIEM availability | P95 ≤ 5 minutes | Calendar month | 3% monthly fee if missed | SIEM pipeline metrics | Source or network issues beyond Provider control |
| Alert Acknowledgment (P1) | Time to human acknowledgment for Severity 1 | ≤ 15 minutes, 24/7 | Per incident | 5% monthly fee per miss (max 15%) | Ticketing timestamps | Multiple concurrent MCIs; declared DR |
| Incident Response Initiation (P1) | Time to begin containment/IR actions for Severity 1 | ≤ 60 minutes (mandatory) | Per incident | 5% monthly fee per miss (max 15%) | IR logs; bridge recordings | Client approval delay |
| Alert Acknowledgment (P2) | Time to human acknowledgment for Severity 2 | ≤ 30 minutes, 24/7 | Per incident | 2% monthly fee per miss (max 10%) | Ticketing timestamps | As above |
| Containment Target (P1) | Time to contain Severity 1 threat | ≤ 4 hours (target) | Per incident | SIP trigger if 2 misses/month | IR reports | Third-party dependency delays |
| Monthly Reporting | Delivery of KPI/Compliance report | By 5th business day monthly | Monthly | 1% monthly fee if late | Monthly report | Client-caused delays |
| Incident Communications | Update cadence for P1 | Every 30 minutes until containment; hourly until resolution | Per incident | 2% monthly fee per miss | Ticket audit | Client non-responsiveness |

3. Severity Definitions.
   1) Severity 1 (P1): Active data exfiltration, ransomware outbreak, critical system compromise, or regulatory reporting likely.
   2) Severity 2 (P2): High-risk intrusion attempts, lateral movement without confirmed data access, or mission-impacting anomalies.
   3) Severity 3 (P3): Suspicious activity with limited impact.

## 8. Security Incident Management
1. Notification and Engagement.
   1) Provider notifies Client immediately upon confirming P1 with human acknowledgment within 15 minutes and engagement within 60 minutes.
2. Joint Response.
   1) Establish incident bridge; involve Client’s CISO and IT Operations Manager; maintain an incident log.
3. Forensics and Preservation.
   1) Preserve logs, images, and artifacts; coordinate with Client Legal for potential privilege and chain-of-custody.
4. Regulatory Reporting.
   1) Provider supports Client in regulatory notifications; Client retains responsibility for filings unless otherwise agreed.
5. Post-Incident Review.
   1) Deliver Root Cause Analysis (RCA) within 10 business days and implement corrective actions.

## 9. Intellectual Property Rights
1. Ownership.
   1) Client Data remains Client’s sole property.
   2) Client-Owned Deliverables: Deliverables created specifically for Client and paid for in full are owned by Client, excluding Provider Pre-Existing Materials.
   3) Provider Pre-Existing Materials: Tools, methods, templates, and IP developed independently by Provider remain Provider’s property.
2. Licenses.
   1) Provider grants Client a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify, and reproduce Provider Pre-Existing Materials solely as embedded in the Deliverables for Client’s internal business purposes.
   2) Client grants Provider a limited license to use Client materials solely to perform the services.
3. Open Source.
   1) Provider will not include copyleft components that would require disclosure of Client’s confidential materials without Client’s prior written consent.

## 10. Warranties
1. Services Warranty.
   1) Provider will perform services in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards.
2. Compliance Warranty.
   1) Provider will comply with laws and the mandatory standards specified herein, including ISO 27001.
3. Non-Infringement Warranty.
   1) Deliverables and tools used by Provider will not knowingly infringe third-party IP rights.
4. Disclaimer.
   1) Except as expressly stated, Provider disclaims all other warranties to the maximum extent permitted by law.

## 11. Audit, Attestations, and Compliance Monitoring
1. Audit Rights.
   1) Client may audit Provider’s relevant security and privacy controls annually with 30 days’ notice, without undue disruption.
2. Independent Assessments.
   1) Provider will provide current ISO 27001 certificate and (if available) SOC 2 Type II report under NDA.
3. Remediation.
   1) Provider will timely remediate material audit findings; Parties will agree a remediation plan for any critical findings.

## 12. Insurance
1. Minimum Coverage.
   1) Commercial General Liability: $2,000,000 per occurrence.
   2) Professional/Technology E&O: $3,000,000 aggregate.
   3) Cyber/Privacy Liability: $5,000,000 aggregate (including costs for incident response, notification, and regulatory defense).
   4) Workers’ Compensation and Employer’s Liability per statutory requirements.
2. Certificates of insurance to be provided upon request; 30 days’ prior notice of cancellation or material change.

## 13. Indemnification
1. Provider Indemnity.
   1) Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Client from third-party claims arising from: (a) bodily injury or tangible property damage caused by Provider’s negligence or willful misconduct; (b) Provider’s breach of confidentiality or data protection obligations; and (c) infringement by the Deliverables or Provider tools as used by Client per the Agreement.
2. Client Indemnity.
   1) Client shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Provider from third-party claims arising from: (a) Client-provided materials that infringe; (b) Client’s misuse of the services contrary to the Agreement.
3. IP Remedies.
   1) For an infringement claim, Provider may: (a) procure a license; (b) modify/replace to be non-infringing; or (c) if not commercially reasonable, terminate the affected services and refund prepaid fees for the unused period.

## 14. Limitation of Liability
1. Cap.
   1) Except for Exclusions, each Party’s aggregate liability is limited to the fees paid or payable by Client under the applicable SOW in the 12 months preceding the claim.
2. Exclusions.
   1) The cap does not apply to: (a) breach of confidentiality; (b) data protection breach caused by a Party’s failure to implement agreed security measures; (c) IP infringement indemnity; or (d) a Party’s willful misconduct or fraud. For these Exclusions, liability is capped at two (2) times the amount in Section 14.1.1.
3. Indirect Damages.
   1) Neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or lost profits, except to the extent such damages are awarded to a third party in a claim covered by indemnity.

## 15. Termination and Transition
1. For Convenience.
   1) Either Party may terminate for convenience on 60 days’ prior written notice after the initial term.
2. For Cause.
   1) Either Party may terminate for material breach if not cured within 30 days of notice (10 days for nonpayment).
3. Insolvency.
   1) Either Party may terminate upon the other Party’s insolvency events permitted by law.
4. Effect of Termination.
   1) Client will pay for services performed through the effective termination date, subject to acceptance criteria and retention terms.
5. Transition Assistance.
   1) Provider will provide up to [X] weeks of reasonable transition assistance at the then-current rates, including knowledge transfer and handover of documentation and runbooks.

## 16. Dispute Resolution and Governing Law
1. Escalation.
   1) Operational disputes escalate to the SOC Manager and Client’s IT Operations Manager; security disputes to Provider’s security lead and Client’s CISO.
2. Executive Resolution.
   1) If unresolved within 15 business days, escalate to senior executives for good-faith negotiation.
3. Mediation/Arbitration.
   1) If still unresolved, Parties will attempt mediation; failing that, disputes shall be resolved by [binding arbitration in City/State/Country] or [courts of competent jurisdiction in City/State/Country], as specified by Client.
4. Governing Law.
   1) This Agreement is governed by the laws of [Jurisdiction], excluding conflict-of-law rules.

## 17. Governance, Reporting, and Communication
1. Steering and Stakeholders.
   1) Quarterly steering committee including Client’s CISO, Compliance Officer, Procurement, and Provider leadership to review KPIs, risk, and roadmap.
2. Operational Cadence.
   1) Weekly/bi-weekly operations meeting; monthly SLA and compliance reporting delivered to Client stakeholders by the 5th business day.
3. Change and Risk Logs.
   1) Maintain shared risk register and change log; track corrective actions and SIP items.

## 18. Publicity, Assignment, and Other Terms
1. Publicity.
   1) No public announcements or use of Client’s marks without prior written consent.
2. Non-Solicitation.
   1) Neither Party will solicit for employment the other Party’s personnel directly involved in the services during the term and for 6 months thereafter, excluding general solicitations.
3. Assignment.
   1) Neither Party may assign the Agreement without the other’s consent, except to an affiliate or in connection with a merger or sale of substantially all assets, with notice.
4. Force Majeure.
   1) Neither Party is liable for delays due to events beyond reasonable control; the affected Party shall mitigate and communicate promptly.
5. Notices.
   1) Notices shall be in writing and delivered to the addresses set forth in the Agreement.
6. Order of Precedence.
   1) In case of conflict: (1) Change Orders; (2) SOW; (3) this Agreement; (4) Provider policies referenced; (5) proposals and other documents.
7. Entire Agreement; Amendments; Severability.
   1) The Agreement is the entire understanding; amendments must be in writing.
   2) If any provision is unenforceable, the remainder remains in effect.

# Compliance Requirements Matrix

|---|---|---|---|---|

| SIEM implementation | RFP (Source 2) | Design, deploy, and operate SIEM | Architecture docs; runbooks; acceptance sign-off | Provider SIEM Lead |

| Performance-based milestones | Contract (Source 3) | Tie payments to milestone acceptance | SOW acceptance forms | Client Project Manager |
| 10% retention until completion | Contract (Source 3) | Apply 10% holdback until project acceptance | Invoices reflecting retention | Provider Finance |
| Data protection and privacy | Best practice | Process per Client instructions; comply with laws; notify breaches promptly | DPA; TOMs; breach notifications | Provider DPO/Privacy Lead |
| Audit and reporting | Best practice | Annual audit support; monthly KPI/SLA reports | ISO cert; SOC 2 (if available); monthly reports | Provider Compliance Officer |
| Incident communications cadence | Best practice | P1 updates every 30 minutes; hourly until resolution | Ticket and comms logs | Provider IR Lead |

# Service Level Agreement (Detailed Metrics)

| SLA Area | Metric | Target | Measurement | Service Credit | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Availability | SOC Monitoring Availability | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Monitoring platform uptime | See Section 7 | Excludes approved maintenance |
| Platform | SIEM Uptime | ≥ 99.9% monthly | SIEM health checks | See Section 7 | Pre-notified maintenance excluded |
| Performance | Event Ingestion Latency | P95 ≤ 5 minutes | SIEM pipeline metrics | See Section 7 | Network/source issues excluded |
| IR – P1 | Acknowledgment | ≤ 15 minutes | Ticket timestamps | See Section 7 | 24/7 coverage |
| IR – P1 | Response Initiation | ≤ 60 minutes | IR logs | See Section 7 | Mandatory requirement |
| IR – P1 | Containment Target | ≤ 4 hours | RCA | SIP if chronic | Target; not always credit-bearing |
| Reporting | Monthly Reporting | By 5th business day | Delivered report | See Section 7 | Includes compliance/KPIs |
| Communications | P1 Update Cadence | 30 min until containment; hourly to resolution | Ticket/comms log | See Section 7 | Escalation tree engaged |

# Regulatory Compliance Commitments
1. ISO 27001.
   1) Maintain certification; provide certificate and Statement of Applicability annually.
2. NIST Alignment.
   1) Align SOC operations with NIST CSF and NIST SP 800-61 for incident handling.
3. Privacy Regimes.
   1) Execute Data Processing Addendum (DPA) where required; implement SCCs for cross-border transfers as necessary.
4. Sectoral/Client-Specific.
   1) Implement HIPAA/PCI/GLBA controls where Client identifies applicable scope; conduct gap analysis and remediation plan if needed.
5. Records and Retention.
   1) Maintain security and incident records for at least 12 months or as required by law or Client policy.

# Payment, Invoicing, and Milestones
1. Milestone Structure.
   1) Example milestones: (a) SIEM design approved; (b) SIEM deployment completed; (c) Log sources onboarded [X% coverage]; (d) Runbooks approved; (e) Go-live with 24/7 SOC; (f) 60-day stabilization.
2. Payment Triggers.
   1) Payments only upon Client acceptance of each milestone; Net 30 after invoice approval.
3. Retention.
   1) 10% retention withheld from each milestone and released upon final completion and acceptance.
4. Time and Materials (if applicable).
   1) T&M invoices monthly with timesheets; still subject to Net 30 and retention terms if specified in the SOW.

# Technical and Organizational Measures (Summary)
1. Access Security: MFA, RBAC, password standards, quarterly access reviews.
2. Network Security: Segmentation, firewalling, IDS/IPS, secure VPN, zero-trust principles where feasible.
3. Endpoint Security: EDR, hardening baselines, patching SLAs.
4. Data Security: Encryption at rest/in transit, key management, DLP where applicable.
5. Monitoring: Centralized SIEM, UEBA, alerting, use case catalog with continuous tuning.
6. Secure Engineering: Change control, code scanning, supply-chain security, signed integrations.
7. Personnel: Background checks, role-based training, confidentiality agreements.
8. Vendor Risk: Subprocessor due diligence, contractual flow-down, continuous monitoring.

# Termination and Dispute Resolution (Detailed)
1. Termination for Chronic SLA Failures.
   1) If Provider fails P1 incident initiation SLA in 3 of 4 consecutive months, Client may terminate affected services without early termination fees.
2. Service Improvement Plan.
   1) Upon significant SLA breach, Provider will submit a SIP within 10 business days, including root cause, corrective actions, and target dates.
3. Dispute Resolution Path.
   1) Operational team -> Stakeholder leads (CISO/IT Ops Manager) -> Executive review -> Mediation -> Arbitration/Court per Section 16.

# Appendices and Schedules
## Schedule A: Roles and Responsibilities
1. Client Responsibilities.
   1) Provide timely access, approvals, and system information; designate decision-makers (CISO, IT Ops).
   2) Maintain accurate asset inventory and log source coverage requirements.
   3) Coordinate with Legal and Compliance for regulatory obligations and breach notifications.
2. Provider Responsibilities.
   1) Deliver services per scope and SLA; maintain certifications and insurance.
   2) Provide runbooks, playbooks, architecture, and monthly/quarterly reports.
   3) Maintain incident communications cadence and escalation paths.

## Schedule B: Change Control Process
1. Initiation: Change request submitted with scope, risk, impact, and rollback plan.
2. Review: Joint review by Provider lead and Client IT Ops Manager.
3. Approval: Written approval by Client’s authorized approver (Procurement/Legal where required).
4. Implementation: Scheduled execution with notification and monitoring.
5. Post-Implementation: Validation and documentation updates.

## Schedule C: Evidence and Reporting
1. Monthly: SLA/KPI report, SIEM health report, alert volumes, use case efficacy, incident summaries, compliance status (ISO).
2. Quarterly: Executive dashboard, risk register review, roadmap updates, audit/audit-readiness updates.
3. On Demand: ISO 27001 certificate, policies (under NDA), penetration test summaries, and change logs.

This legal response is designed to be clear, balanced, and aligned with the RFP’s mandatory requirements, including ISO 27001 compliance, 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation, and a one-hour incident response initiation for Severity 1 incidents, as well as Net 30 payment terms, milestone-based payments, and a 10% retention until project completion.

# Legal Terms and Compliance

## 1. Definitions
1.1 “Agreement” means the executed Master Services Agreement, Statement(s) of Work (SOW), this Legal Terms and Compliance section, and any incorporated policies, addenda, and annexes.  
1.2 “Customer” means the procuring entity identified in the RFP.  
1.3 “Provider” means the bidder/contractor providing the services and deliverables described herein.  
1.4 “Services” means the cybersecurity services including 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM implementation, and incident response as further defined in the applicable SOW.  
1.5 “Deliverables” means any work product, documentation, configurations, dashboards, detection content, runbooks, and reports produced under this Agreement.  
1.6 “Confidential Information” has the meaning set forth in Section 10.  
1.7 “Personal Data” means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person processed under this Agreement.  
1.8 “Security Incident” means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, or destruction of Customer systems or data while controlled by Provider.  
1.9 “Applicable Law” means all laws, regulations, directives, and standards applicable to the Services, including privacy and security laws and the standards specified in this Agreement.  
1.10 “Business Day” means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in the governing jurisdiction.

## 2. Scope of Services
2.1 Provider will deliver 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) monitoring, SIEM implementation and tuning, and incident response with a one-hour response requirement, in alignment with ISO/IEC 27001.  
2.2 Services include:  
  2.2.1 SIEM architecture, implementation, and integration with designated log sources.  
  2.2.2 Use-case development, correlation rules, dashboards, alerts, and reporting.  
  2.2.3 24/7 monitoring, triage, and escalation per the SLA in Section 11.  
  2.2.4 Incident response and containment activities within the agreed windows.  
  2.2.5 Threat intelligence application, vulnerability and patch posture monitoring (as applicable), and runbook creation.  
  2.2.6 Knowledge transfer and stakeholder training for CISO, IT Operations, Compliance, and other identified teams.  
2.3 Any additional services are subject to change control per Section 6.

## 3. Term; Renewal
3.1 Initial term is [36] months from Effective Date unless otherwise stated in the SOW.  
3.2 Agreement automatically renews for successive 12-month terms unless either party provides 60 days’ prior written notice of non-renewal.

## 4. Fees; Payment; Retention; Taxes
4.1 Fees are defined in the SOW and are milestone-based where applicable.  
4.2 Payment Terms: Net 30 days after invoice approval by Customer (per Source 3).  
4.3 Retention: Customer will retain 10% of each invoice until project completion and final acceptance (per Source 3).  
4.4 Milestones: Payment is contingent on verified performance milestones (per Source 3).  
4.5 Invoices: Submitted monthly in arrears unless otherwise specified; must reference SOW, milestone(s) achieved, and service period.  
4.6 Expenses: Pre-approved, at cost, in accordance with Customer’s travel and expense policy.  
4.7 Taxes: Fees exclude taxes; Customer is responsible for applicable taxes except for Provider’s income, franchise, and employment taxes.  
4.8 No setoff: Except as permitted under this Agreement or Applicable Law, neither party may set off without prior written agreement.

## 5. Acceptance
5.1 Deliverables are subject to written acceptance within 10 Business Days of delivery.  
5.2 If Customer identifies material non-conformities, Provider will remediate within a mutually agreed cure period.  
5.3 Acceptance occurs upon written confirmation or if Customer uses the Deliverable in production for 15 consecutive days without material non-conformity notice.

## 6. Change Control
6.1 Changes to scope, timelines, or costs require a written Change Order signed by authorized representatives.  
6.2 Provider will not proceed with changes until the Change Order is executed.  
6.3 Emergency changes to mitigate critical risks may proceed with expedited written approval from Customer’s CISO (or delegate), followed by a formal Change Order.

## 7. Subcontracting
7.1 Provider may not subcontract material portions of the Services without prior written consent from Customer.  
7.2 Provider remains fully responsible for subcontractors and will flow down all obligations, including confidentiality, security, and data protection requirements.  
7.3 Offshore subcontracting or data access requires explicit prior written consent and appropriate transfer safeguards.

## 8. Audit; Compliance Verification
8.1 Customer or its designated auditor may conduct audits (not more than annually, and for cause at any time) on reasonable notice to verify compliance with this Agreement and security controls.  
8.2 Provider will make available SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001 certificate and SoA, and independent penetration test summaries upon request, subject to confidentiality.  
8.3 Material deficiencies will be remediated pursuant to an agreed corrective action plan.

## 9. Insurance
9.1 Provider will maintain at its expense, from reputable insurers:  
  9.1.1 Commercial General Liability: $2,000,000 per occurrence.  
  9.1.2 Professional Liability/Errors & Omissions (including Cyber/Privacy): $5,000,000 aggregate.  
  9.1.3 Network Security & Privacy Liability: $5,000,000 aggregate.  
  9.1.4 Workers’ Compensation and Employer’s Liability as required by law.  
9.2 Certificates of insurance and endorsements naming Customer as additional insured (CGL and E&O to the extent available) will be provided upon request.

## 10. Confidentiality
10.1 Each party will protect the other’s Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own similar information, and no less than reasonable care.  
10.2 Confidential Information includes security architectures, logs, alerts, incident reports, detection content, pricing, and personal data.  
10.3 Exclusions: information that is or becomes public through no fault, was independently developed, or rightfully received without obligation.  
10.4 Use and Disclosure: solely for performing obligations under this Agreement; disclosures only to those with a need to know under confidentiality obligations.  
10.5 Compelled Disclosure: permitted with prompt notice and cooperation to seek protective orders.  
10.6 Return/Destruction: upon termination, as per Section 16.5.

## 11. Service Level Agreement (SLA)
11.1 Scope: Applies to 24/7 SOC monitoring, SIEM operations, incident response, and related managed security services.  
11.2 Definitions: MTTA (Mean Time to Acknowledge); MTTD (Mean Time to Detect); MTTR (Mean Time to Respond/Recover).  
11.3 Measurement Window: Monthly, in UTC, excluding approved maintenance windows.  
11.4 Service Credits: Calculated as a percentage of the monthly recurring service fees (MRC) for affected Services; capped at 15% MRC per month. Service credits are Customer’s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures, except for chronic failures or Security Incidents caused by Provider negligence or willful misconduct.  
11.5 Chronic Failure: Three or more P1 SLA breaches in any rolling 90-day period constitutes chronic failure, permitting Customer to terminate for cause with 15 days’ notice and receive pro-rata refunds without early termination charges.

### 11.6 SLA Metrics and Targets
| Metric | Target | Measurement | Reporting | Service Credit Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOC Availability | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Uptime monitoring | Monthly | 2% MRC per 0.1% below target (max 10%) |
| SIEM Platform Availability (managed) | ≥ 99.9% monthly | Platform telemetry | Monthly | 2% MRC per 0.1% below target (max 10%) |
| Alert MTTA (P1) | ≤ 15 minutes (24/7) | Ticketing/timestamps | Monthly | 5% MRC if >15 min median or >1 outlier >30 min |
| Alert MTTA (P2) | ≤ 30 minutes | Ticketing/timestamps | Monthly | 2% MRC if >30 min median |
| Incident Response Initiation (P1) | ≤ 1 hour from detection (per Source 2) | IR ticketing | Monthly | 5% MRC per breach |
| Containment (P1) | ≤ 4 hours average to containment | IR logs | Monthly | 3% MRC if average >4h |
| Detection Coverage | ≥ 95% of in-scope log sources onboarded and monitored | Asset/log inventory | Monthly | 2% MRC if <95% |
| Use Case Efficacy | ≥ 90% true-positive rate for validated P1 detections | QA sampling | Quarterly | 2% MRC if <90% |
| False Positive Rate | ≤ 10% of P1 alerts | QA sampling | Monthly | 2% MRC if >10% |
| Patch/Vuln Escalation | P1 vulnerabilities escalated within 24 hours | Ticketing | Monthly | 2% MRC if >24h median |
| Reporting Timeliness | Monthly executive and technical reports within 5 Business Days of month-end | Delivery timestamps | Monthly | 1% MRC per late report |

### 11.7 Incident Severity and Escalation
| Severity | Description | Initial Response | Escalation Path |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 (Critical) | Active compromise, material data exfiltration, ransomware, or critical system impact | Acknowledge ≤15 min; IR ≤1 hour | SOC L3 → IR Lead → Customer CISO/IT Ops within 30 min |
| P2 (High) | Exploitable vulnerability with active attempts, suspicious lateral movement | Acknowledge ≤30 min; IR ≤2 hours | SOC L2 → On-call IR → Customer IT Ops |
| P3 (Medium) | Isolated alerts, low likelihood of impact | Acknowledge ≤1 hour; IR ≤4 hours | SOC L1 → L2 as needed |
| P4 (Low) | Informational/security hygiene | Next business day | SOC L1 → Periodic review |

### 11.8 Maintenance Windows and Exclusions
11.8.1 Scheduled maintenance: Sundays 02:00–04:00 UTC with 5 Business Days’ notice.  
11.8.2 Exclusions: Customer-caused outages, force majeure, or third-party failures outside Provider control unless Provider failed to apply commercially reasonable mitigation.

## 12. Warranties
12.1 Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards.  
12.2 Provider warrants it holds and will maintain ISO/IEC 27001 certification or will perform in conformance with ISO/IEC 27001 controls (per Source 2).  
12.3 Deliverables will materially conform to the specifications in the SOW.  
12.4 Provider will not introduce malicious code and will use up-to-date anti-malware and secure SDLC practices for any tooling provided.  
12.5 Legal Compliance: Provider will comply with Applicable Law and Section 14.  
12.6 No infringement: Provider warrants Deliverables and services do not knowingly infringe third-party rights.  
12.7 Disclaimer: Except as set forth herein, Provider disclaims other warranties to the maximum extent permitted by law.

## 13. Intellectual Property Rights
13.1 Background IP: Each party retains ownership of its pre-existing IP.  
13.2 Deliverables:  
  13.2.1 Customer-Owned Option (default): Provider assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in custom Deliverables first created specifically for Customer under this Agreement, excluding Provider Background IP.  
  13.2.2 License-Back: Provider receives a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Customer-owned Deliverables solely to provide the Services.  
13.3 Provider Background IP: Provider retains ownership; grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Provider Background IP as embedded in or necessary to use the Deliverables.  
13.4 Open-Source Software: Provider will comply with applicable open-source licenses; no copyleft license will be used in a manner that requires disclosure of Customer proprietary code or configurations. Provider will provide an OSS notice and SBOM upon request.  
13.5 Third-Party Materials: Provider will secure necessary licenses and flow down rights to Customer.  
13.6 IP Escrow (if applicable): For critical software operated on-prem, Provider will maintain an escrow arrangement with release triggers for insolvency or material breach.

## 14. Regulatory and Legal Compliance
14.1 Security Standards: ISO/IEC 27001 compliance is mandatory (per Source 2). Provider will align controls with NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53 moderate baseline, and CIS Controls v8 as appropriate.  
14.2 Privacy Laws: Provider will comply with GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and other Applicable privacy laws based on processing locations and data subjects.  
14.3 Data Localization/Transfers: Cross-border transfers will use approved mechanisms (e.g., EU SCCs, UK Addendum) and risk assessments.  
14.4 Industry-Specific: If applicable, Provider will execute a BAA for HIPAA-regulated data and comply with PCI DSS for any cardholder data.  
14.5 Export; Sanctions: Provider will comply with export controls and sanctions (e.g., EAR, OFAC, UK/EU sanctions) and will not use prohibited parties.  
14.6 Anti-Bribery: Provider will comply with the FCPA, UK Bribery Act, and analogous laws; maintain policies, training, and books/records.  
14.7 Modern Slavery; Human Rights: Provider will comply with Modern Slavery Acts and maintain a human rights policy.  
14.8 Accessibility (if applicable to deliverables with UI): Conform substantially to WCAG 2.1 AA.

## 15. Data Protection and Privacy
15.1 Roles: Customer is Controller; Provider is Processor/Service Provider.  
15.2 Data Processing Addendum (DPA): Incorporated by reference and shall prevail in case of conflict related to Personal Data.  
15.3 Processing Instructions: Provider will process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Customer.  
15.4 Security Measures: Provider will implement administrative, technical, and physical safeguards including:  
  15.4.1 Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256 or equivalent).  
  15.4.2 Access controls with MFA, least privilege, and role-based access.  
  15.4.3 Network segmentation, EDR on endpoints, and secure log collection.  
  15.4.4 Vulnerability management and annual independent penetration tests.  
  15.4.5 Security event logging and retention per SOW (e.g., ≥ 365 days searchable, ≥ 1 year cold storage).  
15.5 Subprocessors: Prior notification and right to object for material subprocessors; flow-down obligations and due diligence required.  
15.6 Data Subject Requests: Provider will assist Customer to respond within statutory timelines.  
15.7 Breach Notification: Provider will notify Customer without undue delay and in no event later than 24 hours after confirming a Security Incident affecting Customer data.  
15.8 Data Return/Deletion: Upon termination or upon Customer’s written request, Provider will return and/or securely delete Personal Data within 30 days, subject to legal retention requirements.  
15.9 Records; DPIA Support: Provider will maintain processing records and support Customer’s DPIAs and consultations with authorities.  
15.10 Confidentiality of Personnel: Provider ensures staff bound by confidentiality and trained in data protection and security.

## 16. Termination; Transition; Effects
16.1 Termination for Cause: Either party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days of notice (10 days for payment breaches).  
16.2 Termination for Convenience: Customer may terminate any SOW for convenience with 30 days’ notice; Customer pays for Services performed through the effective termination date.  
16.3 Insolvency: Either party may terminate if the other becomes insolvent, enters bankruptcy, or ceases business.  
16.4 Regulatory Termination: Customer may terminate immediately if required by law or regulator.  
16.5 Transition Assistance: For up to 90 days post-termination, Provider will provide reasonable transition assistance at the then-current rates; no rate increase from pre-termination rates.  
16.6 Data Return/Deletion: As per Section 15.8; Provider will certify deletion upon request.  
16.7 Effect on Fees; Retention: Provider will invoice through termination date; Customer may withhold retained amounts until completion of transition and delivery of all materials.  
16.8 Survival: Sections 4, 8, 9, 10, 12–15, 16.5–16.8, 17, and 18 survive termination.

## 17. Liability and Indemnification
17.1 Indemnification by Provider: Provider will defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its affiliates, and their officers, directors, and employees from third-party claims to the extent arising from:  
  17.1.1 IP infringement by the Services or Deliverables (excluding Customer-provided materials);  
  17.1.2 Provider’s breach of confidentiality or data protection obligations;  
  17.1.3 Provider’s gross negligence or willful misconduct causing a Security Incident;  
  17.1.4 Bodily injury or tangible property damage caused by Provider.  
17.2 Indemnification by Customer: Customer will defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Provider from third-party claims arising from Customer data or Customer-provided materials infringing third-party rights, except to the extent caused by Provider.  
17.3 Infringement Remedies: Provider may (at its expense) procure rights, modify to be non-infringing, or replace with substantially equivalent functionality; if not feasible, Customer may terminate impacted Services with pro-rata refunds.  
17.4 Limitation of Liability: Except for excluded claims below, each party’s aggregate liability is limited to the greater of (a) 12 months of fees paid or payable under the applicable SOW, or (b) $1,000,000.  
17.5 Exclusions from Cap: The foregoing cap does not apply to (a) IP infringement indemnity, (b) breach of confidentiality, (c) data protection breaches caused by a party’s negligence or willful misconduct, (d) bodily injury/death, (e) fraud, or (f) intentional misconduct.  
17.6 Exclusion of Certain Damages: Neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, consequential, special, punitive damages, or lost profits/revenue, except to the extent such damages are awarded to a third party in a claim subject to indemnification.  
17.7 Process: Indemnification conditioned on prompt notice, control of defense by indemnifying party, and reasonable cooperation by indemnified party.

## 18. Dispute Resolution; Governing Law
18.1 Executive Escalation: Disputes will be escalated to the parties’ senior executives (including Customer CISO and Provider executive sponsor) who will meet within 10 Business Days to seek resolution.  
18.2 Mediation: If unresolved after escalation, parties will attempt non-binding mediation within 30 days in [City, State/Country].  
18.3 Forum: If still unresolved, disputes will be resolved in the courts of [Jurisdiction/Venue], and the parties consent to exclusive jurisdiction.  
18.4 Governing Law: Laws of [State/Country] without regard to conflict of laws principles.  
18.5 Injunctive Relief: Either party may seek injunctive or equitable relief for actual or threatened misuse of Confidential Information or IP.  
18.6 Attorney’s Fees: The prevailing party in litigation is entitled to reasonable attorney’s fees and costs, as permitted by law.

## 19. Force Majeure
19.1 Neither party is liable for delays or failures caused by events beyond reasonable control (e.g., natural disasters, war, labor disputes, widespread internet outages), provided the affected party:  
  19.1.1 Notifies the other party promptly;  
  19.1.2 Uses diligent efforts to mitigate and resume performance;  
  19.1.3 Continues partial performance where feasible.

## 20. Governance and Stakeholder Engagement
20.1 Steering Committee: Within 30 days of Effective Date, parties will establish a Steering Committee comprising Customer’s CISO, IT Operations Manager, Compliance Officer, Legal Department representative, and Procurement Team representative (per Source 1), and Provider’s engagement manager and security lead.  
20.2 Cadence: Monthly operational reviews; quarterly executive reviews.  
20.3 Reporting: Monthly executive dashboards, incident metrics, SLA performance, risk register, and compliance status.  
20.4 RACI:  
  20.4.1 CISO: accountable for security strategy, severity definitions, and risk acceptance.  
  20.4.2 IT Operations: responsible for remediation actions, patching, and change coordination.  
  20.4.3 Compliance Officer: oversight of ISO 27001 alignment and audit readiness.  
  20.4.4 Legal: contract compliance, privacy, breach notifications.  
  20.4.5 Procurement: commercial and vendor management oversight.

## 21. Publicity; References
21.1 No party will issue press releases or use the other’s name or marks without prior written consent.  
21.2 Anonymized case studies may be used with Customer’s written approval.

## 22. Notices
22.1 Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, overnight courier, or email with confirmation to the contacts specified in the SOW.  
22.2 Notices are effective upon receipt or, for email, upon confirmation.

## 23. Assignment
23.1 Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party’s prior written consent, except to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee assumes all obligations.

## 24. Order of Precedence
24.1 In case of conflict: (1) DPA and regulatory addenda; (2) SOW; (3) this Legal Terms and Compliance; (4) appended policies; (5) purchase order (for administrative details only). Any conflicting pre-printed PO terms are void.

## 25. Entire Agreement; Severability; Waiver; Counterparts
25.1 This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement and supersedes prior discussions.  
25.2 If any provision is held invalid, the remainder remains in effect; parties will replace invalid provisions with lawful ones closest to original intent.  
25.3 Failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver.  
25.4 This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and electronic signatures are binding.

# Compliance Matrix

| Requirement | Standard/Regulation | Contractual Alignment | Evidence/Artifacts | Responsible Stakeholder |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISO 27001 compliance mandatory (Source 2) | ISO/IEC 27001 | Sections 12.2, 14.1, 8.2 | ISO 27001 Certificate, SoA, Internal Audit Reports | Provider CISO; Customer Compliance Officer |
| 24/7 SOC monitoring (Source 2) | Industry best practice (SOC, NIST CSF) | Sections 2, 11 | SOC runbooks, staffing roster, shift schedules | Provider SOC Lead; Customer CISO |
| SIEM implementation (Source 2) | ISO 27001 A.12/A.13; NIST SP 800-92 | Sections 2.2, 11.6 | Architecture, integration plan, use-case catalog | Provider SIEM Architect; Customer IT Ops |
| 1-hour incident response (Source 2) | ISO 27001 A.16 | SLA 11.6, 11.7 | IR procedures, ticketing logs | Provider IR Lead; Customer CISO |
| Payment terms Net 30 (Source 3) | Commercial | Section 4.2 | Invoices, approvals | Customer Procurement; Finance |
| Milestone-based payments (Source 3) | Commercial | Sections 4.1, 4.3, 5 | Milestone acceptance forms | Project Managers (both) |
| 10% retention (Source 3) | Commercial | Section 4.3 | Payment schedules showing retention | Procurement; Finance |
| Data protection | GDPR/UK GDPR/CCPA | Section 15 (DPA); 14.2–14.3 | DPA, SCCs, ROPA | Customer Legal; Provider DPO |
| Audit rights | ISO 27001 A.18; SOC 2 | Section 8 | SOC 2 Type II, pen test reports | Compliance Officer; Legal |
| Incident notification | GDPR Art. 33 | Section 15.7 | Incident reports, timelines | Provider IR Lead; Legal |
| Anti-bribery | FCPA/UK Bribery Act | Section 14.6 | Policy, training records | Provider Compliance; Customer Legal |
| Export controls | EAR/OFAC/EU/UK | Section 14.5 | Screening logs, policies | Provider Compliance |

# Illustrative Milestones and Acceptance Criteria

## Milestones (example for pricing and retention application)
1. Design Complete: SIEM architecture, data source inventory, and runbooks drafted; acceptance by Customer.  
2. Implementation Phase 1: Core SIEM deployed; top 10 log sources integrated; baseline use-cases active.  
3. Implementation Phase 2: All in-scope log sources integrated; dashboards and reports delivered.  
4. Tuning and Optimization: False positive rate ≤10%; P1 use-case efficacy ≥90%.  
5. Go-Live and Knowledge Transfer: 24/7 SOC operations commence; training completed; documentation delivered.

## Acceptance
1. Written confirmation from Customer per Section 5 for each milestone.  
2. Remediation of any material defects identified during UAT prior to acceptance.

# Data Processing Addendum (Summary)

## Roles and Processing Details
1. Controller: Customer; Processor: Provider.  
2. Subject Matter: Security monitoring, incident response, and SIEM operations.  
3. Duration: Term of the Agreement plus data return/deletion period.  
4. Nature and Purpose: Detection, investigation, and response to security events; compliance reporting.  
5. Categories of Data: Log data, user identifiers, device identifiers, network metadata, limited personal data in logs.  
6. Data Subjects: Customer employees, contractors, users, and, where applicable, customers.

## Processor Obligations
1. Process only on documented instructions.  
2. Implement security measures per Section 15.4.  
3. Assist with data subject requests and DPIAs.  
4. Subprocessor controls and prior notice.  
5. International transfer safeguards (SCCs/UK Addendum).  
6. Breach notification within 24 hours of confirmation.

# Schedule: Security Controls Baseline

## Technical Controls
1. Encryption: TLS 1.2+/AES-256 at rest; HSM/KMS where applicable.  
2. Identity and Access: MFA, RBAC, JIT access, quarterly access reviews.  
3. Logging: Centralized SIEM with ≥365 days retention (searchable) and ≥1 year archive.  
4. Vulnerability Management: Monthly scans; P1 remediation target ≤7 days; P2 ≤30 days (Customer-operated remediation timelines may vary).  
5. Hardening: CIS benchmarks; least functionality.  
6. Backup/Recovery: RPO ≤24 hours; RTO ≤4 hours for critical SIEM components.  
7. Secure Development: Code reviews, SAST/DAST, SBOM, supply-chain controls.

## Administrative/Organizational Controls
1. Policies: Security, privacy, IR, acceptable use, change management.  
2. Training: Annual security and privacy training; role-based for SOC staff.  
3. Vendor Risk: Evaluation and monitoring of subprocessors.  
4. Business Continuity: Tested annually; DR exercises.  
5. Incident Response: Documented plan; table-top exercises semi-annually.

# Optional Service Credit Addendum (Illustrative)

| SLA Breach Category | Service Credit |
|---|---|
| Single P1 response breach in a month | 5% of MRC |
| Two P1 breaches in a month | 10% of MRC |

| Availability shortfall of 0.2% (e.g., 99.7%) | 4% of MRC |
| Reporting or coverage shortfalls | 1–2% of MRC each |

# Discrete Legal Requirements Checklist

## Contract Terms and Conditions
1. Net 30 payment, milestone gating, and 10% retention (Source 3).  
2. Acceptance criteria and cure rights (Section 5).  
3. Change control and governance (Sections 6 and 20).  
4. Subcontractor controls and audit rights (Sections 7–8).  
5. Insurance coverage (Section 9).  
6. Warranties and non-infringement (Section 12).  
7. Order of precedence (Section 24).

## Liability and Indemnities
1. Mutual indemnities; IP and data breach coverage (Section 17.1).  
2. Sensible cap with carve-outs (Sections 17.4–17.5).  
3. Consequential damages exclusion with third-party claim carve (Section 17.6).

## Data Protection and Privacy
1. DPA with SCCs/UK Addendum as needed (Sections 14.2–14.3, 15).  
2. 24-hour breach notification (Section 15.7).  
3. Subprocessor controls (Section 15.5).  
4. Return/deletion and certification (Sections 15.8, 16.6).

## Regulatory Compliance
1. ISO 27001 mandatory (Source 2) and auditability (Sections 8, 12.2, 14.1).  
2. Anti-bribery, export controls, sanctions (Sections 14.5–14.6).  
3. Accessibility when applicable (Section 14.8).

## SLA and Performance
1. 24/7 SOC with defined metrics, credits, and chronic failure remedies (Section 11).  
2. Incident response initiation within 1 hour (Source 2).  
3. Availability targets and escalation paths (Section 11.6–11.7).
